The proof uses equivariant Morita bimodules for the quasisimple blocks that occur in the component reduction. We also prove that a block over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ is nilpotent whenever it is Morita equivalent to the group algebra of a finite $p$-group. For the latter result, we establish a criterion for twisted group algebras using derivations of the basic algebra and group transfer.
Semiclassical Weyl laws and noncommutative geometry on open manifolds with conformally cusp metrics

We establish semiclassical Weyl laws on open Riemannian manifolds with conformally cusp metrics of finite volume. These metrics need not be complete, and even when complete they do not have bounded geometry. Moreover, the potentials are bounded, the discreteness of the spectrum being a consequence of the geometry rather than of a confining potential. Therefore, our results lie beyond the scope of recent semiclassical Weyl laws of Dai--Yan and Braverman. The semiclassical Weyl laws are established for fractional Schrödinger operators associated with Dirac operators, magnetic Laplacians, and Hodge Laplacians, under conditions of Moroianu and Golénia--Moroianu which ensure that these operators have discrete spectra. We also obtain extensions of Connes' integration formula for the same operators. In addition, we deal with a class of conformally cusp metrics of infinite volume, in which case the semiclassical Weyl laws and the integration formulas only involve the values at infinity. The results are obtained by applying the abstract semiclassical Weyl laws and integration formulas for spectral triples established in a previous paper.
Sharp Convergence of Extended Douglas--Rachford Splitting with Variable Relaxation

We establish a sharp convergence theory for extended Douglas--Rachford splitting when the first operator is maximally monotone and the second is a convex subdifferential on a real Hilbert space. The resolvent stepsizes may be chosen independently, and the relaxation parameter may depend on the current and past iterates. For fixed stepsizes $α,β>0$, let $\vartheta=\min\{2,2α/β\}$. Assuming the sum of the operators has a zero, we prove weak convergence under $0<θ_k\le\vartheta$ and $\sum_kθ_k(\vartheta-θ_k)=\infty$. Within these pointwise bounds, the divergence condition is also necessary for a universal convergence guarantee when the relaxation sequence is prescribed in advance. Constant relaxation recovers the exact range $0<θ<\vartheta$, resolving a conjecture of Nilsson, Åkerman, and Giselsson. We also establish a sharp bound on growth of the residual, defined as the difference between the two resolvent outputs. We combine this bound with a new Lyapunov function whose definition is independent of the relaxation parameter to obtain a last-iterate residual rate, including $o(N^{-1/2})$ when the relaxation parameters remain uniformly separated from both endpoints.
On the General Position Number of Cacti
Toshihiko Kimura; Yonghwan Kim; Yoshiaki Katayama

Given a graph G=(V,E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges, a subset of vertices $S \subseteq V$ is called a General Position Set (GPS) if no shortest path on G between any two vertices in S contains another vertex from S.
 The General Position Number (GPN) of a graph G is the maximum size of a GPS in G. The decision version of this problem, determining whether the GPN of a graph G is at least a given integer i, is known as the General Position Problem (GPP). The GPP is known to be NP-complete, making the computation of the GPN for general graphs computationally challenging. Hence, much of the existing research has focused on determining the GPN for special classes of graphs. One such class is that of cactus graphs (i.e., cacti), in which any two simple cycles share at most one vertex and no edge. For cactus graphs, several upper and lower bounds on the GPN have been previously presented.
 In this paper, we determine the exact value of the GPN for cactus graphs. We propose a novel graph decomposition that partitions a cactus graph into two types of subgraphs, called bearded cycles and non-beard trees. For each subgraph, we compute a special GPS, named a subGPS. We prove that the union of all maximum subGPSs constitutes a maximum GPS for the original cactus graph. This result allows us to compute the exact GPN for any cactus graph.
Counting fluctuations in the GOE-GUE crossover

We study bulk eigenvalue counting fluctuations in a Gaussian ensemble interpolating between the Gaussian orthogonal and Gaussian unitary ensembles. Realizing this ensemble as the distribution at a fixed time of Hermitian matrix Ornstein-Uhlenbeck flow started from the GOE, we prove a central limit theorem for the one-sided counting function, centered by the semicircle prediction. Its variance grows logarithmically, with a leading coefficient that interpolates between the GOE and GUE values. Specifically, at times $T_N \asymp N^{-1 + \vartheta}$ with fixed $0 < \vartheta < 1$, we prove that the one-sided bulk count is asymptotically Gaussian with leading variance $(1 - \vartheta/2)π^{-2}\log N$. Although the microscopic bulk correlations have their GUE limit throughout this regime, the leading counting variance retains a contribution from the initial GOE matrix.
Undecidable quantum storage: no algorithm can tell from the noise rate whether a fixed circuit remembers

Below a threshold noise rate, error correction lets larger quantum memories store a qubit for longer, without limit. Can the noise rate alone tell us whether a given noisy circuit does this? We construct fixed local circuits for which no algorithm can, already in one dimension under single-qubit noise. Each circuit is translation-invariant and time-periodic, with depolarizing noise on every wire after every layer, including all classical control. A computable list of disjoint rate intervals is indexed by the inputs $n$ of a universal Turing machine; local noise statistics select the input that the circuit simulates, and halting triggers erasure. If the machine runs forever on $n$, a qubit is stored throughout the $n$-th interval at entanglement fidelity at least $15/16$ for a time that grows without bound with size: linearly on rings, exponentially in six dimensions. The encoding and decoding maps are noiseless and global; they depend on $n$, the system size and, for decoding, the time, but not on the rate. If it halts, the fidelity of every encoding falls below $1/2+η$, for any fixed $η>0$, after a time independent of size and rate. The labels of the intervals with unbounded storage form a $Π^0_1$-complete set, and intervals of both kinds accumulate at zero, so these circuits have no noise threshold. Without rate selection, the ring construction is a translation-invariant, time-periodic memory: from an initialized classical hierarchy it stores a qubit for a time linear in the ring length at every sufficiently small rate, addressing the memory part of a one-dimensional question raised by Dünnweber, Styliaris and Trivedi. These are existence results: registers and interaction ranges are very large and the rates astronomically small.
Feedback Exact Controllability of the Nonlinear Diffusion Equation with Controller in Coefficients
One designs a feedback controller for semilinear parabolic equations with controller in diffusion coefficients which steers the initial data y0 in a given state y1 in a finite time.
Handover Cost Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks using an RL-based Multiple-Column Selection Strategy via Branch-and-Price
Mandar R. Nalavade; Gaurav S. Kasbekar; Koushik Kar

Next-generation wireless networks increasingly rely on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites for broad coverage and low latency, making efficient handover management essential. We formulate satellite handover as a combinatorial optimization problem, assigning each ground user to exactly one capacity-limited, visible satellite while minimizing network handover costs. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based branch-and-price (B&P) framework with learned multiple-column selection (MCS) to accelerate column generation while retaining exact dynamic programming pricing. We also develop two lightweight heuristic policies: handover-aware visibility duration (HAVD) for online decisions and congestion-aware predictive (CAP) for offline planning. Additionally, a local-search repair algorithm adapts precomputed B&P or MCS-B&P solutions to demand perturbations through single-flip and per-user trajectory re-optimization, avoiding complete re-optimization. Simulations using realistic large scale constellations, including Starlink Gen-1, demonstrate that MCS-B&P achieves solution quality comparable to exact B&P with fewer column-generation iterations, fewer branch-and-bound nodes, and reduced computation time. HAVD and CAP offer effective online and offline cost-latency trade-offs, while local-search repair recovers most performance losses due to demand perturbations at a fraction of the computational cost of full re-optimization.
Contact rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants

We study $C^0$-rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants on closed contact manifolds. We prove that Poisson commutation is closed under uniform convergence, establish weak rigidity for pairs without common zeros, and obtain lower semicontinuity under quantitative control of Reeb derivatives. A three-dimensional counterexample shows that unrestricted weak rigidity fails. For partitions of unity, the contact bracket itself controls the Reeb derivatives. Using monotone homogeneous quasi-morphisms and the Cant--Kilgore--Zhang spectral invariant, we derive positive lower bounds for invariants of open covers and configurations of compact subsets. Applications include a quantitative contact big fiber theorem, bounds on Hamiltonian chord durations and Reeb travel times, and deformations of contact one-forms.
Killing Scales for Conformal Killing Tensors of Rank Two and Higher
Simon C. W. Goodwin; A. Rod Gover; Thomas Leistner

We study which metrics in a conformal class admit a Killing tensor with prescribed conformal Killing trace-free part. We call such metrics Killing scales. We also consider whether a given conformal Killing tensor is itself a Killing tensor for some metric in the conformal class, as well as the analogous problem for conformal Killing-Yano forms. Our approach to this problem uses conformal and projective tractors, and the prolongations provided by the BGG splitting operators of the projective and conformal Killing operators. For rank two conformal Killing tensors, we characterise local Killing scales for arbitrary scales on arbitrary conformal manifolds, extending recent results that were restricted to Einstein scales on conformally flat manifolds. The criterion is expressed in terms of the scale tractor and the BGG prolongation of the conformal Killing tensor. We also obtain Killing scale criteria for higher-rank conformal Killing tensors and conformal Killing-Yano forms, under additional hypotheses involving Einstein scales and normal solutions. We describe the tractor geometry of special Einstein products, including Ricci-flat products, and use these constructions to give examples beyond the conformally flat setting.
From Footprints to Service Regions: Modeling and Analysis of Dense LEO Satellite Networks Using an Orbit-Aware Cox Point Process

In dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, several accessible satellites cover the same location. A footprint therefore identifies where communication is feasible but does not determine which satellite serves each user. The service region of a satellite, namely the set of locations it serves, governs satellite load, resource sharing, and user throughput. Using an orbit-aware Cox point process on a common orbital shell, we model each service region as the intersection of a satellite's spherical-cap footprint and its spherical Voronoi cell under nearest-satellite association. We then use Palm calculus to derive exact expressions for the mean area and perimeter and a coverage--load identity. After coverage saturates, mean area and load decrease inversely with population. In contrast, adding satellites along existing orbits leaves a positive limiting mean perimeter. We connect this geometry to an approximate noise-limited user rate. Along the tested densification paths, the increase in user rate comes mainly from the decrease in mean satellite load rather than from the improvement of the serving link. We also compare the model with Walker constellations with Starlink-type parameters, using Cox parameters matched to the local orbit and satellite densities at each latitude. The model reproduces the mean area and perimeter of these constellations over broad latitude ranges, with larger differences near component maximum latitudes. These results show that service-region geometry, and hence satellite load and user rate, depend not only on the total satellite population but also on its allocation across orbital planes.
When do local bounds permit optimal edge-colorings?

Let $G$ be a multigraph with maximum degree $Δ(G)$, maximum multiplicity $μ(G)$, and chromatic index $χ'(G)$. A proper edge-coloring is locally bounded if each edge $e$ in $G$ with endvertices $u$ and $v$ is assigned a color at most $\max\{d_G(u)+μ_G(u),d_G(v)+μ_G(v)\}$, where $d_G(w)$ and $μ_G(w)$ respectively denote the degree of $w$ and the maximum multiplicity of an edge incident with $w$. The well-known Vizing's theorem guarantees a proper edge-coloring with at most $Δ(G)+μ(G)$ colors. Recently, the local version of this theorem was established for simple graphs by Christiansen, resolving a conjecture posed by Bonamy, Delcourt, Lang, and Postle, and extended to multigraphs by Conley, Grebík, and Pikhurko. In this paper, we define the local chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $χ'_{loc}(G)$, as the least positive integer $k$ for which $G$ admits a locally bounded proper edge-coloring with colors in $\{1,2,...,k\}$. Thus $Δ(G)\leχ'(G)\leχ'_{loc}(G)\leΔ(G)+μ(G)$. We give equivalent characterizations and sufficient conditions for the equality $χ'_{loc}(G)=χ'(G)$, identifying when the local bounds in Vizing's theorem can be satisfied using the minimum possible number of colors. In particular, we prove this equality for every regular multigraph, every multigraph $G$ with $Δ(G)\le 4$, and every simple graph in which the vertices of degree at least five induce a subgraph of maximum degree at most two. Moreover, we construct a simple graph $G$ with $χ'(G)=Δ(G)=5$ and $χ'_{loc}(G)=6$, showing that these local bounds can force the use of an additional color even in simple graphs. Consequently, five is the smallest possible maximum degree for which satisfying these local bounds can require more than $χ'(G)$ colors.
Random homomorphisms from affine to spherical reflection groups

The goal of this paper is to understand the set $\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)$ of homomorphisms from an affine reflection group $\widetilde{W}$ to its associated spherical reflection group $W$. We do this in three ways: numerically, by deriving an explicit formula for $|\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)|$; probabilistically, by exploring the question what does a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}\to W$ look like?; and algebraically, by explicitly writing down all possible homomorphisms on the standard generators. For example, we show that as $n\to\infty$ the probability that a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}_n\to W_n$ is surjective tends to $\frac{3}{4}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n}$ or $D_n$, to $\frac{9}{16}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n+1}$, and to $1$ if $W_n$ is of type $A_n.$
Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation

Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages. Onboard computing resources rarely allow the solution of a cold-started, long-duration nonconvex optimal control problem, especially in dynamically challenging regions such as the cislunar to translunar corridor of the Earth-Moon system. This paper develops data augmentation and training techniques that enable a neural network to predict accurate initial costates of the indirect method. A recovery trajectory is then built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm. Training data are produced by the backward generation of optimal examples method, extending prior approaches to the circular restricted three-body problem. A novel anchor trajectory approach is developed to cover the relevant state space, and costate rescaling and a Hamiltonian loss term are used to improve learning. The method is demonstrated on Earth-Moon transfers from a high Earth orbit to halo orbits about L1 and L2. Under navigation errors and thruster outages, a spacecraft reaches the target orbit more often with the proposed method than with nominal-trajectory tracking or fully numerical reoptimization. Onboard computation is reduced by more than an order of magnitude compared with reoptimization.
A ring of symmetric Hermitian modular forms of degree $2$ with integral Fourier coefficients II

We exhibit 24 homogeneous generators for the graded \(\Z\)-algebra of symmetric Hermitian modular forms of degree 2 over \(\Q(i)\) with integral Fourier coefficients, where the weight \(k\) is even and the character is \(\det^{k/2}\). We prove that 24 is the minimum number of algebra generators. For the subalgebra in weights divisible by 4, Kurihara reduced the generating set given in our earlier work to 11 forms. We show that 13 further forms generate the direct sum of the components in weights congruent to 2 modulo 4 as a module over this subalgebra. For \(p=2\) and \(p=3\), we show that the ring of Fourier expansions modulo \(p\) is a polynomial ring over \(\F_p\) generated by the reductions of 4 forms of weights \(8,12,12,16\). We also record the diagonal Sturm bound \(\lfloor k/8\rfloor\) modulo every prime \(p\) and verify its sharpness in every even weight \(k\ne2\).
FAS-Assisted Self-Interference Mitigation for In-Band Full-Duplex Communications
Hanjiang Hong; Kai-Kit Wong; Jian Sang; Yiyan Wu; Hyundong Shin

In-band full-duplex (IBFD) communication relies on effective self-interference cancellation (SIC) to overcome the strong loopback self-interference (SI). While fluid antenna system (FAS)-assisted SIC offers superior SI suppression by dynamically selecting the FAS port to minimize the residual SI power, it incurs high pilot overhead to acquire channel state information (CSI) for both forward and loopback channels. This raises the question of whether forward channel CSI is necessary for effective SI mitigation. To address this challenge, we propose a pilot-efficient FAS-assisted SI mitigation (FAS-SIM) approach that selects the FAS port solely based on the loopback SI channel. Theoretical performance analysis of the forward signal is provided. Numerical results then reveal that FAS-SIM achieves SI suppression and a forward-link rate comparable to the conventional method, while reducing port-selection training overhead by 50%, offering a low-overhead solution for IBFD communications.
Interface invariants of rhombohedral graphene with layer-dependent potentials and couplings

Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.
Construction of Universal Safe Stabilizing Formulas with Weighted Centroid Methodology
Pio Ong; Max H. Cohen; Aaron D. Ames; Jorge Cortes

Control Lyapunov and control barrier functions ensure stability and safety, respectively, by imposing state-dependent affine constraints on the control input. Controller design can therefore be viewed as the problem of selecting an admissible input from the set defined by these constraints. This paper adopts this perspective and develops a weighted-centroid methodology for constructing explicit feedback formulas that are provably smooth. The selection method relies on the fact that weighted centroids of a convex set lie within the set. We establish conditions on the weight functions that guarantee smoothness and continuity for several classes of constraints, including single constraints, mirrored constraints, linearly independent multiple constraints, and two-constraint Gaussian constructions. The framework recovers Sontag's universal formula and generates other new explicit formulas. When specialized to control-theoretic settings, the resulting formulas yield smooth safety filters, stabilizing controllers, and safe-stabilizing controllers. Simulation and hardware experiments on a small quadrotor illustrate the practical benefits of the proposed construction.
On rescuing diverging algorithms: crossing infinity in continuous Newton methods via a self-similarity detection framework
Gianluca Fabiani; Ralf Hannemann-Tamás; Alexander Mitsos; Jonathan D. Hauenstein; Constantinos Siettos; Panayotis G. Kevrekidis; Ioannis G. Kevrekidis

We address the solution of systems of nonlinear algebraic equations via continuous Newton methods; these methods reformulate the discrete Newton update as an initial value problem for a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) whose stationary points correspond to the desired roots. A fundamental challenge arises when the Jacobian of these ODEs becomes singular along the solution trajectory, inducing blow-up in the vector field --or in the state itself-- and causing the numerical integration to break down before reaching the desired root. To overcome this difficulty, we propose a directional self-similar blow-up detection and crossing procedure, wrapped around an adaptive step-size ODE solver with event detection. The method assumes local self-similar behavior near the blow-up; the self-similarity exponent, blow-up time, and amplitude are estimated on the fly from a short sequence of threshold crossings via linear regression, requiring no prior knowledge of the singularity location, its order, or the blow-up regime---in contrast to approaches that rely on explicit analytical continuation or problem-specific coordinate transformations. The estimated exponent distinguishes two qualitatively different scenarios at finite time: one in which only the vector field diverges while the state remains finite, admitting an explicit integral correction, and one in which the state itself blows-up. In addition, infinite-time divergence of the state (the so-called "grow-up" regime) is handled through a suitable time reparameterization. In higher dimensions, we track the norm of the vector field along its instantaneous direction; near a simple singularity, the flow asymptotically aligns with a single dominant direction (see text), reducing detection and estimation to a scalar problem regardless of ambient space dimension.
The Role of Mathematicians in Mathematics
Some reflections on the role of mathematicians in an age of proofs found and verified by machines.
Weighted Carleson embedding on product of trees in general dimension

We prove the equivalence of the Carleson embedding on $n$-trees (arbitrary Cartesian product of trees) and the box condition, for arbitrary nonnegative measures and generalized product weights. For product weights, we obtain the sharp coefficient $4^n$. This extends the bi-tree and tri-tree embedding theorems of \cite{AMPVZ} and \cite{MPVZ} to every dimension. We also give two applications of the Carleson embedding: we characterize Carleson measures for the classical Dirichlet space on the polydisc $\mathbb D^n$ and deduce criteria for bounded composition operators from this space into weighted Bergman spaces, generalizing the results from \cite{MPVZ} and \cite{Beslikas2025}. Finally, we define a generalized logarithmic Dirichlet space and characterize its Carleson measures.
The dimension of optimal plans in multi-marginal optimal transport

For general cost functions, we determine the maximal dimension on which solutions to the multi-marginal optimal transport problem with absolutely continuous marginals are concentrated. The dimension is obtained via a novel characteristic integer associated with the Hessian of the cost function. Applications are given to important examples of multi-marginal problems like Wasserstein barycenters, Wasserstein cubic splines and Brenier's generalized Euler equations.
Note on the extendability problem for invariant quasimorphisms for mapping class groups
Morimichi Kawasaki; Mitsuaki Kimura; Shuhei Maruyama; Takahiro Matsushita; Masato Mimura

In this note, we study the extendability problem of invariant quasimorphisms for short exact sequences related to mapping class groups of surfaces, possibly with one boundary component or one marked point. Using a recent result of Blatz, we prove that if the genus is at least two, then every homogeneous quasimorphism on the Torelli group that is invariant by the conjugation action by the mapping class group is uniquely extendable to the whole mapping class group. Contrastingly, for the surface with one marked point whose genus is at least three, we show the existence of a homogeneous Torelli-group-invariant quasimorphism on the Johnson kernel that is not extendable.
Stability of a Paraboloidal Steady Solution for the 2D Surface Growth Model

In this paper we consider the stability problem of 2D surface growth model. To be specific, we prove that the small perturbation of the paraboloidal steady solution decays to zero in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The decay occurs both for the perturbation and its gradient, whose decay rates are $O(t^{-1/2})$ and $O(t^{-1}\log t)$, respectively. The proof is based on the linearization of the perturbation equation and the bootstrap argument to close the statement in nonlinear equation.
 Sufficient conditions for stability require the initial data and its gradient of the perturbation to be small in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and Wiener algebra $\mathcal{A}$. It is notable that the smallness in second derivative is not necessary, which is physically reasonable because large second derivative would lead to high surface energy and it is expected to be relaxed in short time. We also prove existence and uniqueness of mild solution for perturbation equation under those conditions.
Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli with multilinear weights

We study the average distribution of primes up to $x$ in arithmetic progressions to moduli $q$ larger than $\sqrt{x}$, where $q = q_1 \cdots q_n$ ($n \geqslant 2$) with conveniently sized divisors $q_1, \ldots, q_n$ and the average is weighted by an arbitrary divisor-bounded multilinear weight. Specifically, we show that the primes up to $x$ are equidistributed in the residue class $a \pmod{q_1 q_2}$ on average over moduli $q_1 q_2$ as large as $x^{8/15 - \varepsilon}$ when the average is weighted by a bilinear weight and the sizes of $q_1$ and $q_2$ lie in an explicit region, improving the exponent $9/17$ for bilinear weights obtained recently by Li. The new ingredient here is an estimate for the Type-II convolution sums with both factors have size about $x^{1/2}$. With this estimate, the level of distribution $8/15$ in the bilinear case is no longer limited by the Type-II sums but by the Type-I$_3$ sums, or the current range in the ternary divisor problem. We also get further improvements for $n \geqslant 3$ using a simple form of Harman's sieve together with various arithmetic information, including the Type-II estimate mentioned above. We group the divisors $q_1, \ldots, q_n$ in different ways in order to use arithmetic information more efficiently. Specifically, we reach $x^{145/266 - \varepsilon}$ for trilinear weights, $x^{457/814 - \varepsilon}$ for quadrilinear weights and $x^{3614/6353 - \varepsilon}$ for quintilinear weights. As the number of divisors increases, the exponent approaches $4/7$, the long-standing result with well-factorable weights proved by Bombieri, Friedlander and Iwaniec.
Moore spaces, polyhedral products, and positive scalar curvature

Gromov conjectured that the macroscopic dimension of the universal cover of a closed $n$-manifold of positive scalar curvature is at most $n-2$. Gromov's conjecture holds for a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 5$, provided that its fundamental group has property $(*)_m$, i.e., its classifying space is stably homotopy equivalent to a wedge of Moore spaces. We prove property $(*)_m$ for a large class of groups, including for instance the fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups with low-dimensional nerves, pure braid groups, and many graph products thereof. As an additional application of independent interest, we show that there are finite-index subgroups of right-angled Artin groups that do not have property $(*)_m$ and can have arbitrary torsion in their (co)homology in any degree.
Plane Curves Whose Curvature Is a Function of the Distance to the Tangent Line: Relations Between Karpenkov's Areal and Angular Densities

For a plane curve and a point $O$, O. Karpenkov introduced the areal density $A$ and the angular density $B$ as smooth counterparts of the alternating entries of an LLS sequence. Here $A$ is the signed distance from $O$ to the tangent line, and, with the order of the chords in the signed definition fixed here, $A^2B=κ$, where $κ$ is the signed curvature. A relation between the two densities therefore prescribes the curvature as a function of the distance to the tangent line. Karpenkov asked which curves have $AB$, or $B$ alone, constant. The equation $AB=C$ gives the shrinking, stationary and expanding profiles of planar curve shortening. For constant nonzero $B$, choose the orientation so that $B>0$. Curves with positive support have periodic support or are centred circles. The noncircular closed curves are classified by their turning fractions in $(1/2,1/\sqrt3)$; the centred circle is the only embedded closed solution. Negative support gives smooth open graphs whose two ends approach rays from the origin. On positive support the polar reciprocal is a constant-force orbit, and the original curve is a rotated and scaled velocity curve of that orbit. For $A^3B=C$ we determine which ends extend to infinity, reach a cusp, or spiral into the origin. We describe regularity and the range of turning fractions for the positive-support family $A^pB=C$. Finally, for a general relation $B=Φ(A)$ the polar reciprocal is an orbit of the central force $L^2/Φ(1/r)$; we describe the ends of all arcs with $AB<0$ and show that a closed curve with turning fraction $m/n$ has exactly $n(m-1)$ double points. We also describe the curves whose areal or angular density is a linear function of the arclength.
Strong holonomicity of functions on curves

Let $X$ be a smooth affine irreducible curve over $\mathbb C$, and let ${\mathcal D} = {\mathcal D} (X)$ be the ring of global differential operators on $X$. To every nonzero operator $L \in {\mathcal D} $ we attach a non-negative integer $n(L)$, the holonomicity index of $L$, which is defined in an elementary way, by counting solutions of $L$ in the truncated local rings at the singular points of $L$. Our main theorem shows that $n(L)$ coincides with the Calogero--Moser index of the Weyl closure ${\rm cl}(L) = {\mathcal D}(K) \cap {\mathcal D} $ of $L$, i.e. with the integer $n$ labelling the Calogero--Moser space $ {\mathcal C}_n(X,\mathcal{I})$ that contains the isomorphism class of the left ideal ${\rm cl}(L)$ under the classification of ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ given in [Berest--Chalykh, 2012]. The proof is based on a dual version of the Cannings--Holland correspondence, which describes left ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ in terms of finite-dimensional spaces of algebraic distributions on $X$, and an explicit formula for the Calogero--Moser index given in terms of these distributions. We apply these results to annihilators of locally holomorphic functions on $X$: we call a holonomic function $f$ strongly holonomic if the Calogero--Moser index of ${\rm Ann}_{\mathcal D}(f)$ is positive, and we compute this index in a number of interesting cases.
Sub-Gaussian HDLSS Principal Component Analysis: High-Probability Theory and Numerical Evidence for NRM, CDM, and Block Noise Reduction

We study principal component analysis when the dimension d is much larger than the sample size n under an independent-factor sub-Gaussian model. The dual sample covariance is decomposed into a finite-rank score matrix, an isotropic bulk shift, and a high-probability remainder governed by the bulk trace τ_0, Frobenius scale q_0, and largest noise eigenvalue b_0 = ||Λ_0||_{op}. This decomposition separates fixed-score HDLSS limits from joint limits in which n also grows. It shows that sequential noise reduction generally targets a score oracle containing a later-spike subtraction, while an oracle block correction avoids that subtraction when the signal rank is known. A parallel cross-data-matrix bound explains the benefit and cost of sample splitting. Reproducible Gaussian-factor simulations with 1,000 replications per configuration confirm the score-oracle approximation, the multi-spike subtraction, the separation between eigenvalue and eigenvector scales, and the population transition when n grows.
Note on OpenAI's proof of the base of Lagrangian fibrations
OpenAI proved that every Lagrangian fibration of a compact hyper-Kähler manifold has a base $\mathbb P^n$. This expository note summarizes the last section of their paper.
A bound for Stieltjes constants of the Riemann zeta function

The coefficients appearing in the Laurent expansion of the Riemann zeta function are known as the Stieltjes constants and are denoted by $γ_n$. Several authors, including Berndt, Matsuoka, Williams and Zhang, and Saad Eddin, have investigated upper bounds for $|γ_n|$, with the best known result due to Pauli and Saidak \cite{MR4671618}. In 2003, based on numerical evidence, Kreminski \cite{MR1972742} conjectured that Matsuoka's bound \cite{MR827790} could be considerably improved. Motivated by this conjecture, we employ the saddle-point method to derive an asymptotic formula for the Stieltjes constants, with the saddle point expressed explicitly in terms of the Lambert $W$-function. The resulting formula yields an asymptotic upper bound of the correct order of magnitude. Moreover, the resulting bound is consistent with the conjecture of Farr, Pauli, and Saidak \cite{MR4280128}.
On the performance of the randomized Euler scheme for nonlinear ODEs under inexact information
Tomasz Bochacik; Bartosz Fober; Paweł Przybyłowicz

We analyze the randomized explicit Euler scheme for nonlinear ordinary differential equations under a local one-sided Lipschitz condition, local Hölder regularity in the space variable, and Hölder regularity in the time variable. We allow for noisy evaluations of the right-hand side. For the resulting approximation, we derive an error bound in which the contribution associated with the Hölder regularity in the time variable exhibits the characteristic 1/2-order gain of randomized methods. While existing results cover deterministic schemes under the one-sided Lipschitz condition and randomized schemes under the classical Lipschitz condition, our results combine randomized approximation and one-sided Lipschitz regularity.
Linear and non-linear integro-differential equations with variable coefficients and Sonin kernels

We study linear and non-linear integro-differential equations, with Sonin and absolutely continuous kernels, and with variable coefficients which are either integrable or continuous functions. In the linear case, for all cases, the unique solution is given explicitly by a convergent infinite series involving compositions of convolutions of the kernels and the variable coefficients. Many examples are provided. For the non-linear case, the existence and uniqueness are established under a suitable condition in the non-linear term. The analytic solution is given by the limit of the iterative sequence found from the method of successive approximations. The exact analytical expressions for several problems are found by computing the iterative sequences that approximate the solution.

Path integrals in quantum field theory are commonly approached through finite-dimensional approximations, but existence and regulator independence of the infinite-dimensional limit require separate analysis. We introduce a scheme in which spacetime remains continuous and the field is expanded in a discrete complete family of localized functions, called a functional lattice. Truncation to finite-dimensional functional subspaces yields ordinary finite-dimensional integrals while leaving the continuum differential operator unchanged. For the massive free Euclidean scalar field, we prove convergence of the finite-dimensional covariance operators and normalized generating functionals by a Galerkin argument. The limit is independent of the compatible functional lattice: any sequence of finite-dimensional subspaces dense in the quadratic-form domain converges to the same continuum covariance and generating functional. A direct Minkowski construction is obtained at fixed Feynman regulator $iε$, followed by the distributional limit $ε\downarrow0$. For interacting theories, each truncation gives an ordinary non-Gaussian integral. At fixed perturbative order, convergence follows when the finite-resolution graph integrands converge pointwise and admit an integrable majorant independent of the functional resolution. Numerical results for one-dimensional $φ^4$ theory approach the known first- and second-order mass-gap coefficients, while four-dimensional calculations exhibit the expected mass divergence and logarithmic wave-function renormalization. Thus functional lattices provide a continuum-space approach to path integrals with mathematically controlled limits in the cases considered here.
Mirror Descent at the Edge of Stability

In many deep learning settings, gradient descent has been shown to operate at the edge of stability -- a regime where the largest eigenvalue of the loss Hessian hovers around $2/η$. We study this phenomenon in mirror descent, a generalization of gradient descent. As mirror descent is non-Euclidean, existing explanations of the edge of stability phase do not extend to this setting. We generalize the existing notion of sharpness to introduce mirror sharpness, which measures the curvature of the loss with respect to the mirror potential. Empirically, we observe that the mirror sharpness hovers slightly above the $2/η$ threshold. Furthermore, we derive a dual central flow ODE for mirror descent that models iterates in continuous time at the onset of edge of stability. Our ODE provides insights into the difficulties of extending existing arguments for why sharpness stabilizes at $2/η$ from gradient descent to mirror descent in full generality.
An Exact Penalty Method for Large-Scale Equality-Constrained Nonlinear Optimization
Maxence Gollier; Youssef Diouane; Dominique Orban

We present an exact penalty method for equality-constrained nonlinear optimization. Our approach transforms the smooth, constrained problem into a sequence of nonsmooth, unconstrained problems by penalizing the constraint violation by its Euclidean norm. An outer loop updates the penalty parameter and the subproblem tolerances, while an inner loop solves each penalized subproblem with a quadratic regularization method. The method also includes a local infeasibility detection mechanism, an extrapolation strategy for warm-starting subproblems, and nonmonotone acceptance rules. We establish global convergence to first-order stationary points under a bounded penalty parameter assumption, with a worst-case complexity of \(\mathcal{O}(|\log ε|\,ε^{-2})\) inner iterations. We implement the method in Penelopt, an open-source Julia solver for constrained nonlinear optimization. On \(224\) problems from the CUTEst collection, Penelopt is competitive with IPOPT and more robust than the recent solvers MadNLP and Uno. These results establish exact penalty methods as a practical alternative to conventional methods for solving equality-constrained nonlinear optimization problems. To the best of our knowledge, Penelopt is the first practical implementation of an exact penalty method for large-scale constrained nonlinear optimization.
Automorphism groups of Severi--Brauer varieties of odd prime degree over $\mathbb{Q}$
Raisa V. Serova; Anastasia V. Vikulova
We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroup of automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer variety of odd prime degree $p$ over the field of rational numbers is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}.$
A Calculus Gradient: Child Poverty, Mathematics Preparation, and First-Year College Performance at a Hispanic-Serving University

The San Antonio metropolitan area has one of the highest poverty rates among large U.S. metropolitan areas. Within Bexar County, where the city is located, child poverty varies widely across school districts. We link entrants of the city's public research university, a broad-access Hispanic-Serving Institution, to their sending schools and districts, and examine their preparation scores and first-year outcomes. Across the nation's school districts, enrollment in widely taken core courses (Algebra II, Geometry, Biology) shows little relation to child poverty, while enrollment in Calculus and Advanced Placement mathematics and science is far lower where child poverty is higher, nationally and within Bexar County. Among linked entrants, mathematics preparation differs with the school and district. Entrants with stronger mathematics preparation earn higher first-year grades in nearly every subject. Most entrants who do not return after the first year had unsuccessful courses, and mathematics is the largest single source of those outcomes. Among students who change major, mathematics is one of the subjects with grades furthest below their own averages. Within the same course and term, larger mathematics sections go with more unsuccessful outcomes for entrants with lower mathematics preparation, which identifies a hypothesis for testing smaller sections. Recorded between Fall 2014 and Fall 2019, these outcomes offer a reference point for change after the pandemic, test-optional admissions, and generative artificial intelligence. The analysis is reproducible; adapting it elsewhere requires local definitions and linkage validation. All results are associations among the students of one institution; establishing causes would require a designed study.
Parallel batch scheduling for optimizing hospital sterilization operations: arc-flow formulations, column generation and Lagrangian heuristics for flowtime minimization

In a recent work by Schlembach et al., the problem of optimally managing sterilization operations in hospitals has been modeled as a machine scheduling problem with parallel batch processing and minimum flowtime objective, and heuristically solved by column generation. We draw upon this approach, developing arc-flow formulations and related column-generation procedures, using an exact dynamic programming algorithm to solve the pricing problems. We further derive Lagrangian relaxations based on minimum cost flows and shortest paths, with subgradient optimization and the volume algorithm guiding batch generation. A makespan bound for schedules minimizing total flow time provides a finite horizon when no operational limit is known. Computational experiments on literature benchmarks and more challenging generated instances demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches. The arc-flow model solves all literature benchmark instances to proven optimality within seconds, while the Lagrangian heuristics deliver high-quality schedules with substantially reduced computational effort.

At $β_*^2=8π$ we construct the two-dimensional sine--Gordon vacuum from a noncompact real lattice field with nearest-neighbor kinetic energy, positive cosine activity and zero Dirichlet data. Its mass $M$ is the lower edge of the energy spectrum above the vacuum. In units of the length $a_{\rm exit}$ at which the flow leaves weak coupling it obeys $0<c_-\le M a_{\rm exit}\le c_+<\infty$ on compact positive endpoint intervals, with uniform constants. A prescribed response to a smooth background in a fixed square determines the nonlinear asymptotically free bare parameters at each sufficiently fine cutoff. In the local relativistic continuum theory the vacuum is unique, physical dilation realizes every positive mass, and literal derivatives generate the reflected Hilbert space even for finite composite and contact families. Variance and exponential moments of a derivative smear rule out a Gaussian law. A connected correlation of some finite even order above two is nonzero on separated supports. The construction gives universality for the specified finite nonnegative higher harmonics, the field equation, topological current and geometric stress tensor with their Ward, trace and contact identities, and a normalized source-transfer theorem with explicit finite-scale hypotheses.
Convergence analysis of resonant frequency approximation in periodic Helmholtz problems
Jiho Hong; Woojoo Lee; Mikyoung Lim

We investigate resonant frequencies of the Helmholtz equation in periodic structures under quasi-periodic conditions, using approximations of the associated quasi-periodic Green function, which is represented by a lattice sum. By formulating the periodic Helmholtz problem using layer potential operators whose kernel is given by the quasi-periodic Green function, resonant frequencies correspond to characteristic values of an associated operator-valued function. Based on two approximation methods for the quasi-periodic Green function, the Ewald method and the shifted Green function method, we propose the corresponding approximation schemes for resonant frequencies. Furthermore, we establish convergence rates for the resulting approximations using Gohberg--Sigal theory, where the Ewald method yields exponential convergence, while the shifted Green function method yields algebraic convergence. Numerical computations are presented to validate and compare the proposed approximation schemes.
Wet-part doubling for log-concave probability measures

Let $μ$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geqslant 2$. We study the growth of $w_μ(t)=μ(\{x:q_μ(x)\leqslant t\})$, where $q_μ$ is the Tukey half-space depth function of $μ$. We prove that $w_μ$ satisfies the doubling bound $$w_μ(λt)\leqslant C^nλ\left(1+\frac{\logλ}{n-1}\right)^{n-1}w_μ(t)$$ for every $λ>1$ and $0<t<1/λ$, where $C>0$ is an absolute constant. It follows that for every $\varepsilon>0$ we may write $w_μ(λt) \leqslant A_\varepsilon^n λ^{1+\varepsilon}w_μ(t)$ for some constant $A_\varepsilon>0$. We construct a family of symmetric log-concave measures in every dimension $n\geqslant2$ showing that no linear doubling bound with a dimension-dependent constant holds uniformly over this class. The proof of the doubling bound uses a pointwise comparison of half-space depth with the Cramér transform, dual radial coordinates, and a relative entropy estimate for transverse covariance determinants.
The Dunford-Pettis property and complemented Hilbert subspaces of Sobolev martingale spaces

Let $L^1_W$ be the space of integrable terminal values of martingales on a homogeneous tree whose local differences belong to a fixed matrix space $W$. We show that $L^1_W$ has the Dunford-Pettis property if and only if $W$ is spanned by its rank-one matrices. Every complemented reflexive subspace of $L^1_W$ is isomorphic to a Hilbert space. Under the second structural condition of Ayoush, Stolyarov and Wojciechowski, the martingale fractional integral of order $\frac12$ is completely continuous and fails to be absolutely $2$-summing. This gives nonisomorphism with $L^1$ for $W\ne0$. On the $4$-ary tree we exhibit all three possible combinations of the Dunford-Pettis property and the existence of a complemented copy of $\ell^2$. In one example a bounded operator into $\ell^4$ fails to be completely continuous, although every bounded operator into a Hilbert space is completely continuous. We also prove that, for every $n\ge1$, each complemented reflexive subspace of $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^n)$ is isomorphic to a Hilbert space.
Economic cap coverings for log-concave measures

Let $μ$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Write $q_μ$ for its half-space depth, $W_t=\{q_μ\leqslant t\}$ for its wet part, and $w_μ(t)=μ(W_t)$. For sufficiently small $t$, we construct a cover of $W_t$ by half-spaces of measure at most $A_nt$, with cardinality bounded by $$D_n\frac{w_μ(t)-w_μ(a_nt)}{t},$$ where the constants depend only on $n$. For each $0<\varepsilon\leqslant 1$ we also construct a cover by half-spaces of measure at most $(1+\varepsilon)t$, with cardinality bounded by $$B_n\varepsilon^{-(n-1)/2}\frac{w_μ(t)-w_μ(a_nt)}{t}.$$ The exponent $(n-1)/2$ is optimal for $n\geqslant 2$, as shown by the Gaussian example. We further establish containment coverings for half-spaces in every dimension: there is a family of $O_n(w_μ(t)/t)$ Borel covering sets, each of $μ$-measure $O_n(t)$, such that every half-space of measure at most $t$ is contained in one covering set. We also obtain a relative wet-part estimate with sharp exponent $2/(n+1)$ and a reverse doubling inequality.

We introduce and study a class of geometric dynamical systems on Riemannian manifolds called spin-geodesic systems, in which the motion of a point is coupled to an internal classical spin through a symmetric endomorphism field $B$, the spin-coupling field. These systems may be viewed as $B$-dependent deformations of geodesic motion and have connections with frame flows, magnetic geodesic flows, and nonholonomic rolling systems. We show that every spin-geodesic system admits an equivalent interpretation as a no-slip rolling system in an abstract ambient geometry; when the associated metric connection, determined by $B$, is flat, this construction reduces, under the usual integrability hypotheses, to ordinary rolling on a Euclidean hypersurface. Our second main result is a Liouville theorem: for an arbitrary symmetric spin-coupling field B, the spin-geodesic flow preserves the canonical Liouville volume on its mechanical phase space. This holds even though the flow is not symplectic unless $B$ is identically zero.
The coordinate dependence of numerical rank: charts adapted to level sets

Sampling a smooth field on a grid can give an array of high numerical rank even when the field is simple. A Gaussian ridge rotated off the grid axes is the standard example: in coordinates which follow the ridge, the same field has rank one. The rank therefore depends on the chart, that is, on the coordinates in which the field is sampled. We ask which properties of a chart control this rank. For a field which depends on position only through a function $φ$, a chart whose coordinate lines follow the level sets of $φ$ gives rank one. Building on this, we show four things. First, mesh quality does not control rank: a chart whose cells have perfect size and shape can still give infinite rank. Second, when a chart follows the level sets of an estimate of $φ$, the extra rank depends on a single quantity, the defect, which measures how much the true field varies along each coordinate line. Its size matters only logarithmically, its complexity through a count which cannot be improved in general, and when the defect is simple across the level sets the cost stays small. Third, whether the defect is simple can be checked by differentiating the true level function along the flow which builds the chart. Fourth, rank and invertibility fail differently. When the curve behind an offset chart is perturbed, the rank grows slowly, but the chart stops being invertible abruptly, once the offset exceeds the distance at which neighboring normals of the curve first cross. A chart built from the level sets of a field estimate stays invertible when the gradient of the estimate does not vanish on the band and the coordinate lines along each level set do not cross themselves. Pre-registered experiments in two dimensions show how far the bounds are from the observed ranks, and suggest when each kind of chart is preferable; two choices in the last comparison were made after the experiments.
A Principled Framework for PDE-Based Shock Capturing in High-Order Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
Aaron Marques; Alireza H. Razavi; Masayuki Yano; Matthew J. Zahr

PDE-based artificial viscosity (AV) captures shocks in high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods by solving an auxiliary PDE for a smooth viscosity field. The behavior of that field is set by how the terms of the AV PDE scale with the element size $h$ and polynomial degree $p$, and by how its coefficients are parametrized. This work derives both choices from analysis and studies the impact these choices have on the implicit steady-state solver. First, an $L^2$-projection analysis shows that the thinnest shock a polynomial space can represent monotonically scales with the resolution length $\bar h = h/p$, and a scaling analysis of the AV PDE gives concrete conditions on its diffusion and source terms for the solution to be self-similar in $\bar h$. Prior formulations satisfy them only under $h$-refinement at fixed $p$; the AV PDE is scaled so that they hold under $hp$-refinement, and the captured shock thins accordingly. Second, a Green's-function analysis of the steady AV PDE gives closed-form expressions for the width and magnitude of the AV. In the standard parametrization the two are coupled: raising the diffusion coefficient widens the AV but lowers its peak. An alternative parametrization of the decay coefficient removes the coupling in the Green's-function response and inverts it in the coupled state-AV problem, so that widening the AV raises its peak instead of lowering it. Third, a parameter study on a Mach 5 viscous flow over a half-cylinder characterizes how the choice of solution variables and the AV PDE's time, width, and magnitude coefficients affect the robustness and cost of the implicit solve. The choice of variables dominates robustness, with entropy variables converging over the largest region of the width-magnitude parameter space. Together, the three contributions make PDE-based AV more predictable to tune and its implicit solve more robust.
Trigonal Elliptic Coordinates on the Sphere and Some Applications

We construct a theta-function parametrization of the unit sphere adapted to the eight trigonal directions. The construction follows from a cubic theta identity discussed by Bobek and admits an equivalent representation in Jacobi elliptic functions. The angular parameter and theta nome give a nonorthogonal coordinate system whose squared Cartesian components are related to the three-component Volterra chain. An algebraic change of angle, retaining the nome, yields orthogonal coordinates with explicit metric coefficients and a diagonal Laplace--Beltrami operator. We apply both parametrizations to the geometry of O'Brien's reduced Jahn--Teller model and give compact expressions for real spherical harmonics of degrees two and three. The orthogonal angle is the polar angle of an $E_g$ quadrupolar doublet, while one octupolar harmonic depends only on the nome within each octant.
Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
A. Rod Gover; Jarosław Kopiński; Andrew Waldron

We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.
On derived Galois deformation rings in characteristic 0 and a conjecture of Venkatesh

Let $Π$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\operatorname{GL}_n$ over a CM field $F$, and $ρ$ its associated Galois representation in characteristic 0. With mild assumptions, we use the Taylor--Wiles method to define a free action of the potentially semistable derived deformation ring of $ρ$ on the $Π$-part of the $p$-adic cohomology of $\operatorname{GL}_n/F$, confirming a prediction of Venkatesh. As a key step, we establish an equivalence between the derived deformation ring of $ρ$ with the completion at the point corresponding to $ρ$ of the derived deformation ring of the mod $p$ reduction $\barρ$, generalising well-known results by Kisin.
Perfect state transfer on trees in the normalized Laplacian quantum walk

We prove that, in the normalized-Laplacian model, perfect state transfer between two vertices of a tree can only happen if they are at distance at most $2$. We show that a conjecture of Coutinho and Baptista, stating that the only trees admitting perfect state transfer are $K_2$ and $P_3$, is true when the two vertices are at odd distance. We then construct infinite families of trees admitting perfect state transfer, disproving their conjecture in the general case.
Achievable Rate and Reconstruction Fidelity of FeFET-Based Compute-in-Pixel Arrays
Mohamed Akrout; Md Rahatul Islam Udoy; Ahmedullah Aziz; Nuria Gonzalez-Prelcic; Robert W. Heath

Compute-in-pixel (CiP) image sensors such as MACPix weight each photodiode voltage by a conductance stored in a ferroelectric FET and sum the currents on a column bus, so that $N$ pixels are read as $M<N$ weighted sums before digitization. We model the column bus as a Gaussian multiple-access channel and derive its achievable rate under thermal and shot noise, device variation, and ADC distortion. Conductance variation acts as noise proportional to the scene energy, which limits the rate to $4.5$ bits per readout and makes a 6-bit ADC sufficient. End-to-end simulations recover natural images at $26.3$ dB from 2 bits per pixel and, for sparse scenes, reduce the edge-node energy by up to $6.4\times$ against raw 8-bit readout.
Improved Omega results for Riesz sums of a class of $L$-functions
Arindam Roy; Jagannath Sahoo; Akshaa Vatwani

We investigate a general class of $L$-functions satisfying functional equations with multiple gamma factors, and establish sharper lower bounds for the error terms associated with the Riesz sums of their coefficients. By integrating the resonance method with Riesz smoothing, we improve upon previously known omega results for the corresponding Riesz sums. We prove these estimates within a unified axiomatic framework under a precise set of hypotheses. Our general theorem can be applied to several classical arithmetic problems, including the $k$-fold Piltz divisor function $d_{\mathbb{K},k}(n)$ over a number field $\mathbb{K}$, as well as the lattice point counting functions for the circle, ellipse, and sphere problems. In particular, we sharpen the classical $Ω$-bound for the error in counting lattice points in the ellipse $u^2+5v^2\le x$, strengthening a result of Nowak. Moreover, for the smoothed error terms corresponding to the divisor and circle problems, we improve upon previously known $Ω$-bounds by increasing the exponent of the $\log\log x$ factor and sharpening the $\log\log\log x$ dependence by replacing exponential decay factors of the form $\exp(-c\sqrt{\log\log\log x})$ in previous results with an explicit polynomial power of $\log\log\log x$.
Elliptic curves with torsion Z/5: exact rank four over Q(k) and rank at least five infinitely often

We give two elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(k)$ with torsion group $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank exactly $4$, with four explicit independent points. The upper bounds come from reducing the relevant elliptic surfaces modulo suitable primes and are unconditional. They match the known lower bound for the generic rank with this torsion, due to Eroshkin, and are not isomorphic to Eroshkin's curve or to each other: their parametrising maps to $X_1(5)$ have degree $8$ instead of $12$, the constructions are dihedral rather than biquadratic, and their branch loci differ. In each case, two of the points come from a ``doubling'' step in the spirit of Jaswal. Adding one further condition to the second curve, coming from a quadratic twist over an intermediate conic, gives a fifth independent point over a genus-one curve of rank two. Hence there are infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank at least $5$, improving the known bound $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 4$ to $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 5$.
Limit theorems for almost conditionally identically distributed random variables

$ξ$-Almost Conditional Identically Distributed ($ξ$-a.c.i.d.) random variables are generalizations of conditional identically distributed (c.i.d.) and exchangeable ones. $ξ$-a.c.i.d. random variables arise naturally in applications in statistics, such as in recursive algorithms and heteroskedastic observations, and are parametrized by a sequence $ξ=(ξ_{n})_{n\geq 0}$ that quantifies departure from the c.i.d. property. In this work, we extend limit theorems for exchangeable and c.i.d. random variables to the more general setting of $ξ$-a.c.i.d. random variables. After proving a Strong Law of Large Numbers, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the asymptotic directing measure of the sequence to be absolutely continuous with respect to a given $σ$-finite measure. Then, under regularity assumptions on the parameter $ξ$, three different Central Limit Theorems for $ξ$-a.c.i.d. sequences are derived, involving the predictive, empirical and asymptotic directing distributions. These theorems have several statistical applications, including the construction of asymptotic credible intervals in Bayesian predictive inference.
On locked states for damped driven Jaynes--Cummings equations
A. I. Komech; E. A. Kopylova

We consider damped driven version of the Jaynes-Cummings equation which describes quantised one-mode Maxwell field coupled to a two-level molecule. The pumping and dissipation operator are polynomial in the creation and annihilation operators. The structure of the dissipation operator corresponds to the theory of completely positive trace preserving operators due to Lindblad, Kossakowski and others. We construct examples of {\it locked states} which are stationary states of the corresponding averaged dynamics in the interaction picture. The states are nonnegative Hermitian density operators with finite Hilbert-Schmidt norm. The calculations rely on the recurrence equation for diagonal entries.
Exotic Universal Covers and Free Cyclic Actions from the Cartwright-Steger Surface
Anar Akhmedov; B. Doug Park; Sümeyra Sakallı; Sai-Kee Yeung

For every $m\geq2$, we construct a closed minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $35$, and signature $1$. The construction is a genus-five symplectic sum of a blowup of the regular fourfold Cartwright-Steger cover and a cyclic Akhmedov-Park manifold. The gluing identifies the homomorphisms from the two surface groups to $\Z/m$. The universal cover is minimal symplectic and is homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $(18m-1)\CP\#(17m-1)\CPb$. It admits a free symplectic action of $\Z/m$. Intermediate quotients give examples with fundamental group $\Z/n$ and characteristic numbers $(e,σ)=(35k,k)$ for every $n\geq2$ and $k\geq1$. Using the same Cartwright-Steger summand, we also construct, for every $m\geq2$, a minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $31$, and signature $1$, whose minimal symplectic universal cover is an exotic copy of $(16m-1)\CP\#(15m-1)\CPb$ with a free symplectic $\Z/m$-action.
The Z[tau]-foam: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam as arithmetic in the icosahedral module
Miguel E. Pérez Ibarra; Jaziel Flores Rodríguez

Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam is a substitution that fills the regular dodecahedron with dodecahedral bubbles of sizes tau^{-k}, tau=(1+sqrt(5))/2, using the seven kinds of cells into which the twelve planes of its stellation cut it. We rewrite it as exact arithmetic in one Z[tau]-module of rank three, the span M of the six five-fold axes, on which the icosahedral group acts by 120 matrices in GL(3,Z[tau]). A placed inflated copy of a cell is a union of cells iff its facet levels lie in {+-1,+-tau^3} and it lies in the dodecahedron. Solving this finite linear system for all scales at once gives exactly the 22 rules known from a geometric search; no rule exists at any scale other than 1,tau,tau^2,tau^3. The substitution becomes integer arithmetic on six-tuples and reproduces the bubbles of the geometric foam exactly. Whether a point of M is the centre of a bubble of size tau^{-k} is decided by at most k+3 exact sign vectors (its address), without building the foam, and all bubbles of one size are obtained by sieving the points of M whose Galois conjugate satisfies |x^*|<=2 tau^k, a bound we prove with computer assistance. The number of bubbles of size tau^{-k} is A beta^k+O(|beta'|^k) with beta=(1+sqrt(29))/2. Hence the closure of the rescaled conjugates of the bubble centres has box dimension at most log_tau(beta)=2.4123<3, and the bubbles are not selected by any cut-and-project window with interior. The other foams of the 1999 article are sub-foams of this one. The 50400 substitutions allowed by the rule list give 18899 bubble sets, and the Dodecafoam is a product set of 13440 of them, to the depth tested. In four dimensions the same linear system, for the star cut of the 120-cell, reproduces the 718 clusters of a geometric search and adds the scale sqrt(5) tau^2.
Nonparametric estimation of a common marginal hazard function under censoring and spatio-temporal dependence
Ibrahim Loudy; Kowir Pambo Bello; Stéphane Bouka; Guy Martial Nkiet

This article investigates the nonparametric estimation of a common pooled marginal hazard function from right-censored durations exhibiting spatio-temporal dependence.
 We propose two estimators based respectively on the Nadaraya-Watson method and the (k)-nearest neighbors (k)-NN) approach. Under assumptions of stationarity, regularity, non-informative censoring, and weak spatio-temporal dependence, we establish their pointwise and uniform convergence rates as well as their optimal asymptotic order. A simulation study compares their finite-sample performance.
 Two real-data applications with right censoring are considered: a multicenter clinical trial with 53.8 percent censoring and 1,746 geolocated and time-stamped requests submitted to New York City's 311 municipal service, of which 35.5 percent are censored.
 The empirical results illustrate the relevance of the proposed methods in the presence of spatial and temporal dependence.
Nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in {-1,0,1}

We determine all nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$. The problem reduces to describing the set $\cN_n$ of pairs $(d,b)\in\{-1,0,1\}^n\times\{-1,1\}^{n-1}$ for which the tridiagonal matrices with diagonal $d$ and with products $b_k$ of opposite off-diagonal entries have characteristic polynomial $λ^n$. We show that $\cN_n$ is obtained from $\cN_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ by one of two explicit ``folding'' operations, according to the parity of $n$. As a consequence, $\cN_n$ is non-empty precisely when $n=1$ or $3\cdot2^j-1\le n\le2^{j+2}-1$ for some $j\ge0$, in which case it has $2^{\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$ elements. This yields a formula for the number of nilpotent $n\times n$ tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$, which begins $1,9,73,585,4809,39113$. The case $d=0$ is a conjecture of Corless, established in an earlier paper. The main new ingredient is a rigidity phenomenon: a pair as above, of size $n\ge2$, whose characteristic polynomial is congruent to $λ^n$ modulo $4$ is necessarily a fold of a smaller pair. It follows that such a pair is nilpotent as soon as its characteristic polynomial is congruent to $λ^n$ modulo $2^{1+\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$. Finally we show that the eigenvalue zero of an $m\times m$ matrix in Corless's skew-symmetric family has multiplicity at most $2^{v_2(m+1)}-1$, with equality attained. The classification, the rigidity statement, the cardinality of the sets $\cN_n$ and the criterion modulo $2^{1+\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$ have been formalised in Lean~4.

The aim of this paper is to revisit our work [J. Funct. Anal. 277 (2019), 333--367], where fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces were introduced and their behavior as the fractional parameter $s\uparrow1$ was studied, and to redo it without assuming the $Δ_2$ condition on the Young function $G$ or on its complementary function. Since that paper appeared, the theory of these spaces has been considerably developed, and the tools available today allow for a cleaner treatment in full generality. We prove a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type formula as $s\uparrow1$, a compactness and lower semicontinuity result for sequences with bounded energy, a Poincaré inequality uniform in $s$, and the $Γ$-convergence of the fractional modulars to a local modular on arbitrary open sets. As an application we study the asymptotic behavior of minimizers and of solutions of Dirichlet problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian as $s\uparrow1$. This version also corrects some errors in the original paper, and it is intended to serve as a more complete and reliable reference for these results.

Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative Noetherian algebras over an arbitrary field $\Bbbk$ such that $A\otimes_\Bbbk B$ is Noetherian. Let $I$ and $J$ be ideals of $A$ and $B$, respectively, and let $L$ and $N$ be nonzero finitely generated modules over $A$ and $B$, respectively. In \cite{R4}, the author investigates the relationships between certain algebraic properties of $L\otimes_\Bbbk N$ and the corresponding properties of $L$ and $N$, and vice versa. In the present paper, we characterize the Gorensteinness, approximate Cohen--Macaulayness, and maximal depth property of $L\otimes_\Bbbk N$ with respect to $\mathcal{I}=I\otimes_\Bbbk B+A\otimes_\Bbbk J$ in terms of the corresponding properties of $L$ and $N$ with respect to $I$ and $J$, respectively. In particular, when $A$ and $B$ are local rings, we describe these properties of $L \otimes_{\Bbbk} N$ as a module over the local ring $A \otimes_\Bbbk B$.
Independent and end-faithful spanning trees in infinite graphs

Spanning trees rooted at the same vertex are independent if, for each vertex other than the root, the paths from the root to that vertex are pairwise distinct and internally vertex-disjoint. Zehavi and Itai conjectured that, for every positive integer $k$, every finite $k$-connected graph has $k$ independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. We show that every $2$-connected graph, finite or infinite, has two independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. For locally finite $2$-connected graphs, both trees can be chosen end-faithful. We also prove that every locally finite $3$-connected chordal graph has three independent end-faithful spanning trees. Counterexamples show that local finiteness is essential for the version with independent end-faithful spanning trees. We further show that every $3$-connected graph with a universal vertex or a finite vertex cover has three independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex.
Robust Pair--Restricted Lipschitz Regression with Global--Local Transfer
Sergi Sanjuan; Enrique A. Sánchez Pérez; Roger Arnau

We develop a robust pair-restricted Lipschitz regression framework for grouped longitudinal data represented as finite trajectories in a space equipped with a prescribed or learned pseudometric. For a fixed geometry, latent responses and a Lipschitz bound are estimated jointly through a convex optimisation problem with constraints imposed on selected trajectory pairs. We show that the choice of fidelity loss leads to different structural behaviour: Huber regularisation strictly reduces the pair-restricted Lipschitz seminorm whenever the exact interpolant has a finite positive seminorm, whereas $L^1$ fidelity can preserve exact interpolation below a data-dependent threshold. For grouped observations, global and local Lipschitz structures are combined while keeping group identity outside the trajectory geometry. The global component draws on observations from other groups, while the local component uses each group's history to account for group-specific behaviour. We also characterise when group-specific observations can be fitted exactly under a shared Lipschitz bound and establish a regularity bound for the combined predictor. We describe a computational implementation based on constraint generation and illustrate the framework through an application to longitudinal sow-production data.
Invariant subspace problem for trace-class perturbations of subnormal operators
Kunyu Guo; Chunlan Jiang; Penghui Wang; Zeyou Zhu

Let $S$ be a subnormal operator on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and let $K$ be a trace class operator. In the present paper, we prove that $S+K$ has a nontrivial invariant subspace. Furthermore, for a normal operator $S$, we prove that if the Hausdorff dimension of $σ(S)$ is greater than $1$, then $S+K$ has a hyperinvariant half-space.
Weak-Weak Stability for Multi-Species Nonlocal Cross-Diffusion Systems with Endpoint Lorentz Kernels
Ansgar Jüngel; Tuan Tung Nguyen; Zhiwei Sun

The quantitative weak-weak stability for multi-species nonlocal cross-diffusion systems on the torus is established. The interactions of the species are described by a symmetric, positive semidefinite matrix-valued kernel whose gradient belongs to the endpoint Lorentz space $L^{d,\infty}$, where $d\ge 2$ is the space dimension. The central estimate, formulated in terms of a modulated Hellinger distance-interaction energy, yields uniqueness of solutions with finite Boltzmann entropy and Fisher information. The proof relies on a two-level endpoint mechanism: The Boltzmann entropy controls the interaction energy, while the Fisher information controls the associated force field. Further results are the immediate $L^2$ regularization and the exponential decay to the homogeneous equilibrium. As a particular application, uniqueness and stability for the two-dimensional Poisson-Nernst-Planck system with periodic Coulomb kernels are obtained.
Totally geodesic sets and Caratheodory geometry in the polydisk

A subset $V$ of the polydisk ${\mathbb D}^N$ is called totally geodesic if every pair of points in $V$ lie on a
 Kobayashi geodesic of ${\mathbb D}^N$ that lies entirely in $V$. It is called a Caratheodory set if its intrinsic Caratheodory metric agrees with the Caratheodory metric inherited from ${\mathbb D}^N$.
 We prove that for algebraic subvarieties of the polydisk these two notions coincide, and we obtain a complete geometric classification of such sets. The invariant metric geometry of the polydisk is unexpectedly rigid: every such set is, up to automorphism, built from only two basic geometric objects: disks and a distinguished family of two-dimensional algebraic surfaces that we call Roman surfaces.
 Roman surfaces arise independently in the study of the three-point interpolation problem in the polydisk.
JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer

As semiconductor device dimensions approach phonon mean free paths, heat transport enters ballistic and quasi-ballistic regimes where Fourier's law becomes inadequate. The phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) describes these nonequilibrium effects but presents significant computational challenges. This work introduces JAX-Nano, a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable phonon BTE solver for nanoscale heat transport. The solver integrates steady-state and transient BTE formulations within a unified finite-volume framework, supporting structured and unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, phonon scattering, volumetric heat generation, and multiple boundary conditions. Automatic differentiation enables gradient computation with respect to transport properties, boundary conditions, heat-generation rates, and geometric parameters without separately derived adjoint equations. Numerical predictions are validated against analytical solutions and established BTE solvers across diffusive-to-ballistic regimes. Applications to complex three-dimensional geometries are demonstrated using single-fin, double-fin, and arrayed fin field-effect transistor (FinFET) configurations. Gradient-based inverse learning enables single- and multi-parameter identification, including simultaneous recovery of mode-resolved phonon relaxation times and spatially distributed heat-generation rates in steady-state and transient problems. GPU performance and scalability are evaluated with respect to spatial resolution, angular discretization, and phonon bands, including comparisons with an MPI-based BTE solver. JAX-Nano provides a unified computational framework for three-dimensional phonon transport, automatic differentiation, and inverse parameter identification, enabling sensitivity analysis and optimization of nanoscale thermal systems.
An Implicit Discrete Adjoint Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Sensitivity Analysis and Shape Optimization in Multiscale Gas Flows
Yuze Zhu; Hangkong Wu; Kun Xu

Accurate and efficient gradient-based sensitivity evaluation remains challenging for performance optimization in multiscale flows with complex geometries. To address this challenge, this work develops a matrix-free discrete adjoint method for the steady implicit unified gas-kinetic scheme (UGKS) through the exact linearization and transposition of its converged fixed-point operator. The method employs a hybrid differentiation strategy that combines local automatic differentiation (AD) of complex nonlinear kinetic kernels with analytically derived tangent and transpose operators for the coupled macroscopic--microscopic implicit updates and mass-conservation projection.
