This makes them hard to embed and to represent accurately on current quantum annealers, in line with our D-Wave experiments.
The Global Solutions to Nonlinear Thermoelastic Systems under a Null Condition

We study the Cauchy problem for a class of homogeneous, isotropic nonlinear thermoelastic systems in three space dimensions. Under a null condition for purely elastic part of our system which is different from those considered by Sideris, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global classical solutions with smallness assumptions on the initial data. We use Klainerman--Sideris weighted energy estimates and time-weighted energy estimates for the heat equation to establish global existence. Moreover, we improve upon the global existence result of Ponce and Racke, who assumed that the purely elastic nonlinear terms vanish.
Generalized Markov numbers and plane lattices

We give new explicit constructions of lattice rules in the two-dimensional square and torus. It is well-known that uniformly distributed lattices (in the sense of low-discrepancy) arise from continued fractions with bounded partial denominators. We demonstrate how integers solutions of the generalized Markov equation $x^2+y^2+z^2 = kxyz-k+3$ give rise to such lattices.
Linear and Quadratic Penalties for Cardinality Constraints in Unconstrained Binary Optimization
Roman Kužel; Mátyás Koniorczyk; Janez Povh

We study penalty strategies for converting constrained binary optimization problems to quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) form on the example of the sparsest $k$-subgraph problem. We adopt an augmented Lagrangian approach involving a linear penalty in addition to the commonly used quadratic one, and show the benefits of this approach. From the constraint structure, we derive sufficient bounds on the penalty coefficients. We conduct extensive experiments comparing combinations of our different penalty strategies with a wide range of classical and quantum QUBO solvers. Our experiments show that to obtain a good-quality solution, the right penalty strategy is almost as important as the quality of the QUBO solver, and iterative approaches appear to be the most efficient. We discuss the mechanisms that lead to a degradation of the solution quality due to large quadratic penalties.
Local well-posedness for generalized inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equations

We consider the initial value problem for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation \begin{equation*} i\partial_t u+Δu=a(x)|u|^αu, \end{equation*} where $a(x)$ is a spatially dependent coefficient. We study a general class of coefficients that includes the usual inhomogeneous nonlinearity $a(x)=λ|x|^{-b}$ and coefficients with multiple singularities. We establish local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^N)$ for both the $H^s$-subcritical and $H^s$-critical cases under suitable assumptions on $a(x)$. We also extend a fractional difference estimate of Fujiwara to Lorentz spaces.
Moments, Equilibrium Equations and Barycentric Coordinates

In a previous article, we applied the classical theory of moments to establish equilibrium equations for rather general finite systems of interacting particles. An equilibrium of such a system occurs if and only if the corresponding ``zeroth'' moment $μ_0$ and the first moment $μ_1$ vanish. Our focus then was on the relationship between $μ_0$, $μ_1$ and the second moment $μ_2$ in order to produce systems of equilibrium equations solely dependent on mutual distances, including a generalization of the Albouy-Chenciner equations for central configurations in Celestial Mechanics. In the present work, we explore in depth the condition of simultaneously vanishing $μ_0$ and $μ_1$ on its own. This condition defines at once a vector space which is studied via barycentric coordinates and elementary exterior algebra, thereby yielding families of equilibrium equations for systems with any consistent number $n$ of particles and dimension $d$. As before, the present equilibrium equations are homogeneous as well as invariant by oriented isometries (for interactions depending only on mutual distances). Our method also develops and extends the approach by A. Albouy from central configurations of codimension $c=(n-1)-d$ equal to one, the so-called Dziobek configurations, to equilibria of systems of interacting particles of arbitrary codimension. Despite the similar appearance, our generalized Albouy equations constitute new equilibrium equations when $c$ is greater than one, even in the case of central configurations. The paper closes with applications to central configurations, with specific results for $n=5,6$ in dimension $d=2$.
The Boolean completion of $\mathsf{S}(L)$: a refinement of localic mereology
M. Andrew Moshier; Imanol Mozo Carollo

We construct and study the Boolean completion of the coframe $\mathsf{S}(L)$ of sublocales of a frame $L$. Realizing $\mathsf{S}(L)$ as a basis for an Alexandroff topology on $L$ and passing to the regular elements of the associated frame, we obtain a complete Boolean algebra $\mathsf{P}(L)$ whose elements are certain subsets of $L$ generalizing sublocale sets; we call them the \emph{parts} of $L$. We show that $\mathsf{S}(L)$ embeds into $\mathsf{P}(L)$ as the left adjoint of a Galois connection and that the canonical embedding of $L$ into $\mathsf{S}(L)$ extends to $\mathsf{P}(L)$. From a mereological standpoint, this completion is motivated by universalism: after proving that mereological sums and exact joins coincide for separative posets, we identify $\mathsf{P}(L)$ as the sum-completion (equivalently, the exact-join-completion) of $\mathsf{S}(L)$, thereby supplying the mereological sums that $\mathsf{S}(L)$ lacks. Finally, we single out several distinguished parts of a frame: the pointless part, which extends Ball's construction beyond the $T_1$ setting, together with the part of merely points and the topological glue, the former of the two having no counterpart in the classical theory of sublocales.
Classification of strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure surface singularities with imperfect residue fields

We study strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure normal surface singularities whose residue fields are not necessarily perfect. We characterize strong $F$-regularity in terms of the weighted dual graph and geometric reducedness of the exceptional components of the minimal resolution, extending Hara's classification over algebraically closed residue fields. We also determine the possible dual graphs of $F$-pure surface singularities and give converse criteria. Notably, the exceptional components of an $F$-pure surface singularity are geometrically reduced unless the singularity is a rational double point.

For reflected Brownian motion in an interval of length $N$, we consider the first time at which the length of time since the most recent visit to the boundary reaches $M$; this random `lifetime' comes from the interpretation in which the Brownian motion has a finite energy capacity $M$, uses energy at unit rate in the interior, and gets its energy replenished up to $M$ on every visit to the boundary. We prove distributional asymptotics for the lifetime in three different regimes depending on the relative growth of $N$ and $M$; these one-dimensional results parallel results in the random walk case by Wade and Grinfeld. We also present some initial results on the multidimensional version of the problem, for one scaling regime in the case of a ball, and conjectures on the behaviour in general domains.
Determinantal upper bounds for ternary matrices

We obtain a new, sharper upper bound for the determinant of a matrix of order $n \equiv 2 \pmod{3}$ with entries in the complex third-roots of unity. This bound is an analog of Ehlich's bound for binary matrices of order $n \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$ and it is obtained by first applying an appropriate normalization, or balancing, procedure for matrices with root-of-unity entries and then generalizing Ehlich's argument. This new bound achieves an asymptotic fraction of approximately 74% of the Hadamard bound.
Do DeepONet Trunk-Basis Preconditioners Need Training?
Jaemin Oh; Jerome Darbon; George Em Karniadakis

Trunk-basis (TB) preconditioners build the coarse space of a two-level Schwarz preconditioner from the trunk functions of a trained deep operator network (DeepONet), restricted to subdomains. Their effectiveness has been attributed to spectral bias since networks learn low frequencies first, complementing a smoother that removes the high-frequency error. Spectral bias, however, is a property of training, whereas a randomly initialized trunk with a smooth activation is already smooth. We therefore ask whether TB preconditioners need training. In one dimension, we prove that on each subdomain the span of untrained trunk functions is close to the space of low-degree polynomials under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions. Numerically, for the Poisson equation and three-dimensional linear elasticity with constant coefficients, untrained TB and piecewise polynomial coarse spaces of equal dimension yield close conjugate gradient iteration counts, while training with the standard \(\ell^2\) loss sometimes increases them. Training can improve iteration counts when high-contrast coefficients make the low-energy modes non-smooth, and if the loss measures the error in the energy norm. For the Poisson equation with contrast \(10^5\), energy-trained TB coarse spaces need fewer iterations than piecewise polynomials of equal dimension, whereas \(\ell^2\)-trained ones do not. For a topology-optimized elastic cantilever with contrast \(10^6\), the energy-trained TB space enriched with the rigid-body modes gives the fewest iterations at larger coarse dimensions. This suggests that for neural operator-based hybrid solvers, a network's inductive bias and training objective should match the solver.
A proof of Cigler's quadratic recurrence for Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions

For an integer $k\ge0$ let $a_{n,k}(x,c)$ be the generating polynomial of the Motzkin paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,k)$ that never go below height $0$, where level steps have weight $c+x$ at height $0$ and weight $c$ at positive height, and let $D_{k,n}(x,c)=\det(a_{i+j,k}(x,c))_{0\le i,j\le n-1}$. We prove that for all $k\ge0$ and $n\ge2k+2$ $$D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2,$$ a quadratic recurrence conjectured by J. Cigler in 2023 (eq. (18) of arXiv:2309.15557 and MathOverflow question 456683). As a by-product we obtain an expression of $D_{k,n}$ as a $k\times k$ determinant built from Chebyshev polynomials reduced modulo $U_k-xU_{k-1}$, together with a bilinear identity for these $k\times k$ determinants that holds for all integer shifts. We also give a proof of Cigler's companion conjecture that $D_{k,n}(x,c)$ equals the determinant of an explicit matrix $H_{k,n}(x)$ with entries $0$, $1$ and powers of $x$, and in particular does not depend on $c$; this statement has recently been proved by V. Jandhyala, and our proof was found independently. The proofs use Chebyshev polynomials, a model of $\mathbb{Q}(x)[X]/(U_k-xU_{k-1})$ by antisymmetric Laurent polynomials, a lemma on complementary minors, and a three-term Plücker relation.
Regular quadratic lattices are rare over real quadratic fields

We show that a positive definite regular quadratic lattice of rank at least 4 over a totally real number field contains a regular sublattice that represents precisely the totally positive integers lying in an ideal. Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis and a conjecture on class numbers, it follows that, for each $m$, real quadratic fields admitting a positive definite regular lattice of some rank between 4 and $m$ have density 0. Unconditionally, only finitely many real quadratic fields of narrow class number 1 admit a positive definite regular lattice of some rank between 4 and 7.
Incentive-Based Regulatory Mechanism for Tariff Design in District Heating and Cooling Networks
Hossein Hesamzadeh; Wicak Ananduta; Eric Dumont; Zacharie De Greve

Low-temperature district heating and cooling networks exchange heat bidirectionally at near-ambient temperatures. When one supplier owns the shared loop, it controls both the tariff and the network temperature that sets every user's conversion efficiency. Existing price-cap and cost-based rules leave this non-price instrument unregulated and reach neither the first-best dispatch nor an explicit division of gains. This paper proposes a two-part, incentive-based tariff that anchors the supplier's lump-sum fee, per building and hour, to an audited outside alternative and divides the participation gains through one regulated share. We model a mixed-integer bilevel Stackelberg game in which the supplier sets hourly tariffs and the temperature regime, anticipating the buildings' co-optimization of electricity and thermal exchange. We prove that the mechanism attains the first-best welfare, posts the shadow price of the efficient dispatch as its tariff, keeps every building at or above its outside option every hour, and keeps the supplier solvent whenever operation adds surplus. A Belgian case study confirms these properties. The mechanism reproduces the centralized welfare whenever operation is worthwhile, declines to operate otherwise, holds the loop at its first-best temperature, and outperforms cap-based regulation and Ramsey pricing in welfare, user protection, and cost recovery.

Extremal problems concerning the maximum number of cliques in $n$-vertex graphs from a given graph class have been widely investigated. In this contribution, we present several results on counting cliques that extend beyond the existing framework. Firstly, we address this problem for the class of optimal 1-planar graphs where we determine the maximum numbers of copies of $K_3$, $K_4$, and $K_5$ in an $n$-vertex optimal 1-planar graphs and characterize all extremal graphs. This resolves Question {\b 8.1} of Gollin-Hendrey-Methuku-Tompkins-Zhang. Secondly, we prove that every 3-connected plane quadrangulation on $n\geq14$ vertices has at most $2n-14$ 3-separators and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs. This confirms Conjecture {\b 8.2} posed by Gollin-Hendrey-Methuku-Tompkins-Zhang. Lastly, we construct, for every integer $r\geq1$, a simple 2-planar graph with $5r+3$ vertices and $44r+1$ triangles, thus disproving Conjecture {\b 8.3} of theirs. Our proofs use radial graphs, tree decomposition and SPQR trees.
Uniqueness of $L_{p}$ Minkowski Problem in the supercritical range near the affine exponent

We study the isotropic $ L_{p} $-Minkowski problem. The equation is affine invariant at the exponent $ p = -n-1 $, where all origin-centered ellipsoids with the volume of the unit ball are solutions, and it is known that the unit sphere is the only solution for $ p \in (-n-1, 1) $. We prove uniform $ C^{0} $ estimates for all solutions in the supercritical range $ p < -n-1 $. This allows us to prove a key spectral estimate of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator on solutions. We then utilize the Rayleigh quotient method with position vectors as test functions for the operator adapted from Ivaki-Milman to prove uniqueness in the range $ p \in (-n-1- δ_{n}, -n-1) $ for some $ δ_{n} > 0 $.
Real-analytic actions of higher-rank lattices preserving an ergodic volume

We classify real-analytic actions of higher-rank lattices that preserve an ergodic smooth volume on a compact manifold. On an invariant open dense set of full volume, the action is analytically conjugate to the restriction of an affine action on finitely many copies of one double quotient. The conjugacy carries Haar probability to the given volume. Analytic germ superrigidity supplies local coordinates with measurable dependence on the center. The conditional measures on coarse Lyapunov manifolds determine the law of a displaced center. A two-point joining pairs charts whose evaluations agree there and gives the change of coordinates. The resulting analytic frame bundle carries a coframe whose vector fields integrate to the homogeneous model. This gives the open homogeneous classification in Zimmer's program.
Giacomo Brunello; Wojciech Flieger; Yoshiaki Goto; Saiei-Jaeyeong Matsubara-Heo; Nobuki Takayama

We study the holonomic $D$-module whose solutions are generic-mass banana Feynman integrals with complex propagator powers and spacetime dimension. We call this the banana $D$-module. Two properties of the banana $D$-module are studied: its holonomic rank and the irreducibility of the monodromy representation. This is achieved by relating the banana $D$-module to Lauricella $F_{C}$ hypergeometric systems. Further, we expand the generic-mass banana Feynman integral and the associated discontinuity integral in terms of series solutions. Finally, we analyze the Pfaffian system arising from the banana $D$-module and construct an explicit $d\log$ representation in the equal-mass specialization.
Marie Amalore Nambi; Francesco Navarra; Ayesha Asloob Qureshi; Dharm Veer

The highest nonzero squarefree power of an edge ideal always has linear quotients, whereas this property can fail even for the facet ideal of a pure two-dimensional simplicial tree. This raises the question of which combinatorial conditions ensure linear quotients beyond the graph case. We characterize the squarefree powers of facet ideals of pure simplicial forests that have linear quotients, showing that this property is equivalent to having a linear resolution or being linearly related. We also investigate the corresponding question for undirected path ideals of forests. Here the highest nonzero squarefree power always has linear quotients for $3$-path ideals, whereas the analogous assertion fails for $4$-path ideals of trees.
Rigidity and nonrigidity for interval translation maps

Almost every infinite-type interval translation map in the Bruin--Troubetzkoy family, and in Bruin's family with any fixed number of branches, is rigid for its invariant probability, where typicality is understood with respect to the intrinsic induction parameter measure. We prove this by exhibiting explicit repeated-word blocks in the induction and showing that their cylinders recur. In the opposite direction, we give a sufficient condition for nonrigidity of a primitive aperiodic substitution: the existence of a rational periodic vector of its incidence matrix in the return-word space whose coordinate sum is nonzero. The proof gives a uniform positive lower bound for symbol discrepancies at all sufficiently large times. For self-similar Bruin maps with primitive period substitution, the same condition also implies weak mixing. We apply the nonrigidity condition to an explicit self-similar infinite-type Bruin map on eight intervals, specifying its algebraic parameters and verifying its return words.
Coerciveness for complex Hessian type equations
Gao Chen; Junbang Liu; Sijie Nie

We study complex Hessian type equations associated with right-Noetherian polynomials on compact Kähler manifolds of complex dimension $n$. For two such polynomials of the same degree $2\le d\le n$ in strict proper position, we prove that under the integrability condition and the assumption that the admissible space $\mathcal{H}_2$ is non-empty, smooth admissible solvability for $f_1$, the $d_1$-coerciveness of the associated variational functional $J_1$ on normalized potentials, and the numerical criterion for $f_1$ are equivalent to each other. This extends the existence-coerciveness correspondence of Chen-Ghosh-Wang to the lower-degree setting under weaker polynomial conditions.
Approximating technique for the solution to the ${H}^{\infty}$ -optimal control problem

This paper continues the results published in [G. Marinoschi, Appl. Math. Optimiz. 94:44, 1-29, 2026], by presenting an approximating method of calculating the solution to the $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem, which solves the robust stabilization of a system by a feedback controller, and to the associated Riccati equation. This method generates a sequence of infinite dimensional systems approximating the original system and the solution to the approximating $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem is proved to converge to the solution of the original $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem. An example for calculating the solution to the Riccati equation and the feedback controller is provided at the end.
Additive cubes are avoidable by a non-uniform morphism of length $6$ over $\{0,a,b\}$ (with $b \ge 4$ and $\gcd(a,b) = 1$)

We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over every ternary alphabet $\{0, a, b\}$ with $1 \le a < b$, $\gcd(a, b) = 1$, and $b \ge 4$, thereby solving and extending Rao's~(2015) conjecture from $b \ge 6$ down to $b \ge 4$. Our construction applies a single dual pair of parameterized non-uniform morphisms of image length at most~$6$ to the additive-cube-free word $\mathbf{w}$ of Cassaigne et al.~(2014). For $b \ge 10$, we prove that every additive square in the image is an abelian square, reducing additive cubes to abelian cubes; the absence of abelian cubes and the $24$ finite cases with $4 \le b \le 9$ are then certified via the finite-graph method of Jamet and Rosenfeld~(2026).
Operative Representation of Quasi-Arithmetic Means, Complex Branch Structure, and Covariant Commutator Defects in Iterated Logarithmic Operation Hierarchies

We investigate the bidirectional family of commutative binary operations $\mathrm{Op}_m^{(a)}[x,y] = f_a^{(-m)}(f_a^{(m)}(x) + f_a^{(m)}(y))$ ($m \in \mathbb{Z}$) generated by iterating the scaled logarithmic Cauchy isomorphism $f_a(z) = \frac{1}{a}\ln(z)$ ($a > 0$). Our analysis focuses on three structural properties of this hierarchy. First, we show that for all $m \ge -1$ the associated quasi-arithmetic Kolmogorov-Nagumo means $S_{\mathrm{Op}_m}(\mathbf{x})$ admit a closed two-stage operative representation $S_{\mathrm{Op}_m}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathrm{Op}_{m+1}^{(a)}[\mathrm{Op}_m^{(a)}[\mathbf{x}], N_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(n)]$ with normalization factor $N_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(n) = f_a^{(-m)}(1/n)$, and prove that this internal operative normalizability via a distributive adjacent level characterizes logarithmic generators among continuously conjugated group operations. Second, we show that for $m \le -2$ and $n \ge 2$ the normalization factor leaves the positive real domain $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, motivating the analytic continuation onto the Riemann surface of the logarithm; there, a fundamental dichotomy emerges between the internal branch-index invariance of $\mathrm{Op}_{-1}^{(a)}$ and the associativity defect $ω(x,z)$ generated by $\mathrm{Op}_2^{(a)}$. Third, for arbitrary levels $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ and sample sizes $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we derive the general covariance pushforward theorem $\mathrm{Sp}_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) = f_a^{(-m)}(\mathrm{Cov}(f_a^{(m)}(\mathbf{x}), f_a^{(m)}(\mathbf{y})))$ governing the commutator defect between mean formation and the adjacent operation.
Weighted fixed-bidegree subelliptic estimates for the \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on Lipschitz pseudoconvex domain

We establish two types of \emph{a priori} subelliptic estimates for the twisted \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on a bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary. The estimates feature a subelliptic gain in \((0, 1/2)\) and are uniform with respect to the bidegree. The boundary is assumed to satisfy a plurisubharmonic-type condition, characterized by the local existence, near each boundary point, of a bounded plurisubharmonic function whose Hessian blows up algebraically near the boundary, with potentially different exponents at different points. The twisting function is holomorphic in a neighborhood of the domain, has bounded gradient, and its critical set inside the domain consists of isolated interior points with finite vanishing orders.
Solutions with one dimensional concentration for a two dimensional Schrödinger model with general potential and involving mass subcritical and supercritical exponents
Lipeng Duan; Suting Wei; Jun Yang

We prove the existence of solution $(\tilde u, λ)$ which concentrates on stationary and non-degenerate curve, as $p_ε\to 6$, to the following mass-constraint nonlinear Schrödinger equation \begin{align*} \begin{cases} - Δ\tilde u + W({\bf y}) \tilde u - |\tilde u|^{p_ε-2} \tilde u = λ\tilde u, \quad {\bf y} \in \mathbb{R}^2, \\[2mm] \int_{\R^2} |\tilde u|^2 {\mathrm d} {\bf y} =a. \end{cases} \end{align*} Here $λ$ is a Lagrange multiplier, $ W({\bf y})$ is a real-valued potential, $a \in \mathbb{R}_+$ is a constant, $p_ε= 6 \pm ε, ε\ll 1$ and $6$ is the $L^2$-critical exponent in the sense of concentration on a codimension 1 submanifold. When constructing the solution concentrating on a curve, we utilize some delicate transformations to overcome the challenges posed by the non-uniform boundedness of length of concentrating curves. In addition, we employ some refined analytical techniques to overcome the strong resonance phenomena caused by the $L^2$ constraint. Our result partially answers the Ambrosetti-Malchiodi-Ni conjecture in the setting of the mass-constrained nonlinear elliptic equation.
Constraint-Aware Anticlustering Decomposition for Certifying Pairwise-Constrained Clustering
Anna Livia Croella; Veronica Piccialli; Antonio M. Sudoso

Certifying the quality of feasible solutions to large-scale minimum sum-of-squares clustering with pairwise must-link and cannot-link constraints remains challenging, as it requires strong lower bounds on the optimal objective value. We propose a decomposition framework that partitions the data points into smaller subsets, called anticlusters, and solves the induced clustering subproblems to obtain a certified optimality gap for the original problem. To preserve pairwise information, we introduce the Constrained Anticlustering Problem (CAP), which assigns each connected component of the constraint graph to a single anticluster while seeking geometrically representative subsets. We formulate CAP as a mixed-integer second-order cone program and develop a variable neighborhood search heuristic to construct high-quality decompositions. The resulting lower bound remains valid even when the induced subproblems are not solved to global optimality. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets with up to approximately 4,000 observations show that our approach can achieve mean optimality gaps below 1% at a modest computational cost.
Global Critical $L^3$ Well-Posedness for the Stochastic Tamed Navier--Stokes Equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with Wiener and Jump Noise

We study the global well-posedness for the three dimensional stochastic tamed Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with multiplicative Wiener and compensated Poisson noise. When noise coefficients are globally Lipschitz on $L^3_σ(\mathbb R^3)$ and satisfy spatial $H^1_σ$ regularity assumptions, the system admits a pathwise unique global, probabilistically strong, critical mild solution for any initial datum $u_0 \in L^0(Ω, \mathcal F_0; L^3_σ(\mathbb R^3)) $. Neither smallness nor moment or finite kinetic energy assumptions on $u_0$ are required. We also establish that the global solution depends continuously in probability on the initial datum in uniform-in-time $L^3$ and space-time $L^5$ norms on every finite time interval.
Boundary gradient asymptotics for superquadratic viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equations via optimal control

We study the boundary behavior of the maximal solution of \[ -Δu + |\nabla u|^{p} + λu = f \] on arbitrary bounded $C^{2}$ domains, where $p > 2$ and $λ> 0$. For bounded state-dependent terms $f$, we resolve a conjecture of Lasry and Lions by establishing sharp boundary gradient asymptotics without geometric restrictions on the domain. Previously, such asymptotics were established only for certain classes of domains with additional restrictions on $p$ and $f$. We also extend the analysis to state-dependent terms that may be singular near the boundary and obtain sharp boundary profiles and gradient asymptotics. Our approach relies on stochastic optimal control and boundary blow-up analysis. Dynamic programming estimates and comparisons of near-optimal trajectories establish tangential invariance of boundary blow-up limits, leading to the identification of one-dimensional profiles and the asymptotic formulas. For the associated state-constrained control problem, we establish sharp asymptotics for the minimizing feedback and deduce its admissibility and optimality, with corresponding results for the ergodic problem.
Scattering by two parallel semi--infinite arrays of sound--soft scatterers

This article considers the scattering of an acoustic wave by two identical semi--infinite arrays of point scatterers which are positioned parallel to one another. The resulting system of scattering coefficients is formulated as a pair of coupled discrete Wiener--Hopf equations with a full $2\times2$ matrix kernel composed of two scalar kernel functions that represent interaction within the selected array and between the two arrays. Exploiting the symmetry of the two arrays, we introduce symmetric and antisymmetric components of the scattering coefficients, which decouple the matrix Wiener--Hopf system into two independent scalar problems with kernels given by the sum and difference of the two original kernel functions. The scalar Wiener--Hopf equations are then solved using the Wiener--Hopf technique in a very similar way to what has previously been used to solve the semi--infinite array problem. The original definitions of the two scalar kernels are represented by a lattice sum and practical evaluation techniques are discussed. Comparisons with previous work are also critically discussed. The resulting formulation provides an exact analytical solution to a coupled semi--infinite array problem and illustrates how symmetry can reduce a discrete matrix Wiener--Hopf problem to two scalar problems.
An affine surface with 3-step nilpotent fundamental group

We construct a smooth complex affine surface $Y$ such that $π_1(Y)$ is virtually $3$-step nilpotent, but not virtually $2$-step nilpotent. This gives a negative answer to the quasi-projective version of Campana's nilpotency problem.

Let us call a trivial braid hard if it cannot be untangled by Reidemeister moves without increasing the number of crossings. Are there hard trivial braids? Our paper answers this question. Hard braids exist. For every number of strands starting from 4, for every even length starting from 16, we present examples of hard trivial braids of that size. Our smallest example is minimal. We prove that there are no hard braids on three strands. On four strands our shortest example, of length 16, is a shortest hard braid. The hard braids in that family can be untangled without increasing their length if we use Reidemeister moves and an infinite family of moves $σ_i^{\varepsilon}σ_j^{m}σ_i^{-\varepsilon} \leftrightarrowσ_j^{-\varepsilon}σ_i^{m}σ_j^{\varepsilon}$, which involve only three strands. We also build a harder family of hard braids which no moves confined to a bounded number of strands can untangle. For every $m$ we construct a trivial braid on $4m$ strands, of length $16m^2$, which can be untangled without increasing its length by moves on $2m+1$ strands but not not on $2m$ strands.

This article gives a survey of the AF-embedding problem for $C^*$-algebras. The problem asks when a given $C^*$-algebra $A$ embeds into an \emph{approximately finite dimensional} (AF) $C^*$-algebra (a direct limit of finite dimensional $C^*$-algebras). This is largely based on my paper ``Subalgebras of simple AF algebras,'' which shows that separable, exact $C^*$-algebras satisfying the UCT and admitting a faithful, quasidiagonal trace embed into a unital, simple AF algebra. Some other results are also discussed.
Diameter Growth of $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ under Cliff Metrics

Cliff metrics are right invariant Riemannian metrics on the unitary group $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ introduced by Nielsen and his collaborators in the geometric approach for gate complexity in quantum computations. In this paper, we compute the exponential growth rate for the diameter of $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ equipped with cliff metrics as $N \rightarrow \infty$. We prove that if the norm of most generalized Pauli matrices are sufficiently large, this growth rate coincides with the growth rate of maximal gate complexity obtained by Knill.
The inverted harmonic oscillator in Segal-Bargmann space: Time-asymmetric propagator reconstruction and bi-coherent states
Hongze Ding; Ni Liu; J. -Q. Liang

We investigate the real-time dynamics and resonance quantization of the inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Its self-adjoint Hamiltonian on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ has a real continuous spectrum, while generalized resonance states outside $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ have purely imaginary energies $\pm i\hbarω(n+1/2)$. In coordinate space, these states are expressed in terms of complex Hermite polynomials and are biorthonormal under the Fresnel Gaussian pairing. Adapting Moriconi's coordinate-time transformation to the real-time path integral, we derive the exact Feynman propagator. Using Mehler's formula, we show that each discrete expansion alone reconstructs the full unitary kernel on its time half-axis, with the decaying Gamow-Siegert branch converging for $T>0$ and the growing antiresonant branch converging for $T<0$. In the complex-scaled Segal-Bargmann representation, the two Hamiltonians take the form $\pm i\hbarω(z(d/dz)+1/2)$, and their monomial eigenfunctions map back to the dual complex Hermite states. The two convergence domains correspond to one-sided contraction semigroups of dilations. Finally, we construct bi-coherent states whose biorthogonal position and momentum second cumulants are purely imaginary and complex conjugate, with product $\hbar^2/4$. The corresponding Heisenberg expectation values follow the exact classical hyperbolic trajectories for arbitrary real initial positions and momenta.

Let \(\Pow(S)\) denote the semigroup of all nonempty subsets of a semigroup \(S\), with multiplication induced from \(S\). We prove that every monoid \(M\) is reconstructible from \(\Pow(M)\), even among arbitrary semigroups: if \(\Pow(M)\cong\Pow(T)\), then \(T\) is a monoid and \(M\cong T\). The resulting isomorphism is uniquely determined by the singleton subsets of units and the two-point subsets \(\{1,a\}\) of nonunits. The main difficulty is to recover multiplication without assuming that an isomorphism of power semigroups preserves singletons. We resolve it by reconstructing finite multiplication cycles and the translation geometry of infinite mixed-power orbits. We also describe the induced split epimorphism between automorphism groups and exhibit examples where nonregular singletons are not preserved.
A 2D Free Boundary Model for Atherosclerosis with Diffusion and Elasticity
Ghada Abi Younes; Nader El Khatib; Nicolai Bessonov; Vitaly Volpert

We propose a coupled elasticity--diffusion model on a deformable domain to describe the interaction between diffusion and mechanical deformation. We first study the two-dimensional formulation and investigate its numerical behavior. A quasi-stationary formulation is then derived, and a linear relation between the total mass of the diffusing species and the volume change of the domain is established. Next, a one-dimensional reduction is introduced as a particular case of the two-dimensional model to provide additional analytical insight into the coupled dynamics. Finally, the proposed framework is applied to a model of atherosclerosis, where numerical simulations illustrate the influence of the model parameters on inflammatory wave propagation and arterial wall deformation.
Gradient Stability of the Morrey and Hardy inequalities

We find that the quantitative gradient stability estimate for the Morrey inequality in a ball $B_R$ fails with respect to any exponent of the {\it gradient-level} distance $D_M(u):=\inf\{\|\nabla u-\nabla v\|_{L^p(B_R)}:v\in \mathcal{M}\}$. Instead, the estimate holds with $D_M(u^\star),$ the gradient-level distance between the Schwarz symmetrization $u^\star$ and the space of Morrey extremals $\mathcal{M}$. Nevertheless, we establish a gradient stability estimate for the Morrey inequality by slightly `weakening' the above distance. We also obtain analogous gradient stability for the geometric $L^p$-Hardy inequality in certain domains. Distinct behaviors in the stability of these two inequalities have been discussed. Furthermore, in the $L^2$-case, we investigate the optimal constants and their attainability in both the Morrey and Hardy gradient stability inequalities.
The Garnett--Jones distance theorem for rectangles

For the family of all axis-parallel rectangles in $\mathbb R^d$, $d>1$, we characterize the distance of a real- or complex-valued function of rectangular bounded mean oscillation (little bmo) to $L^\infty$ by the reciprocal of its critical exponential integrability exponent. For each $α>0$ at which the rectangular exponential moment of $f$ is finite, we construct a bounded correction so that the residual has mean absolute oscillation bounded by a dimension-dependent constant times $1/α$ on every rectangle. The proof bounds products of coordinate maximal operators between two sets in terms of the supremum of their density product over common test rectangles. Selecting a longest interval along each path lets us remove repeated visits to a coordinate, so the density exponent is independent of the number of factors. The maximal-operator estimate holds with every positive density exponent below $1/6$ in two dimensions and below $1/24$ in three dimensions.
Consensus of Consensus: Decentralized Consensus-Based Optimization
Stefania Bellavia; Massimo Fornasier; Greta Malaspina; Tim Roith

We propose and analyze a decentralized variant of Consensus-Based Optimization (CBO) for the global minimization of continuous, possibly non-convex functions accessible only through a stochastic, possibly biased, zeroth-order oracle with bounded mean-squared error. The agents are split among $N$ units of an undirected communication network. Each unit evolves its swarm of $M$ agents towards a local tracking variable, which follows the network average of the local consensus points through one round of neighbour-to-neighbour communication via a doubly stochastic mixing matrix, without any central coordinator. We show that, under an explicit condition linking the drift and diffusion parameters to $M$, all agents reach consensus almost surely, at an exponential mean-square rate governed by the spectrum of the mixing matrix. Using a finite-agent quantitative Laplace principle, we prove that, for large $α$ and provided some agent visits a neighbourhood of the global minimizer with sufficient probability, the expected mean-squared distance of the swarm from the minimizer falls below any tolerance within an explicit number of iterations, at a rate that deteriorates for poorly connected networks. We verify this hitting assumption for a simplified dynamics. Experiments on benchmarks up to dimension $d=1000$, with stochastic objectives, and on a federated learning task demonstrate the method's effectiveness.
Lower bounds for mixed moments of modular and Dirichlet $L$-functions

Let $f$ be a fixed holomorphic Hecke cusp form of level one. For every fixed positive integer $k$, we prove a lower bound of order $q(\log q)^{2k^2}$ for the $2k$-th moment of $L(1/2,f\otimesχ)L(1/2,χ)$ over primitive characters modulo a sufficiently large prime $q$.
Non-local ergodic measures in symplectic dynamics

We consider the direct product of two symplectomorphisms, one of which exhibits a basic set and the other one acts on a compact surface and has a non-degenerate elliptic equilibrium. Under a local domination condition we show that a typical real-analytic perturbation of this system displays a large normally hyperbolic lamination on which the natural invariant measure is ergodic. The proof, which introduces a novel geometric source of semi-local ergodicity, combines tools ranging from KAM theory to geometric measure theory and is robust enough to be of interest in more general configurations.

We introduce Reset Quantum Channels (RQCs), a class of quantum channels acting on a Hilbert space structured as a direct sum of an arbitrary number of subspaces. Within each subspace, the state evolves unitarily; across subspaces, it is transferred by measure-and-prepare resets along given states. In this general setting, we show that the determination of their invariant states reduces to a stochastic eigenvalue problem, whose size is set by the number of reset states rather than by the dimension of the Hilbert space, and we discuss the uniqueness of these states. We further address the primitivity and the spectrum of these channels, which we compute explicitly when the reset states commute with the unitary evolutions. Applications include a small system coupled to several thermal reservoirs. We also consider random unitary evolutions and analyze the averages of the invariant states in this setup. Finally, we show that a suitable continuous-time limit yields Lindblad generators of reset type on the algebra of block-diagonal operators.
Claw-free difference graphs of finite groups

Let $\D(G)$ be the difference graph of a finite group $G$: the graph on the non-isolated vertices of $\PE(G)-\Pg(G)$, where $x\sim_{\D} y$ if and only if $\gen{x,y}$ is cyclic and neither of $x,y$ lies in the cyclic group generated by the other. A claw is the graph $K_{1,3}$ and a graph is claw-free if it has no induced claw. We prove that for every finite group $G$, $\D(G)$ is claw-free if and only if it is a disjoint union of copies of the path $P_3$, if and only if the element orders of $G$ are prime powers or $6$, every element of order $3$ has at most one involution in its centralizer, and every involution has at most one subgroup of order $3$ in its centralizer (equivalently: $C_G(a)$ has a normal Sylow $2$-subgroup of order at most $2$ for every $a$ of order $3$, and $C_G(u)$ a normal Sylow $3$-subgroup of order at most $3$ for every involution $u$). Consequences: a nilpotent group that is not a $p$-group has claw-free $\D$ if and only if $G\cong C_6$; $\D(\Sym_n)$ is claw-free if and only if $n\le 5$; $\D(\Alt_n)$ is claw-free if and only if $n\le 6$; a non-abelian simple group has claw-free $\D$ if and only if it is EPPO or $\PSL_2(11)$ or $\PSL_2(13)$, proved family by family (this uses the classification of finite simple groups). For soluble groups we obtain a complete classification: the non-EPPO soluble groups with claw-free $\D$ are $C_6$, $D_{12}$, $C_3\rtimes C_4$ and the Frobenius groups $N\rtimes K$ with $N$ an abelian $r$-group, $r\ge 5$, and $K\cong C_6$ or $C_3\rtimes C_4$. For every group with claw-free non-empty $\D$ we show $|O_2(G)|\le 2$ and $|O_3(G)|\le 3$, and we give non-soluble examples ($\Sym_5$, $\PGL_2(7)$, $\PSL_2(11)$, $\PSL_2(13)$). We also prove that the full enhanced power graph is claw-free only for cyclic groups and clarify the relations between claw-freeness of $\D(G)$, $\Pg(G)$ and $\PE(G)$.
Structure-preserving compression of Matrix Product States
Pouriya Ghadimi; Maximilian Fröhlich; Aaron Sander; Martin Eigel; Richard M. Milbradt

Matrix product state time evolution relies on compression to control the growth of bond dimensions, but compression can break the conservation laws of the equation being solved. A truncation is not the flow of a Hermitian generator, so even a small truncation error can violate exact algebraic identities of the Schrödinger equation. For any matrix product state integrator that leaves the state in canonical form with an orthogonality center, a scalar correction restores an admissible global invariant after compression whenever the resulting scalar quadratic constraint equation admits a real root, without enlarging any bond dimension. Rank-preserving recovery searches other canonical centers when that correction fails. The geometry of the low-rank manifold provides sufficient conditions for conservation by the fixed-rank projected flow and bounds what corrections within a frozen center frame can achieve. Numerical experiments demonstrate that recovery can be required even along accurate truncated trajectories.
How many states does an exact relaxation model need? Sharp state complexity and geometric obstructions for reversible chains

How many states does a reversible Markov model need to reproduce two prescribed relaxation modes exactly? We maximize the smaller of the two stationary coordinate variances over all finite reversible chains whose states lie in a given convex region and whose coordinates relax at rates $1$ and $ρ$. Detailed balance turns this into the equilibrium of a tension-only cable network whose loads depend on the stationary masses. For the moment curve of the Wright-Fisher diffusion no finite chain is optimal: maximizing sequences converge to a unique beta law, and the best deficit with $N$ states is of order $N^{-2}$. We find the exact leading constant for states on the curve and for states in its convex hull, together with the optimal cube-root density of states. The hull constant is the curve constant times $c/(1+c)$, $c=(ρ-2)/ρ$; at $ρ=5/2$ the hull needs $\sqrt{6}$ times fewer states, although the limiting law is the same. For $ρ>8/3$ any upward enlargement of the hull lowers the constant again. All lower bounds hold for arbitrary transition graphs. At every fixed number of states an optimizer exists. On a seven-gon the smallest optimal chain jumps from three to four states while the optimal value stays constant, and a family of polygons forces the state count to grow linearly with the number of sides. Monotone vector fields give exact upper certificates, which solve an asymmetric quadrilateral at all rates and 381 polygon-rate instances in exact arithmetic. We formulate a finite-realizability problem and a finite-dictionary conjecture for polygons, and derive state budgets and exclusion tests for finite kinetic models.
Improved perimeter bounds for Hausdorff approximation by convex polygons

We investigate how closely a convex polygon with at most n vertices can approximate a plane convex body of given perimeter. For free approximation in the Euclidean Hausdorff metric we improve Popov's bound for every $n \geq 3$. We also improve his inscribed bound for every $n \geq 3$ and his circumscribed bound for $n = 3$. The common step is to join successive boundary contacts of the body and estimate the perimeter lost in passing to their convex hull.
Maoxuan Miao; Shurong Zheng; You-Gan Wang; Jiming Jiang

We introduce a family of smooth $q$-polynomial losses for robust joint regression--scale estimation. The family contains the Cauchy loss at $q=1$ and converges pointwise to the squared loss as $q$ increases. For every finite $q$, its regression score is bounded and redescending, while its scale score is bounded and permits explicit analysis of scale existence. We formulate simultaneous estimation through a surrogate likelihood with a common scale calibration $κ=1/2$ and select $q$ by maximizing the normalized surrogate likelihood over a finite candidate set. We investigate existence, large-sample behaviour, and the robustness implications of the loss family and discuss how optional modification of the scale score, for example by taking $κ=q/2$, can increase the threshold against scale explosion. This breakdown-oriented adjustment is distinct from the baseline estimator and requires its own joint breakdown analysis. An MM-type algorithm provides a practical implementation. Numerical investigations assess the resulting robustness--efficiency trade-off under different tail regimes.
Real stable multivariate Delannoy polynomials and their Rayleigh differences

The univariate Delannoy polynomials are known to have only real zeros. We construct a real stable multivariate refinement of these polynomials using weighted lattice paths and give both algebraic and combinatorial proofs of stability. More strongly, we show that every Rayleigh difference of the multivariate Delannoy polynomials is a perfect square and give an explicit factorization.
Boundary concentration and Pohozaev identity for the fractional p-Laplacian

We prove a Pohozaev-like identity for bounded weak solutions of the fractional p-Laplace equation with a locally Lipschitz nonlinearity on bounded C^2 domains, provided that s>max{1/2-1/p,0}. We compare the weak equations for the solution and its spatial deformation to show that the first-order contribution of the energy remainder is concentrated at the boundary. The boundary term involves the weighted trace, with a coefficient expressed by an integral of the one-dimensional boundary profile.
Structure-Preserving Model Reduction of Metriplectic Systems via Oblique Projections and Block Structure

Metriplectic systems combine conservative and dissipative dynamics and are characterized by energy conservation and entropy production. The degeneracy conditions underlying these properties are generally not preserved by standard projection-based model order reduction. We develop two structure-preserving reduction strategies. The first enforces degeneracy conditions through oblique projections and combines gradient-preserving and matrix empirical interpolation for hyper-reduction. The second constructs reduced bases adapted to available operator block structure, preserving degeneracy without online oblique corrections. We establish sufficient conditions for preserving the Jacobi identity and derive a priori error estimates. Numerical tests on benchmark problems demonstrate accuracy, thermodynamic consistency, and computational efficiency.
Finite Angular Derivative Sets and Almost Isometries of the Hyperbolic Disc

We prove that a subset $E$ of the unit circle is the set of points at which an analytic self-map of the unit disc has a finite angular derivative if and only if $E$ is an $F_σ$ set. We also prove that, for every countable dense subset $E$ of the unit circle, there exists an almost isometry in the sense of Garnett--Papadimitrakis whose angular derivative is finite precisely on $E$.
Very weak solutions of nonlinear elliptic systems with Orlicz growth

In this work we consider non-linear elliptic equations with respect to Orlicz growth, for instance equations of the form $$ \mathrm{div}(φ(\vert 
abla u \vert) 
abla u)= 0. $$ We study very weak solutions to this system, that is, solutions that are not a priori in the correct energy space to this equation ($φ(\vert 
abla u \vert) \vert 
abla u \vert^2 \in L^1$). On the one hand, using rather mild assumptions on the corresponding Orlicz space (we need either the $Δ_2$ or $
abla_2$ condition, but not both at the same time), we can show that the integrability of very weak solutions improves to the energy space, provided that the initial integrability is close enough to the energy space. On the other hand, mirroring the construction of Colombo and Tione (Non-classical solutions of the $p$-Laplace equation, J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2024), for the $p$-Laplacian, we give a construction of 'wild' solutions for a $L \log L$-type Laplacian.
A Structured Levenberg--Marquardt Method for Binary Tensor Completion
Yannan Chen; Xihong Yan; Bobin Zheng

We develop a structured Levenberg--Marquardt (LM) method with trust-region globalization for binary tensor completion, using triple decomposition and a logistic loss. Under a local component-residual error bound and positive outer curvature, we prove quadratic convergence of the exact iteration for damping exponents $1\leδ\le2$, without requiring full row rank. A constant-rank criterion and an explicit rank-one certificate provide sufficient conditions for the residual error bound. The analysis decomposes the local error into outer-loss linearization, factor linearization, and regularization contributions. For a symmetric nonquadratic logistic--LSE family with $δ=2$, cancellation improves the objective-model error to fourth order and the decrease-ratio error to second order. A synthetic experiment illustrates the local quadratic convergence rate. On the HCP and Enron datasets, the proposed method improves binary tensor completion accuracy while requiring fewer outer iterations than the first-order methods.
A Combinatorial Construction of Symmetric Magic Squares of Order Four

We construct all symmetric nonnegative integer matrices of order four having a common sum on every row, column, and both diagonals. The construction is a disjoint union of twelve translates of free submonoids, each with five uniquely determined nonnegative integer parameters.Twelve is the smallest possible number of classes among finite disjoint unions of translates of free submonoids generated by five elements, even when generators outside the Hilbert basis are allowed. A comparison-based case analysis supplies integer inverse formulas and assigns every point on the shared faces to exactly one class. The normal forms prove that the twelve primitive extreme-ray generators form the entire Hilbert basis: eight have magic sum two and four have magic sum four. We exhibit the underlying regular unimodular triangulation and a single perturbation direction producing all half-open boundary conventions. The resulting positive multivariate generating function specializes to an explicit rational function and a quasipolynomial of period four in the magic sum. A further consequence is a reflexive lattice polytope associated with positive symmetric magic squares.
Pairing and modular: Generalized electrons and quasiholes inside the $\boxtimes$ of topological orders

We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topologically ordered systems, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A'}$ sharing the common (non-group-like) structure $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}=\overline{\mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}}$, through the nonabelian anyon analog of the pair creation mechanism denoted as $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}=\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}\boxtimes \mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}$. We identify $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the generalized version of electron operators in general topological orders or hidden current with (half-)integer spin involving the conformal embeddings. We provide a way to construct $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the hidden topological operator and identify $\mathbf{A}\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}\mathbf{A'}$, a general class of topoloical orders, as the $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$-extended symmetry topological field theory. We also conjecture a series of underlying (unexplored) modular invariants, connecting the conformal embedding and the pairing.
Balanced Boolean Functions from Sparse Niho-Type Permutation Polynomials: Few-Valued Walsh Spectra and Applications

We study balanced Boolean functions parameterized by two-to-one mappings of the forms $P(x+x^2)$ and $P(x+x^{-1})$, where $P$ is a sparse permutation polynomial with generalized Niho-type exponents. First, for $q=2^m$ with $m$ even, we determine the complete four-valued Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function parameterized by $Q(x+x^2)$, where $Q(x)=x(1+x^{q-1}+x^{2(q-1)})$. We then generalize a permutation polynomial studied by Gupta and Sharma to the parameterized family $P_λ(x)=x^{3q-1}+λx^{2q}+λx^2$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. We prove that $P_λ$ is a permutation polynomial if and only if either $λ=0$, or $λ\ne0$ and $X^3+X+λ^{-1}$ has no root in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Moreover, the number of admissible parameters is $(q+2)/3$ when $m$ is even and $(q+4)/3$ when $m$ is odd. Thus, admissible parameters exist for every $m\geq2$, and approximately one-third of the elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$ yield permutation polynomials. For every admissible parameter $λ$, we determine the complete Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function $f_λ$ parameterized by $P_λ(x+x^2)$ and prove that this distribution is independent of $λ$. For $m\geq3$, these functions have the five-valued Walsh spectrum ${q,0,-q,-2q,-3q}$, while for $m=2$ the spectrum degenerates to four values. As applications, their supports yield projective minimal binary five-weight codes, sets with five hyperplane intersection numbers, and regular cubelike Cayley graphs with six distinct eigenvalues. Finally, for mappings of the form $P(x+x^{-1})$, we construct an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions with simple explicit trace representations.
On the Laugesen--Siudeja Conjecture: A Sharp Lower Bound and Failure of the Upper Bound

We prove the sharp lower bound in the Laugesen--Siudeja conjecture and give a counterexample to its upper bound. For every bounded convex planar domain, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $λ_1$, the area $A$, and the centroidal polar moment of inertia $I$ satisfy $λ_1A^3/I>9π^2/2$. The constant is approached by thin isosceles triangles. The lower bound follows from a rectangle comparison in the principal directions of the covariance matrix and a planar random-triangle inequality. For the upper bound, we exhibit an isosceles trapezoid on which $λ_1A^3/I>12π^2$, using Temple's inequality and exact arithmetic.
Linear Convergence of Adaptive Accelerated Gradient Methods: A Unified Framework

We establish a unified Lyapunov framework for adaptive accelerated gradient methods on smooth, strongly convex objectives. Conditions on local curvature, stepsize ratios, and coefficient variation ensure eventual linear convergence without assuming stepsize convergence. We verify these conditions for specified AdaNAG-G, smooth unconstrained AC-FGM, and AdaAGM policies and use them to design VC-FG and CC-FG. The verified adaptive main iterations require neither global smoothness nor strong-convexity parameters and avoid restart and backtracking. The framework also sharpens a fixed-step FISTA/NAG-type bound. Experiments on four smooth, strongly convex problem families illustrate complementary performance of the new methods.
Gradient-based optimization of buoyancy distributions for lazy-wave risers

This paper presents a novel gradient-based approach for optimizing the buoyancy distribution of lazy-wave offshore risers. The static response is modeled with a total potential energy formulation for a geometrically nonlinear, inextensible beam on an elastic seabed. The total potential energy is discretized by finite differences and the resulting nonlinear equilibrium system is solved by a two stage continuation procedure, in which the line length and then the buoyancy load are increased incrementally, with Newton--Raphson iterations and an Armijo line search. The design variables are the uplift ratios at the nodes where buoyancy modules may be installed. The optimization minimizes a quadratic measure of buoyancy demand subject to constraints on the maximum curvature and effective tension. The gradients of the constraints are computed by means of a discrete adjoint sensitivity analysis. Three design parametrizations are compared: a continuous formulation with independent nodal uplift ratios, a grouped formulation with fixed module assignments, and a formulation inspired by discrete material optimization that simultaneously selects the uplift ratios of a small catalog of module types and their placement along the riser. The latter yields practical designs with a limited number of module sizes. The framework provides a flexible and computationally efficient tool for preliminary design of lazy-wave configurations.
Vanishing bond-percolation threshold implies vanishing contact-process threshold
Benedikt Jahnel; Lukas Lüchtrath; Christian Mönch

We show that for any infinite, locally finite and connected graph $G$ and $p\in(0,1/2]$ the survival probability of the contact process with infection rate $λ\ge20p$ is at least $3/4$ times the bond percolation probability with retention probability $p$. In particular, $λ_c(G)\le20\,p_c(G)$ whenever $p_c(G)<1/2$, and $p_c(G)=0$ implies $λ_c(G)=0$. The proof uses a submartingale built from percolation clusters on finite balls. We contrast this with the SIR epidemic, in which every vertex is infected at most once, and for which there are graphs with $p_c(G)=0$ on which the SIR epidemic dies out almost surely for every infection rate.
A 3D PINN-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
Celia Taboada; Luis Nuñez; Angélica Casero; Pedro Navas

Cardiovascular fluid dynamics modeling relies heavily on mesh-based numerical methods such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). While accurate, these methods entail significant computational costs and complex meshing workflows that limit their translation to clinical practice. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless alternative that embeds the governing equations directly into neural network training. In this work, we propose a PINN framework for pulsatile blood flow in patient-specific geometries with dynamic lumped-parameter Windkessel (RCR) outlet conditions representing distal vascular impedance. Coupling the Windkessel ODE to a 3D network raises two difficulties: the ODE alone does not fix the pressure level, and the local pressure variations that drive the flow are orders of magnitude smaller than the basal pressure imposed by the outlet. We address them by decomposing pressure into a time-dependent basal part and a spatially varying part, an initial condition and gauge for the Windkessel equation, a global mass-balance constraint, and a periodic Fourier embedding of time. Validated on 2D canonical channels (steady and pulsatile, with and without RCR outlet), the framework is then applied to a patient-specific right pulmonary artery, reproducing outlet flow, mean pressure, and the velocity and dynamic pressure fields with errors on the order of the data resolution. Finally, we solve the inverse problem of identifying the three Windkessel parameters of the outlet from synthetic data, recovering them with errors of about 0.3% from deliberately wrong initial values. Residual biases in the local pressure field and the need to test robustness to noisy clinical data remain open, but the results support PINNs as complementary tools for meshless hemodynamics and patient-specific digital twins.
A Validation-Driven Bilevel Optimization Method for Mesh-Free PDE Solvers and Its Error Analysis
Yongcun Song; Shangzhi Zeng; Jin Zhang; Lvgang Zhang

Mesh-free partial differential equation (PDE) solvers construct discrete systems from residuals at sampled points. These solvers fit coefficients in a parameterized trial representation and select solver-design parameters governing the representation, training-residual weighting, and regularization. These parameters strongly affect solution accuracy, yet existing selection strategies are largely tailored to particular solver classes. To address this limitation, we formulate a unified validation-driven bilevel optimization framework applicable across different solver classes, in which the lower level fits coefficients using training collocation residuals, while the upper level selects solver-design parameters using held-out validation residuals. For nonlinear PDEs, however, solving the nonlinear lower-level problem to high accuracy is costly, while the adjoint system is typically ill-conditioned and indefinite. To address this issue, we propose an efficient implicit hypergradient method that approximates the lower-level response using finite, warm-started damped Gauss-Newton (GN) updates. For the adjoint solve, we use the damped GN matrix to compute an initial adjoint and to precondition a finite number of minimum residual iterations. To quantify the errors introduced by these approximations, we derive local hypergradient error bounds that separate the contributions of the finite lower-level solve, adjoint damping, and the final adjoint residual. Combining this analysis with validation sampling bounds and residual stability, we relate validation residuals to PDE solution accuracy and establish error bounds for the computed PDE solution. Numerical experiments on several nonlinear PDEs, including a high-dimensional problem, demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method across Kansa, random feature and extreme learning machine, and physics-informed neural network solvers.
Dual-Agent DRL based Cooperative Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-ISAC Networks
Kaijian Yang; Feng Wang; Guojun Han; Xin Wang; Vincent K. N. Lau

This paper considers a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network, where multiple ground base stations (BSs) provide integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services for multiple communication UAVs (C-UAVs) and sensing UAVs (S-UAVs). With the objective of maximizing the average sum rate of C-UAVs over the entire flight episode, we jointly optimize the multi-BS multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, subject to the BS transmit power budget and the sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of S-UAVs, as well as the flight mission and collision avoidance constraints of C-UAVs and S-UAVs. Based on the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) technique, we develop a dual-agent scheme, termed DeepDA-OPT, to solve the resulting constrained Markov decision process (MDP). In the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme, two agents, i.e., Agent-B and Agent-T, are specifically deployed for learning the multi-BS ISAC transmit beamformers and the C-UAV/S-UAV trajectories, respectively, where the optimal BS receive beamformers for the sensing echo signals of S-UAVs are obtained in closed form by leveraging the generalized Rayleigh quotient theorem. To mitigate the overestimation of value functions, both Agent-B and Agent-T are trained based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy-gradient algorithm. In addition, a constraint-aware noise exploration policy is employed, and the reward function is designed to incorporate a sensing penalty and a flight urgency penalty, thereby guiding the training of Agent-B and Agent-T. Numerical results show that, compared with the baseline schemes, the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme achieves a higher average sum rate of C-UAVs, while the sensing SINR constraints are empirically well satisfied and no collision violation is observed under the evaluated settings.
A local symmetry forces positivity for projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metrics

We prove that a projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metric has positive Einstein constant as soon as it admits one nonzero local real-holomorphic Killing field. Neither completeness nor a prescribed global group action is assumed. This gives a partial answer, under a local symmetry hypothesis, to the general positivity problem for Kahler-Einstein submanifolds of (finite-dimensional) projective space. The key observation is that, by Calabi rigidity, a local real-holomorphic Killing field is induced by a projective unitary vector field whose tangency propagates along any connected global Kahler immersion, without a simple-connectivity assumption. Applied to Hulin's complete continuation, this produces a global Killing field with a bounded Hamiltonian potential given by the ambient projective moment map. The resulting Laplace equation, the Omori--Yau maximum principle and Yau's Liouville theorem exclude both negative and zero Einstein curvature. We also prove a non-Einstein obstruction under uniformly negative Ricci curvature and obtain compact equivariant continuations.

In exact slow $2$-Nim, a move removes one token from each of two nonempty piles. For any number of piles, we relate Smith remoteness in the exact game to the remoteness $D$ of Moore's slow game on the piles that remain after a largest pile is removed. If the total number of tokens $N$ is odd, the exact game has remoteness $\min(D,\lfloor N/2\rfloor)$. If $N$ is even, its remoteness equals $D$ when $2D\le N$ and is either $N/2$ or $N/2-1$ otherwise. Both values can occur for the same $N$, $D$, and number of piles. We determine $D$ explicitly for five piles. This gives a six-pile remoteness formula and a rule for selecting an optimal move. Both take $O(b)$ bit operations when each pile size has at most $b$ bits. We also give a closed formula for positions with any number of unit piles and two further piles of arbitrary size. For the GM move rule, we prove the proposed descriptions of the exceptions in the four- and five-pile games and give the exact threshold at which a specified six-pile move ceases to be optimal as the largest pile grows. Finally, we classify all outcome-preserving sorted translations for five and six piles.
Karcher means of structured matrices are asymptotically structured: a study via Schatten estimates for the additive Richardson iteration

In the present work, we first study the additive Richardson iteration for the Karcher mean of complex Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrix sequences, by obtaining normalized Schatten estimates independent of the matrix dimension. These estimates are used to prove that Karcher means of structured matrices are asymptotically structured and this is proven for input HPD Toeplitz and generalized locally Toeplitz (GLT) matrix sequences. More precisely, we provide the a.c.s. approximation, which is the key for demonstrating the GLT closure under Schatten spectral bounds, and the GLT conclusion can be extended to matrix sequences with symbols that are positive definite almost everywhere. Ad hoc numerical experiments illustrate the spectral distribution consequences of these results and few related computational advantages. Concluding remarks and open problems are provided in the final section.

We construct local and global comparison maps for the Hikita conjecture in quiver gauge theories and study their analogues for finite non symmetric Cartan pairs. The construction uses quiver Hecke description of Coulomb branch and microlocal geometry. It yields comparison maps from B-algebras to the cohomology of some Lagrangians of quiver varieties. For arbitrary symmetric types, the local and global comparison maps are surjective and are isomorphisms under a B-algebra dimension bound. In finite non symmetric types, the local image is the image of the Kirwan map, i.e., the tautological subalgebra. It can be proper. Under some assumptions we also construct a non symmetric global comparison map. Crystal theoretic methods identify the set of nonempty Lagrangians with the set of isomorphism classes of simple modules of the category $\mathscr O$ of the Coulomb branch, and proves that the Lagrangians are nonempty for $\ell$-dominant $\ell$-highest weights. The proof uses microlocal modules of Coulomb branches that we define. We prove they form integral bases of the Grothendieck group of the category $\mathscr O$, with Jordan-Hölder multiplicities given by characteristic cycles. In symmetric type we prove an isomorphism between based quasimap modules at homogeneous polarized points of quiver varieties and co-specialized microlocal modules. The proof uses hyperbolic restriction and Braden's theorem. We conjecture an extension to all homogeneous points and a relative version.
A fast automatically adaptive integral equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems
Tianze Zhang; Yixuan Ma; Jun Wang

We present a fast, high-order, automatically adaptive integral-equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems. The method builds on the fast direct solver for linear second-kind integral equations and completes the mathematical formulation needed for general boundary conditions, including cases in which the simplest background Green's function is singular and cases with genuinely rank-deficient boundary conditions. Nonlinear problems are written as nonlinear second-kind integral equations and are solved by combining this fast adaptive linear solver with Newton iteration and user-specified continuation. In this way the nonlinear solver inherits the full strengths of the linear integral-equation method: a fast direct solver, arbitrary order accuracy, and automatic adaptive resolution with only a small overhead over a solve on the final mesh. The resulting algorithm is particularly effective for problems with localized or multiscale structure, including boundary layers, dense oscillations, transition regions, hypersensitive optimal-control systems, and singular perturbations. The same framework also provides a computational foundation for future studies of bifurcation and solution-branch exploration.
Gap-label bounds and optical reconstruction of Landau-subband quantum geometry

We derive a magnetic gap-label lower bound on the internal quantum weight of Landau subbands that remains nonzero even when the occupied Chern number vanishes. Using the second fundamental forms of nested subbundles to decompose the quantum geometric tensor, we isolate the constraint imposed by the uniform parent curvature and show that the excess quantum weight above the bound equals twice the weaker circular transition weight. For a noninteracting parabolic band with a periodic scalar potential, Landau-level mixing preserves the integrated relative curvature while the occupied direct gap remains open. Nevertheless, uncorrected sub-cyclotron absorption need not satisfy the projected bound. Using exact circular-dipole relations, we reconstruct the low-frequency guiding-centre weight and signed dichroism from circularly polarized absorption. This reconstruction removes the first-order orbit-polarization contribution. For an insulating filling of an isolated lowest-Landau-level-derived cluster, a potential-gradient estimate bounds the omitted remote-transition weight quadratically at weak coupling. This yields a finite-window lower bound on reconstructed quantum weight and bounds the deviation of reconstructed dichroism from the integrated relative curvature.
Conservative Implicit and Explicit Solvers for Reactive Conformable Transport with Multirate Memory

In this article, we analyze conservative implicit and explicit schemes for reactive transport with a conformable time scale and multirate exchange. The conformable derivative defines a local change of time coordinate, while exchange with immobile regions supplies the memory. Positive Gauss--Jacobi quadrature approximates the prescribed exchange spectrum by finite compartments. Both schemes use conservative finite-volume fluxes. Forward Euler gives the explicit update; backward Euler initializes the implicit second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2). Eliminating the compartment states reduces each implicit step to a tridiagonal system. Under stated mesh and regularity conditions, we prove implicit solvability, conditional explicit positivity and stability, and discrete mass balance. A cell-average error estimate separates spatial, compartment and temporal contributions. Its proof accounts for the boundary fluxes and the BDF2 startup error. Source-specific bounds make the temporal and memory prefactors uniform under mesh and compartment refinement. For a broader positive-history model, continuous residual estimates have coefficients independent of memory strength and kernel mass. Local coercivity gives a sharper coefficient. Manufactured tests recover second-order spatial convergence, first-order Euler convergence and second-order BDF2 convergence. Separate experiments examine the memory and combined estimates. In a prescribed porous-medium application, the finest numerical states differ by $3.57\times10^{-5}$ in relative space--time $L^2$. Independent resolution checks support the computed pulse attenuation, immobile storage and release after injection ends.
Smoothed Conformal Testing with Small Calibration Sets

A small calibration sample restricts split conformal $p$-values to a coarse rank grid. Randomization removes this discretization, but its effect depends on both the smoothing interval and the allocation of auxiliary random variables. Independent tie-block randomization is exactly valid under null exchangeability. When calibration and null scores are jointly exchangeable conditional on the alternative scores, we prove positive regression dependence and hence Benjamini--Hochberg false discovery rate control, including for atomic score distributions. Smoothing over calibration-dependent rank cells agrees with tie-block randomization when calibration scores are distinct and no test score ties a calibration score, but can fail marginal validity with atoms. Assigning sorted random draws according to score order can invalidate even a single null $p$-value. An exact two-test example violates the usual $π_0α$ bound, and simulations with continuous scores exhibit false discovery rates above the nominal level $α$. Finally, conditional moment identities and normal-model illustrations show that removing the rank grid does not remove calibration uncertainty. Randomization can produce additional discoveries, including when ordinary conformal testing cannot reject at all, but it does not generally substitute for a larger calibration sample.
A Geometric Approach to the Classification of Locally-APN Niho-Type Power Functions

Let $q=2^m$ with $m\geq 2$. We develop a geometric approach to the classification of locally-APN Niho-type power functions over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. Our approach begins with a characterization of $\mathbb{F}_q$-homogeneous functions: the conditions $D_F(a,F(a))=q$ and $D_F(a,b)\leq 2$ for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^*$ and $b\neq F(a)$ hold if and only if the projective graph of $F$ is a $(q+1)$-arc in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$. For Niho-type power functions, this differential condition is equivalent to the locally-APN property. Applying the classification of $(q+1)$-arcs and the description of their stabilizers, we prove, for $m\geq 3$, that $F_s(x)=x^{s(q-1)+1}$ is locally-APN if and only if $s\equiv(2^k+1)^{-1}\pmod{q+1}$ for some $1\leq k\leq 2m-1$ satisfying $\gcd(k,m)=\gcd(2^k+1,q+1)=1$. Together with the known case $m=2$ and the sufficient condition of Xie et al., this gives the complete classification and confirms the conjecture of Cui, Luo, and Xiang.
The geometric expansion of the coarse trace formula of GL(4)
Haoyang Wang; Xinghua Cui; Weilong Zhang; Zhifeng Peng

We study the non-semisimple terms in the geometric side of Arthur's trace formula of $\rm{GL}(4)$ for the further study of the invariant trace formula. After modifying the zeta function and Arthur's definition of the weighted orbital integrals, we compare the two ways to calculate the distributions $J^T(f)$ of the geometric side, we can obtain that the distributions can be written as the linear combanition of the weighted orbital integrals. In particular, we get the coefficients $a^M(S,γ)$, for all $γ\in \rm{GL}(4,F)$, expressed by the measure and zeta functions.
Stochastic Differential Equations on the Simplex

We propose a framework for simplex-valued diffusion processes, formulated as solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by antisymmetric Brownian motion. Our edge-wise representation includes the multivariate Jacobi processes and the general class of continuous simplex-valued polynomial diffusions. Also, it allows bounded, locally Lipschitz state-dependent drift rates and edge weights. We establish weak solutions, as well as global strong existence and pathwise uniqueness for strictly positive initial states under a sufficient boundary non-attainment condition.
Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
