As a result, we prove that if $f$ has no nontrivial inner twists, then $E_f$ is generated by a single prime Fourier coefficient, for a set of prime ideals of Dirichlet density one. We derive this result as a consequence of a more general theorem established for $F_f$.
Semigroup Hessian Estimates for Underdamped Langevin Dynamics

For the semigroup $e^{t\mathcal L}$ of the underdamped Langevin dynamics, we bound the Hessian $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ when $
abla f$ is uniformly bounded. When the potential is strongly convex outside a ball and has bounded second and third derivatives, and the damping rate is above an explicit threshold, the bounds on $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ decay exponentially in time with constants free of the dimension. The proof combines the Wasserstein contraction of the dynamics with a Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for the degenerate noise. As an application, we prove the uniform-in-time error of the stochastic gradient UBU integrator, with an explicit coefficient of the numerical bias in the step size, proportional to the covariance of the stochastic gradient noise.
Uncovering Multimorbidity Patterns Through a Novel Randomized Clustering Algorithm

Patients with several chronic conditions rarely share the same combination: in four years of the nationally representative Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), we find 32,789 distinct combinations of two to seven conditions, and over 90% of those involving four or more occur in a single patient. Methods that search for common combinations discard most of this heterogeneity. We present the Randomized Length Sequential Clustering Algorithm (RLSCA), which links diseases by lift, a pairwise association measure counted only above a user-set support threshold. A mixed-integer program repeatedly selects and removes the group of conditions with the greatest internal lift, up to a random size; 100 iterations yield a database of clusters scored by size, rediscovery frequency, and body systems spanned. In MEPS 2019, stratified by age and sex, RLSCA recovers known groupings at a high threshold, such as diabetes with lipid disorders and hypertension, and at a lower threshold returns clusters of up to eight conditions spanning five body systems. Frequent itemset mining, at its lowest feasible support, finds no set above five conditions; hierarchical clustering cannot control cluster size. With a clinical large language model, the database could suggest which further conditions a patient is at risk of.
Categorification of the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebras of polygons

Let $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ be the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebra of a polygon with $m$ boundary punctures ($m\geq 3$). Building on the quantum cluster algebra structure of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ established by Cao and the authors, and on the monoidal category $\mathcal{C}(Δ^{m-2})$ of finite-dimensional modules over the quantum affine algebra $U_q'(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_n)$ introduced by Kashiwara, Kim, Oh and Park, where $Δ$ is the Garside element of ${\rm Br}_n$, we give a monoidal categorification of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$. As a consequence, $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ has a basis with positive structure constants. A key role is played by the subalgebra $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ spanned by the stated $n$-webs whose $m-1$ edge weights are zero. We show that $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ is a quantum cluster algebra whose seed coincides with the Kashiwara--Kim--Oh--Park seed of $Δ^{m-2}$. Hence it is the quantum Grothendieck ring of a monoidal localization, at the frozen modules, of a subcategory of $\mathcal{C}(Δ^{m-2})$ with the same simple objects, and a quantization of the braid variety $X(Δ^{m-1})$. The whole algebra $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ is a skew Laurent extension of $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ in $(m-1)(n-1)$ frozen variables.
Explicit Error Term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for Function Fields

We prove an explicit error term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for finite generically Galois étale morphisms of affine varieties over finite fields, under a mild condition on their size. The error term generalises the known results for curves, and depends only on invariants of the varieties. We present several applications to the explicit error term. We apply it to existence problems, and to the Bateman-Horn conjecture over finite fields.
Particle separation in a time-correlated Gaussian velocity field: a numerical study

We numerically investigate the dispersion of passive tracer pairs in a two-dimensional, divergence-free, time-correlated Gaussian velocity field. The field is constructed from a sparse set of Fourier modes evolving as independent Ornstein--Uhlenbeck processes, with spatial regularity and scale-dependent temporal decorrelation comparable to those of a power-law Gaussian velocity ensemble. We show that, for spatial roughness exponent $α=0.2$ and temporal decorrelation exponent $β=0.5$, corresponding to the regime $α+β<1$, the extrapolated mean-square distance is compatible with particle separation (in mean-square) at positive time: two particles reach a mean-square positive distance at a finite time, no matter how close they are initially.
AI-Assisted Decision Support for Formula 1 Pit-Stop Strategy: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Programming

Pit-stop strategy in Formula 1 is a sequential decision problem under uncertainty, in which strategists decide at each lap whether to pit and which tire compound to fit. We develop a data-driven simulator, calibrated with historical race data, that captures tire degradation, drivers' recent performance, overtaking, yellow flag events, and rivals' pit-stop decisions. We train agents with five Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms and compare them with a Quadratic Mixed-Integer Programming (QMIP) formulation that is optimal in deterministic single-driver settings. Without uncertainty or competition, all DRL methods except TRPO achieve near-optimal performance. With a full grid of competitors and stochastic race events, the ranking of DRL methods depends on the evaluation setting: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and its recurrent variant are the only methods that improve on the QMIP both in fully simulated races and when the actual 2024 races are replayed. Averaged over eight circuits, PPO improves on the QMIP by 0.33 and 0.49 positions in the two settings and Recurrent PPO by less, and in the replay PPO finishes 0.66 positions ahead of the drivers' actual strategies simulated in the same races. The QMIP performs similarly to the other methods, even though it cannot anticipate yellow flag events. Finally, we use the trained PPO policy as a look-ahead decision-support tool that shows the strategist the distribution of race outcomes under each candidate pit-stop action. Applied retrospectively to eight 2024 races, the look-ahead identifies the laps where the actual decision, the recommendation, or a third action was preferable.
The Strong AJ Conjecture for Hyperbolic Prime Knots is False

Let $K$ be a knot in $S^3$. The strong AJ conjecture relates two of its invariants. The first is the minimal-order annihilator $\widehat A$ of the $n$th colored Jones polynomial $J(n)$. The second is the two-variable $A$-polynomial of Cooper, Culler, Gillet, Long, and Shalen. The conjecture says that after specialization $\varepsilon^*(\widehat A)\asymp A$. Zhang gave the first family of composite-knot counterexamples. For $8_{11}$ the specialization of $\widehat A$ carries an extra trefoil factor $L+M^6$. We prove this by verifying Lê's $\widehat P=\widehat A$ conjecture. Zhang's corrected formulation of the AJ conjecture agrees with Lê's weak AJ conjecture, which we prove for $8_{11}$. Li, Li, and Sun have since reported counterexamples of the weak AJ conjecture among non-hyperbolic prime knots. This work was AI assisted, and parts of it have been formalized in Lean.
Magnetic vector potentials and helicity in periodic domains

For a magnetic field in three-dimensional Euclidean space, we argue about the existence of a magnetic vector potential in a finite cuboid with periodic boundary conditions. We first argue in physical terms by representing periodic domains as tori and show that in some cases, the generating electric current is unphysical. We then represent magnetic fields and vector potentials as differential 2 and 1-forms. For a given magnetic field we ask the question whether a corresponding vector potential exists. Singly periodic domains are shown to always allow for a vector potential. For doubly periodic domains it only exists if the net magnetic flux through the non-periodic dimension vanishes, while for triply periodic domains the net flux must vanish in all directions. This has implications for the definition of magnetic helicity in periodic domains. We show that periodic domains together with a mean magnetic flux lead to contradicting results about the value of the magnetic helicity and we show in a few thought experiments fundamental contradictions to the interpretation as the linking of magnetic field lines. For the helicity we can even construct magnetic fields in periodic domains for which the magnetic helicity exists, but the calculations of the magnetic helicity do not lead to meaningful results due to the gauge freedom. With that we conclude that in presence of a mean magnetic field the calculated magnetic helicity cannot be interpreted geometrically in a straightforward way. However, using the winding gauge we can recover the geometric interpretation of the helicity as the flux averaged magnetic field line winding. Finally, for the solar relevant non-periodic domain with finite point-wise flux and zero integrated flux, using an appropriate gauge transformation the magnetic helicity can be shown to vanish. The winding helicity, however, would lead to a non-vanishing value here.
Steady Generalized Ricci Solitons with SO(3) Symmetries in Dimension Three

We completely classify all gradient, complete, steady generalized Ricci solitons in dimension three with $SO(3)$ symmetry, extending a result of Podestá-Raffero. We further extend this analysis to $n$-forms on $n$-manifolds with an $SO(n)$ symmetry.
On a potential type II singular model of the Navier Stokes equations

It is shown that a particular class of partial type I or type II functions are not singularity models for the three dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with or without smooth, compactly supported forces. This extends part of the results for the axially symmetric case to the full three dimension case. Some connections to the recent literature are also discussed.
On the cyclic and dihedral Ramsey numbers of separated caterpillars and nested matchings
Ivan Damnjanović; Daniil Furmanov; Jon A. Maccarello; Julien Menet

We consider all graphs to have vertex sets of the form $\{0, 1, 2, \ldots, n-1\}$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For graphs $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k$, the cyclic Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{cyc}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ is the smallest $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every $k$-edge-coloring of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H_j$ in color $j$ for some $j \in \{1, 2, \ldots, k\}$, with the vertices appearing in the same cyclic order as in $H_j$. The dihedral Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{dih}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ is defined analogously, with the difference that the direction of the cyclic order is ignored. For $n \ge 2$, a separated caterpillar of order $n$ is a graph obtained by a cyclic shift of the vertex labels from a tree of order $n$ whose edges can be written as $u_1 v_1, u_2 v_2, \ldots, u_{n-1} v_{n-1}$ so that $u_1 \leq u_2 \le \cdots \le u_{n-1} < v_{n-1} \le \cdots \le v_2 \le v_1$, while the trivial graph $K_1$ is the separated caterpillar of order one. For even $n \ge 2$, the nested matching of order $n$ is the $1$-regular graph in which each vertex $v$ is adjacent to $n - 1 - v$. We prove that if $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k$ are separated caterpillars, then $R_{\mathrm{cyc}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ and $R_{\mathrm{dih}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ are both equal to the Ramsey number of stars of the same orders, which was determined by Burr and Roberts. We also prove that $R_{\mathrm{cyc}}(F, H) = R_{\mathrm{dih}}(F, H) = 1 + (a-1)(b-1)$ for any graph $F$ of order $a \ge 2$ in which each vertex $v$ is adjacent to $(v + 1) \bmod a$ and any separated caterpillar $H$ of order $b \in \mathbb{N}$. Moreover, we determine the multicolor cyclic Ramsey numbers whose arguments are stars and nested matchings, provided that at most one of these nested matchings has order divisible by four. Some special cases of these results were recently obtained by Kucheriya, Petr and Yan.
Yau's first eigenvalue conjecture for embedded minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature

Let $M^n$ be a smooth closed connected embedded minimal hypersurface of the unit sphere. Suppose that $M$ has constant scalar curvature. We prove that its first positive Laplace eigenvalue is $n$ and that the ambient coordinate functions span its first eigenspace. To prove both assertions, we consider an eigenfunction $f$ with eigenvalue $0<λ\le n$ orthogonal to every coordinate function. We use $f$ as the density of a single-layer potential on the sphere. The geometry of $M$ gives a lower bound for the Dirichlet energy of this potential. The spherical heat kernel gives a smaller upper bound for the same energy. This contradiction rules out every such nonzero $f$.
Estimating conditional means under missingness-not-at-random with incomplete auxiliary variables
Maya B. Mathur; Shaun Seaman; Willi Zhang; Sean McGrath; Ilya Shpitser

Estimators assuming missingness at random (MAR) can fail under missingness not at random (MNAR). Introducing complete auxiliary variables sometimes restores MAR by breaking dependence between analysis variables and missingness. However, if the auxiliaries are themselves incomplete, MAR typically remains violated. We derive necessary and sufficient, weaker-than-MAR conditions under which the MAR functional $μ_{\rm MAR}$ for a conditional mean $E[Y \mid X]$ is correct. We also propose an alternative identifying functional for $E[Y \mid X]$, called $μ_{\rm MIA}$ for "Marginalization over Incomplete Auxiliaries", along with sufficient conditions for $μ_{\rm MIA}$ to be correct. For MNAR distributions in which all missingness patterns can occur and certain context-specific independences do not occur, there are two straightforward cases where $μ_{\rm MIA}$ is correct for a strict superset of the MNAR distributions for which $μ_{\rm MAR}$ is correct: (1) $X$ is complete and $Y$ is incomplete; or (2) all auxiliary variables are incomplete. In case (1), $μ_{\rm MAR}$ is always incorrect, barring knife-edge cases. Determining whether either case holds requires no knowledge of the MNAR mechanism. We propose estimators of $μ_{\rm MIA}$, including g-computation and doubly robust estimators. Our R package miapack implements a semiparametric iterated-conditional-expectations estimator. We illustrate with real data and present simulations comparing estimators of $μ_{\rm MIA}$ and $μ_{\rm MAR}$.
Structure of linear extensions of posets and lexicographic shelling

We study some structure of linear extensions of a finite poset $P$ by investigating partial orders on the maximal chains of the lattice of order ideals $J(P)$. These partial orders on the maximal chains of $J(P)$ are called maximal chain descent orders (MCDO). MCDOs come from EL-labelings of finite bounded posets and encode the structure of shellings arising from EL-labelings. Every linear extension of $P$ gives an EL-labeling of $J(P)$, and so generates an MCDO. Our main question is: when do different linear extensions of $P$ result in isomorphic MCDOs? We give partial answers to this question. In particular, we prove that linear extensions that are related by an automorphism of $P$ result in isomorphic MCDOs. Additionally, we show that for a certain family of posets, a linear extension $l$ and Schützenberger's evacuation of $l$ generate isomorphic MCDOs. In this case, the isomorphism comes from a well known isomorphism of the weak order on permutations.
Estimating contextual networks via Fisher-scoring surrogate likelihood

When networks are accompanied by vertex-level covariates, effectively integrating and aligning the information underlying both data sources becomes a natural yet critical task. Current spectral approaches, despite their popularity, may yield suboptimal results and necessitate the specification of additional tuning parameters that are contingent upon unobservable signal-to-noise ratios. We propose a tuning-free, likelihood-based learning framework for estimating latent positions in contextual generalized random dot product graphs in the presence of high-dimensional vertex covariates with a low-rank structure. Our method constructs a smooth surrogate likelihood and implements a Fisher-scoring algorithm to iteratively estimate latent positions without introducing additional tuning parameters that depend on the network sparsity. We establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the Fisher-scoring estimator. Application to real-world data further demonstrates the method's practical utility, offering a principled and scalable alternative to spectral approaches for analyzing contextual networks in high-dimensional settings.
For every prime $p\ge 29$, we construct an antipodal spherical $7$-design on $S^{p-1}$ with $42(p-1)(p+2)^2$ points. The construction uses eigenlines of finite Weil operators.
Finite propagation speed for evolutionary equations

We study finite speed of propagation in the framework of evolutionary equations introduced by Rainer Picard in 2009. We establish sufficient conditions on the material law, which is represented by an analytic and bounded operator-valued function, and the unbounded spatial operator that ensure finite speed of propagation of information for solutions. Assuming a linear-in-frequency coercivity bound for spatially local material laws, we prove propagation on backward light cones for weighted $L_2$ solutions without a finite initial time, thus identifying hyperbolic-type evolutionary equations. The characteristic-speed threshold depends on the coercive coefficient and the principal spatial matrices, but not on bounded memory or delay terms or potential positive fractional temporal contributions. We illustrate the result with the scalar wave equation, Maxwell's equations, a fractional model in elasticity, and dual-phase-lag thermoelasticity.
Inexact Proximal Method on Hadamard Manifolds
M. S. Louzeiro; R. Serra; S. Vieira

We propose and analyze two inexact proximal point methods for unconstrained geodesically convex optimization on Hadamard manifolds. The first, a standard inexact proximal point method (SIPPM), accepts approximate subproblem solutions directly as new iterates and applies to arbitrary Hadamard manifolds under a summability condition on the relative error tolerances. The second, a hybrid inexact proximal point method (IHPPM), augments each inexact proximal step with a metric projection onto a half-space-like separating set, allowing the summability requirement to be relaxed to a fixed relative error tolerance at the cost of assuming geodesic convexity of the separating sets. For both methods we establish full asymptotic convergence, global $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iteration-complexity bounds for approximate stationarity, and, under a local growth condition, local $Q$-linear convergence rates---with $Q$-superlinear acceleration for SIPPM when the proximal parameters tend to zero and a refined contraction factor for IHPPM. We further prove that the geodesic convexity of the separating sets holds automatically on Hadamard surfaces and on Hadamard manifolds of constant sectional curvature.
A dynamic variational principle on phase space for Wasserstein cubic splines

Wasserstein cubic splines have been introduced to provide a smooth interpolation in time between prescribed probability measures on $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Their construction for $N$ measures is based on a multi-marginal optimal transport problem on a space of dimension $N\! \cdot \! d$, thus becoming very high-dimensional already for a small number of prescribed measures. We prove that the dimension can be reduced to a fixed number $2d+1$ via a dynamic variational principle on phase space. We also give an example showing that the Monge ansatz, which would also reduce the dimension to a fixed number, fails to capture exact solutions and is in general ill-posed, even for absolutely continuous measures.
Analytic Projective Finsler Metrics and Sprays

We study projective Finsler metrics and sprays on an open subset $U$ of $R^n$. They are characterized by the Hamel equations \[ P_{x^m y^k}y^m=P_{x^k}, \] where $P=P(x, y)$ are function on $TU$ with positive homogeneity: $P(x, cy)= c (x,y)$, $c >0$. This is the Hilbert's Fourth problem in the regular case. We determine all solutions analytic in the base variable. We compare this local representation with earlier work on Hilbert's fourth problem and with the restricted Taylor expansions arising for projective Finsler metrics of constant flag curvature. We conclude with explicit nonlinear projective Finsler metrics and sprays on Euclidean space, including one-sided complete examples and a nonflat complete example.
Benjamin Luke; Sudip Shiwakoti; Shayan Nadeem; Ronald Morgan; Walter Wilcox

Estimating the trace of the inverse of a large quark matrix is a longstanding problem in lattice QCD. The standard approach is Hutchinson's method, which uses random noise vectors to estimate the trace to a desired statistical tolerance. Each noise vector $b$ requires solving a system of linear equations $Ax = b$. In this work, we introduce a new class of Krylov solvers for this task, called Twin methods. Twin methods generate the Krylov polynomial once then reuse it on all other right-hand sides. This reduces the number of basic linear algebra operations in the algorithm and therefore lowers the trace computation time. We apply the Twin approach to BiCG and BiCGStab and test them on lattice QCD matrices of varying size and in a range of computing contexts. We also present a more economical estimation of $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$ which implements a polynomial approximation of $A^{-1}$ and a singular value deflation. In this scheme, the solvers are applied to only a few noise vectors, and the remainder are treated by the polynomial and the deflation. In our tests, the polynomial approximation combined with the deflation yield a 17-fold speedup in the time required to compute the trace over standard Hutchinson's method.
Hypocoercivity estimates via maximum principle in short and long time scales

We prove decay estimates for a large class of linear drift-diffusion operators with hypoelliptic structure. In the main example, the diffusion consists of (possibly superposing) local or nonlocal operators acting on a restricted set of variables, while diffusivity is transported to the whole space thanks to Hörmander-type conditions on the drift term. We prove both short-time and long-time oscillation estimates on the solutions, including bounded-to-Lipschitz smoothing in the sharp time scale and exponential decay, as time goes to infinity, whenever a strict supersolution, with the role of Lyapunov function, is supposed to exist. The estimates are proved with a unifying approach relying on doubling variables and coupling methods, using maximum principle in suitably time scaled moving frames. Applications range from nonlocal kinetic Fokker-Planck equations to heat conduction models in a chain of coupled oscillators.
The double-endpoint Strichartz estimate for dispersion-managed Schrödinger equations
We adapt the near-far argument of Hadama and Toyoshima to establish the double-endpoint Strichartz estimate for dispersion-managed Schrödinger equations.
Large 4-tangles in matroids are characterized by large internally 4-connected minors
Nick Brettell; Johannes Carmesin; Tony Huynh; Matthew E. Kroeker; Florian Lehner; Geoff Whittle

Tangles were first introduced by Robertson and Seymour as an abstract way of treating highly connected substructures in graphs and matroids. For any truly highly connected substructure in a graph or matroid, all of the low-order separations in the object can be oriented towards it. This gives rise to a tangle. A standard question is whether every tangle of a given order in fact arises from some concrete highly connected substructure, such as a minor. It is well known that tangles of order two and three (in both graphs and matroids) are characterized by maximal $2$-connected and $3$-connected minors, respectively. For tangles of order four, it is necessary to consider a weaker notion of connectivity. Carmesin and Kurkofka showed that, for graphs, internal $4$-connectedness suffices. For matroids, Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple and Whittle showed that $4$-tangles arise from weakly $4$-connected minors, that is, minors in which every $3$-separation has a side with at most four elements. In the latter case, the breadth of the tangle (a measure of its complexity) can be preserved exactly, but the authors also asked whether a stronger notion of $4$-connectivity could be used while preserving some fraction of the breadth. In this paper, we answer this question in the affirmative by showing that, in a matroid, any $4$-tangle of sufficiently large breadth is determined by an internally $4$-connected minor whose unique $4$-tangle also has large breadth.
Polynomial sequences of Simplex pivots on 0/1-polytopes

We study the number of Simplex pivots needed to solve linear programs over $0/1$-polytopes, starting from an arbitrary feasible basis and counting degenerate pivots. It has been known since the 1990s that from any extreme point of a 0/1-polytope there exists a monotone path of linear length to an optimal one. However, translating this into a polynomial sequence of Simplex pivots, i.e., improving basis exchanges, has remained an open question. We here provide an affirmative answer, showing that for every 0/1-polytope $\mathcal P \subseteq \mathbb R^d$, an optimal basis can be reached with $O(d^3)$ Simplex pivots, independently of the number of inequalities and of the size of the coefficients.
A Column-Generation Approach to Length-Constrained Shortest Paths under Cascading Causal Failures
Nicolò Aicardi; Zuyuan Zhang; Sridhar Radhakrishnan; Kash Barker; Dritan Nace

In the study of cascading causal node failures, the failure of one set of nodes can trigger the failure of another, possibly non-adjacent, set, and these triggers can propagate in cascades. Given a graph, a set of causal failures, a source-terminal pair, and a constant $α\geq 1$, we study the length-constrained shortest-path problem of finding the maximum subset of causalities whose application preserves a source-terminal path of length at most $α$ times the original distance. We show that the problem is NP-hard, a hardness that reflects the non-local, cascading nature of causal failures. We propose a mixed-integer linear programming formulation with explicit node-integrity variables that decouple the node state from routing, a column-generation algorithm built on a path-based reformulation whose pricing subproblem is solved by a three-level cascade (beam search, label-capped $A^*$, and exact $A^*$ with warm start), and a greedy heuristic as a fast baseline. On the IEEE 300 and Power 5000 benchmarks, all three methods are competitive. In dense synthetic networks of 10,000 to 15,000 nodes, the exact model exhausts its time budget or returns an order of magnitude fewer causalities, whereas column generation remains fast and accurate, emerging as the method of choice for large instances.
Recovering from Averages: An Inverse Problem Perspective on Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
Tina Torabi; Cheuk Hin Ho; Christoph Ortner; Ruo Ning Qiu

Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate the potential energy surface of atomistic systems from quantum-mechanical reference data and enable molecular simulation at near-ab-initio accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Since they are fitted to total energies and forces, it is not obvious what is estimated: the total energy or the many-body potentials from which it is assembled. Mathematically, this can be formulated as a question whether a function can be recovered from averages of its values over random clusters. We study it for a linear model of fixed correlation order in simplified statistical setting. We show that, in the population limit, the potential is identifiable in a natural weighted Sobolev space, and derive finite-sample recovery guarantees. Numerical experiments for pair, three-body, and four-body models support the theory.
Persistent Bass and Lyubeznik Numbers of Stanley Reisner Rings
Kaiyue He; Faisal Suwayyid; Guo-Wei Wei

We define persistent Lyubeznik numbers and persistent Bass numbers of Stanley--Reisner rings along a simplicial filtration. For Lyubeznik numbers we show that the complex of Àlvarez Montaner and Vahidi computing $λ_{p,q}(\kk[Δ])$ is natural for inclusions of simplicial complexes, so that persistent Lyubeznik numbers are ranks of maps on its cohomology. We give an equivalent costar complex, whose terms are reduced homology groups of links of faces and whose differentials are induced by quotient maps; it requires neither Alexander duals nor free resolutions. For Bass numbers at coordinate primes we prove that the Hochster-type formula is natural for inclusions, which identifies the persistent Bass numbers with the persistent graded Betti numbers of Suwayyid and Wei for filtered links. Both families have finite barcodes and satisfy bottleneck stability. Examples, including two isomers with the same persistent homology, exhibit Lyubeznik bars that persistent homology does not detect.
Studies on a Relationship Between Tate Homology and Local Cohomology of Tensor Products of Modules
Mohsen Asgharzadeh; Olgur Celikbas; Arash Sadeghi

We study the local cohomology of finitely generated modules with respect to specialization-closed subsets over commutative Noetherian rings. Our main result establishes a relationship between the local cohomology of tensor products of modules and Tate homology over Gorenstein rings. We present several consequences of our main result, which are of independent interest. For example, we study various aspects of the cohomological rigidity property of tensor products of modules and generalize results of Huneke-Wiegand in this direction. We determine conditions under which the vanishing of a single local cohomology module of a tensor product implies the vanishing of all lower ones, establish bounds for the depth of tensor products of modules, and obtain criteria for freeness of modules over complete intersection rings. Along the way, we also provide a splitting criterion for vector bundles on smooth complete intersections.
Victor Hugo Pereira Rodrigues; Tiago Roux Oliveira; Miroslav Krstic

This paper introduces an event-triggered source seeking control (ET-SSC) strategy for autonomous vehicles modeled as nonholonomic unicycles. The key feature of the proposed design is the separation between the continuous probing motion required for gradient extraction and the event-triggered update of the source-seeking correction. This separation enables aperiodic computation and transmission of the correction while the periodic probing signals remain continuously active. The triggering mechanism acts on a low-pass-filtered gradient estimate, obtained by high-pass (washout) filtering, demodulation, and low-pass filtering of the measured signal, and combines a relative and an absolute threshold. Stability is proved with a time-periodic Lyapunov function constructed along the exponentially stable periodic solution of the filtered closed loop, establishing practical exponential convergence of the vehicle to a neighborhood of the unknown source. The guaranteed minimum dwell time is strictly positive and independent of the probing frequency, which excludes Zeno behavior. Unlike available Lie-bracket analyses of the forward-velocity design, the proposed averaging-based analysis accommodates anisotropic quadratic source fields with distinct spatial curvatures. The resulting ET-SSC framework therefore provides a resource-aware implementation in which the source-seeking correction is updated aperiodically while the information-generating probing motion remains continuous.
Incentive Compatible Mechanisms for Sequential Fair Resource Allocation with Private Demands
Ramtin Salamat; Sean R. Sinclair; Seyed M. R. Iravani

We study a strategic variant of the canonical online fair allocation problem, where a planner must sequentially allocate a divisible resource to agents with privately known demands. At each stage, the planner announces an allocation rule, the agent reports their demand, and the planner allocates resources according to the rule and the reported demand. Unlike the standard model, we allow agents to strategically misreport their needs, as can arise in nonprofit settings where demand is self-reported and monetary transfers are unavailable. We characterize the structure of incentive-compatible (IC) allocation rules in this model, and use this to identify conditions under which the optimal mechanism has a simple cap structure. We then develop an approximation method for the optimal IC mechanism through a careful reduction of the discretized dynamic program to a longest-path problem on a directed acyclic graph. Numerical experiments show that ignoring strategic reporting can be substantially more costly than imposing incentive compatibility.
Thurston measure is stationary with exponential Teichmüller moment

In 1967, Furstenberg proved that every lattice in a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center admits a probability measure whose stationary measure on the associated Furstenberg boundary belongs to the Lebesgue measure class. We prove an analogue of this theorem for the action of the mapping class group on Teichmüller space. Every regular probability measure in the Thurston measure class on the space of projective measured foliations is the stationary measure of a non-elementary random walk with a finite exponential moment in the Teichmüller metric.
A boundary integral equation solver for capsule suspensions
Joar Bagge; Ziyu Du; George Biros

Deformable capsules serve as models for biological cells, such as red blood cells, as well as for synthetic capsules in biomedical and industrial applications. In this work, we introduce a framework for fast and robust simulation of deformable capsules in three-dimensional Stokes flow, both in unbounded domains and in pipe-confined geometries. We solve the Stokes equations using a boundary integral formulation, employing a partition-of-unity discretization for the capsule membrane and the trapezoidal rule with regularization to handle the singular quadrature. Dense periodic interactions are evaluated via a fast Ewald summation scheme, achieving $O(N \log N)$ complexity for $N$ grid points. The interfacial forces on the capsule membrane are modeled using the Skalak constitutive law. We carry out a spectral analysis of this model for small perturbations of a spherical capsule, which indicates that the relaxation dynamics are intrinsically stable. However, the nonlinear character of the Skalak model induces aliasing errors that can compromise numerical stability. To address this when needed, we perform de-aliasing through upsampling and spectral filtering, and we derive guidelines for choosing appropriate filter parameters, thereby stabilizing the method. We investigate the stability and convergence behavior of the resulting scheme and conduct simulations of long-time dynamics, focusing on the relaxation of unconfined capsules and the lateral migration of pipe-confined capsules under various flow conditions.
A functional Breuer-Major theorem under finite variance, with application to the $R/S$ test for long memory

The Breuer-Major theorem (Breuer and Major, 1983) states that, for a function $G$ of Hermite rank $m$ such that $\mathbb{E}(G^{2}(X))<\infty$, and a stationary Gaussian sequence whose correlation function $r$ satisfies $\sum_{i}|r(i)|^{m}<\infty$, the finite dimensional distributions of the normalized partial sum process of $G(X_{i})$ converge to those of a Brownian motion. Whether the functional version of this result holds under these sole conditions has remained open for a long time, the tightness being known only under additional moment assumptions. In this paper we prove that the functional central limit theorem holds under finite variance only. More generally, we give a high order expansion of the partial sum process which covers both short and long-range dependence: the long-range dependent components converge to Hermite processes, while the remainder converges to a Brownian motion. As an application, we discuss the question of testing long-memory in observed data using the $R/S$ statistics. We derive the limiting distributions of the classical and modified $R/S$ statistics, prove the consistency of the test and propose a data-driven choice of the truncation parameter. A Monte Carlo study compares the performances of the classical and modified $R/S$ statistics for both short-memory and long-memory sequences.
The 1-Loop and Ohtsuki-Takata Invariants for Alternating Braids

In a step towards resolving the 1-loop conjecture, Ohtsuki and Takata defined their own eponymous invariant in terms of an open knot diagram, and showed that it is equal to the adjoint Reidemeister torsion for two-bridge knots. Garoufalidis and Yoon then showed that the 1-loop invariant is equal to the Ohtsuki-Takata invariant using a technique involving a collapsed octahedral decomposition. This paper expands those techniques to relate the matrix determinants of the 1-loop and Ohtsuki-Takata invariants for the case of reduced alternating braids.
Opposite filtrations on the parabolic compactified Jacobian

We show that the Hikita filtration on the cohomology of the parabolic compactified Jacobian of the plane curve singularity $x^m=y^n$, $(m,n)=1$, is opposite to the perverse filtration in a precise sense. This implies the parabolic Hilb-vs-Quot conjecture from https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19633, and consequently the main conjecture from https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2115 for these singularities. The new ingredient is an analysis of how the Bott-Mitchell filtration on the homology of the affine Grassmannian of $SL_n$ relates to both of the above filtrations.
Compression with wildcards: The maximum anticliques of König-Egarváry graphs

By definition a König-Egarváry graph is such that the cardinality of each maximum matching equals the cardinality of each minimum vertex-cover. Each bipartite graph has this property. We unravel the structure of the family MACL(G) of all maximum anticliques (independent sets) of a König-Egarváry graph G. This enables us to enumerate $MACL(G)$ not only in output polynomial time, but also in a compressed format (using wildcards). All of this can be viewed as an instance where ALL minimum solutions of a submodular function can be enumerated efficiently.

We study isolation in the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$. When $p=o(1)$ and $np\to\infty$, allowing an $F$-free graph on the undominated vertices gives the same first-order asymptotics for every fixed forest $F$ as the domination number $γ(G)$ in $G(n,p)$. For the ordinary isolation number $ι(G)$ ($F$ is an edge) we prove two-point concentration when $p$ is bounded away from $1$ and $np^2/(\log n)^3\to\infty$. We also identify a transition in the gap $γ(G)-ι(G)$ when $\log(1/p)=o(\log n)$. This gap tends to infinity in probability when $p$ is well below $(\log\log n/\log n)^2$ and is at most one with high probability when $p$ is well above this scale. Finally, for every fixed graph $F$, we show that the classical minimum degree bound for domination is asymptotically sharp for $F$-isolation, even for regular host graphs.
Source Conditions and Sharp Transition Asymptotics for the Factorization Method with Far-Field Data

The factorization method characterizes an obstacle through a range test, but practical implementations replace the associated Picard series by a regularized approximation. This paper studies the resulting regularization bias for inverse acoustic scattering by impedance obstacles. For a disc, we show that every positive-order Hölder source condition fails at each noncentral interior sampling point, whereas logarithmic source conditions hold uniformly on compact interior subsets for every exponent, with explicit constants. At the center, the bias decays linearly with the regularization parameter. We then derive sharp spectral transition asymptotics through the Lambert W function. These asymptotics determine the stabilization rate inside the obstacle, the iterated-logarithmic growth at the boundary, and the divergence outside. They also yield a threshold rule for which the reconstructed disc converges in measure, together with quantitative boundary-location estimates. For general impedance obstacles, we reduce the spectral decay of the symmetrized far-field operator to that of the data-to-pattern operator and obtain two-sided transition bounds in terms of the inradius and any radius larger than the circumradius. For a simply connected obstacle with analytic boundary, positive analytic impedance, and conformal center inside the obstacle, a Faber--Vekua normal form gives the sharp spectral law in terms of logarithmic capacity, with the same leading constant as for the disc. This class includes every convex analytic obstacle. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted spectral transition and illustrate its use in choosing the regularization level. The analytic normal-form result is proved only for a single boundary component.
Finite-Time Singularity Formation for the Three-Dimensional Euler Equations
Levent Alpöge; Tristan Buckmaster; Matei P. Coiculescu

We construct smooth periodic initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations whose solution blows up in finite time. The velocity remains bounded, while the vorticity magnitude at the origin tends to infinity. Away from the origin, the velocity and its time derivative have smooth spatial limits at the singular time. The construction uses localized Craik--Criminale waves as building blocks of a multi-scale construction.
A rigorous Abel-summed Hardy-type identity for $p$-circle domains via regularized Poisson summation

In our previous work, a generalized Hardy-type identity (GHI) for astroid-type $p$-circle domains was formally derived in terms of generalized $p$-Bessel functions. However, the direct application of the Poisson summation formula to the indicator functions of these domains leaves the convergence and rigorous justification of the resulting oscillatory series unresolved. In the present paper, we address this difficulty by introducing an anisotropic regularization based on convolution kernels with Fourier multipliers $e^{-t(|ξ_{1}|^p+|ξ_{2}|^{p})}$. We establish the corresponding regularized Poisson summation identity and rigorously justify the limiting process through uniform estimates for lattice-point sums. A key feature of our analysis is the determination of boundary contributions: smooth boundary points carry weight $1/2$, whereas the contributions from axial cusps vanish for $0<p<1$. These results lead to an Abel-summed GHI, expressed in terms of the distorted-angle-dependent $p$-Bessel functions introduced in our previous work, with explicit boundary corrections. In particular, for $p=2$, the identity recovers the Abel-summed form of the classical Hardy--Voronoï Bessel series. Our result provides a rigorous regularized counterpart of the previously proposed identity, while the convergence of the corresponding unregularized series remains a separate problem.
Avoiding squares over words with lists of size three

We prove that every sequence of lists of size three admits an infinite square-free word, establishing that the Thue choice number of the path is three. More precisely, the number of compatible square-free words of length $n$ is at least $c(5/4)^n$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. The proof combines a computer-assisted construction of weights with the weighted counting method previously introduced by the author. We first consider words avoiding only squares of bounded period and use a finite state model to certify a uniform lower bound on their growth. The counting argument then controls the loss caused by excluding longer squares. The main new ingredient is a coarser description of the states, which makes the computation feasible without restricting the union of the lists. The same computation yields a deterministic polynomial-time strategy for constructing an infinite square-free word when each list is chosen adversarially after the preceding letters have been fixed.
An Optimal Liouville Theorem for the Fully Fractional Heat Equation
Yahong Guo; Yugao Ouyang; Jiongduo Xie

We prove that every nonnegative entire classical solution of the fully fractional heat equation $(\partial_t-Δ)^s u=u^p$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ is identically zero for $n\geq2$, $0<s<1$, and $1<p<(n+2s)/(n-2s)$. No global boundedness, decay, or symmetry assumptions are required for the solutions. The exponent range is sharp, since the critical equation admits positive stationary solutions. Our result provides a fractional counterpart of Quittner's optimal Liouville theorem for the classical semilinear heat equation, while our proof follows a new and simpler approach. For bounded solutions, we combine elliptic nonexistence and compactness to control superlevel set measures by the local energy dissipation of the weighted extension. A local energy inequality then gives nonexistence by iteration. Doubling, local regularity, and a nonlocal convergence theorem yield a universal pointwise bound in terms of the parabolic distance to the boundary, which implies our Liouville theorem for general solutions.
A reciprocal-matrix proof of Sendov's theorem and applications to control theory

This proof grew out of the author's research on interpreting mathematical statements from the viewpoint of control theory. Its value lies both in the understanding it brings and in the applications that arise from the argument. Let $a$ be a simple zero of a polynomial of degree $n\ge 2$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. If $c_1,\ldots,c_{n-1}$ are its critical points, counted with multiplicity, then the reciprocals $1/(a-c_j)$ are the eigenvalues of an explicit matrix built from the other zeros. A failure of Sendov's bound at $a$ would therefore make the associated discrete-time system asymptotically stable. This observation leads to an alternative proof of the quadratic inequality of Tang and Zhang, including its equality case. Building on the reflection and centering arguments of Mazur, Tao and Zhang, we estimate the change in the integral of the derivative product when all the reciprocal displacements are replaced by their mean $s$. An exact pairwise cancellation bounds the difference in terms of the variance. For an interior zero rotated to $0<a<1$, the normalized trace $s$ determines a contour through $\overline{s}/a$. If the mean squared reciprocal distance is at most one, integration along this contour gives $(n-1)(2a\Re(s)-a^2)<20$. A uniform phase estimate and reflection at $1/a$ then rule out this possibility in every degree $n\ge 257$. A fourth-moment estimate treats degrees two through five. For degrees five through 256, three bounds derived from one polynomial moment identity exclude the full range of the two remaining real parameters by exact integer arithmetic. As an application, Sendov's theorem illustrates how differentiating the denominator of a closed-loop transfer function can increase robustness in discrete-time systems and decrease it in continuous-time systems. The proofs have been formalized in Lean 4.
Pathwise Factorization and Uncertainty Quantification for Impedance Obstacles with Random Boundaries

We develop a factorization method with finite-sample statistical guarantees for two-dimensional acoustic scattering by impedance obstacles whose boundary is random and whose data are finitely many noisy multistatic measurements. In the two-dimensional far-field normalization, the symmetrization must act on a phase-rotated far-field operator; we prove the optical and range identities for every realization of a compact family of uniformly bi-Lipschitz domains, with jointly measurable regularized indicators. A quadrature-weighted finite-sample analysis separates angular approximation, measurement noise, test-vector error, and regularization, and yields a consistency theorem for empirical means and variances, joint in all data parameters. Bounded indicators admit simultaneous confidence bands, a diagonal threshold recovers the probability that a sampling point lies in the random obstacle, and a nested design yields unbiased variance components. Computations use a combined-field integral equation proved invertible at all frequencies, and the finite-grid guarantees are examined in a coverage study against a high-accuracy Monte Carlo reference.
The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups

In this work, we prove the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general (quasi-split) unramified $G$. The strategy is to adapt the proof of Chaudouard--Laumon from the split case. In particular, we define the notion of a $ξ$-stable Higgs bundle for a quasi-split reductive group scheme $G$ on a curve, and prove that the stack of such form a proper, finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over the Hitchin base when $G$ has anisotropic center. We then adapt the global cohomological theorem of Chaudouard--Laumon to the quasi-split setting, and perform the required Frobenius-point count to obtain an identity of adelic orbital integrals. A local-to-global argument deduces the WFL for Lie algebras. In the last chapter, we perform a parallel reduction to deduce Waldspurger's nonstandard WFL from a global version which follows from the same geometric theory. Our work implies the Twisted Weighted Fundamental Lemma in good characteristic, which completes Moeglin--Waldspurger's stabilization of the twisted Arthur--Selberg trace formula. We therefore render unconditional the endoscopic classification for classical groups and an array of downstream consequences in automorphic theory.

The anti-Ramsey number was introduced by Erdős, Simonovits, and Sós and is defined to be the maximum number of colors that can be used to color the edges of a graph to avoid a rainbow copy of some graph. One can generalize this by, instead of forbidding a rainbow copy of a graph, putting a cap on the number of colors that appear on any copy of that graph. To be precise, let $\AR(G,H,q)$ be the maximum number of colors that can be used to color $E(G)$ so that every copy of $H$ sees at most $q$ colors. One can see that $\AR(G,H,q)$ is nondecreasing in $q$. In this paper, we investigate the linear and quadratic thresholds of $\AR(G,H,q)$ when $G=K_n$ and $H$ is connected.
Cohomology of twisted tensor products over commutative rings

Over a commutative ground ring, cohomology of a twisted tensor product of two rings mixes their cohomology via the twisting. We focus on bicharacter twistings and give explicit descriptions when the ground ring is itself a module. We state our main results for ground rings that are hereditary and contain roots of unity corresponding to finite grading groups. As a class of examples, we compute cohomology rings of Taft orders over cyclotomic integers.
DNN-Assisted Deterministic Policy Learning for Adaptive IRS-NOMA-OWC Networks
Ahrar N. Hamad; Ahmad A. Qidan; Taisir E. H. El-Gorashi; Jaafar M. H. Elmirghani

Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has been considered a promising technology in optical wireless communication (OWC) networks due to its potential to overcome the line-of-sight (LoS) blockage issue and enhance coverage. In this paper, a dynamic IRS-assisted indoor non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-OWC network is modeled, and an optimization problem is formulated to maximize the sum rate subject to the quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of multiple mobile users, by jointly optimizing the power allocation and the IRS mirror orientations, from which the user's decoding order is induced rather than being fixed. Since the problem is non-convex and the channel conditions vary with user mobility, conventional optimization methods may incur considerable computational overhead. Therefore, a two-stage deep neural network-deep reinforcement learning (DNN-DRL) framework is proposed. In the first stage, the DNN estimates the user's positions and orientations in real time, removing the need for perfect knowledge of the user state. In the second stage, a deterministic policy gradient (DPG)-based DRL algorithm uses these estimates to jointly optimize the power allocation and IRS mirror orientations, with the decoding order updated according to the resulting effective channel gains. The results show that the proposed framework approaches the performance upper bounds and outperforms standard DRL algorithms, conventional optimization methods, and deployments without IRS in terms of sum rate and fairness, while achieving faster convergence. Furthermore, online adaptation of the decoding order maintains higher QoS satisfaction than a fixed decoding order, particularly under high user mobility.
Square-root cancellation in three hyperbolic counting problems via maximal estimates

We study three counting problems for lattice orbits in hyperbolic space: counting orbit points within a prescribed distance of a fixed closed geodesic or a totally geodesic hyperplane, and counting orbit points above a prescribed height at a cusp. For almost every base point, we obtain error bounds of square-root size up to logarithmic factors. For the geodesic and hyperplane counts, these bounds match the conjectured exponents and improve earlier results due to Good and Laaksonen. For these two problems, we adapt the method of maximal estimates developed by Chatzakos and Dimakis for hyperbolic lattice counting, formulating it in both a discrete and a continuous framework. For the hyperplane problem, we also obtain an asymptotic formula for the spatial second moment of the error term, involving an almost periodic function. For the cusp problem, the square-root bound can be deduced from work of Yu, which incorporates Schmidt's dyadic maximal argument. We present a proof, together with an $Ω$-result supporting the optimality of the exponent $1/2$ for at least one cusp of any group that is not essentially cuspidal. In contrast, for the modular group, we obtain a power saving over the exponent $1/2$ for every base point.
Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix

If the Hamiltonian of a large quantum system depends on a variable parameter, its parameter-dependent energy spectrum may often form a dense lattice of avoided crossings. If the parameter slowly changes, the system's time evolution through the avoided crossings tends in the semi-classical limit to change from adiabatic to diabatic across a narrow energy range that has recently been defined as a quantum separatrix. Here we show that in the extreme semi-classical limit of a quasi-continuously dense spectrum, all quantum separatrices form a universal one-parameter family, and that evolution through the separatrix becomes efficiently ergodizing. If the unitary evolution is realistically averaged over small variations in the parameter time dependence, quantum separatrix crossing generates diagonal entropy according to a universal formula. Numerical examples confirm that the results for quasi-continuous spectra remain clearly recognizable in finite systems, with only small finite-size effects.
Connected Cayley Approximation of Power Graphs of Finite Groups

For a nontrivial finite group \(G\), we define its connected intersection density as the maximum, over all connected Cayley graphs on \(G\), of the proportion of edges that also belong to the undirected power graph of \(G\). We show that this density is \(1\) if and only if \(G\) is cyclic, and that it is \(1/4\), \(1/6\), and \(1/12\) for \(A_4\), \(S_4\), and \(A_5\), respectively. For the dihedral group of order \(2n\), with \(n\geq 3\), we give a general formula and show that the connected intersection density equals \((\binom{n}{2}+1)/n^2\) if and only if \(n\) is a prime power. We also give a formula for the connected intersection density of dicyclic groups. For generalized quaternion groups of order \(2N\), where \(N=2^{m-1}\geq 4\), the density is \(\frac{N^2+8}{2N(N+1)}\). For the elementary abelian group \(C_p^r\), where \(p\) is prime and \(r\geq 1\), the density is \(p^{1-r}\).
The regular $N$-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most $N$ sides and fixed area

Let $Φ(P)=|P|μ_1(P)$, where $μ_1(P)$ is the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of $P$. For every $N\ge3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes $Φ$, up to congruence, among simple polygons of fixed area with at most $N$ sides. The values $Φ(R_N)$ increase strictly with $N$. The maximization theorem answers Laugesen's question \cite[Problem~(1), p.~405]{ABLW} and proves the polygonal Szegő--Weinberger conjecture of Laugesen and Siudeja \cite[Conjecture~6.36]{LSH}. It also implies that the triangular lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of the Voronoi cell at fixed covolume.
Dynabase: A Database of Extreme Examples in Arithmetic Dynamics

We introduce Dynabase, a database cataloging extreme examples in arithmetic dynamics related to several major open conjectures: the Morton--Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture and the dynamical analogue of Lang's conjecture on canonical heights, as well as data on postcritically finite maps and maps with nontrivial automorphisms. This database collects the known examples of extreme behavior for these problems and tracks the current status of subproblems based on degree and field of definition.
Optimal Polynomial Approximants vanishing arbitrarily close to the origin
Athanasios Beslikas; Christopher Felder; Douglas T. Pfeffer

This work concerns a sequence of stable polynomials on the bidisk whose affine optimal polynomial approximants in the Hardy space of the bidisk have zero varieties that come arbitrarily close to the origin.

The dual Littlestone dimension of a concept class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}):=\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H}^*)$, is the Littlestone dimension of the dual class $\mathcal{H}^*$, obtained by exchanging the roles of domain points and hypotheses. A classical result of Shelah implies that $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})$ and $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})$ are finite simultaneously, and quantitative results of Hodges [Mathematika, 1981] imply the doubly exponential bound $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}}$. Malliaris and Moran [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2024] asked whether this bound is optimal. We answer this by proving the improved bound \[ \operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})^2)}. \] An exponential dependence is necessary, as witnessed by the class of all binary hypotheses on a finite domain.

Explicit positive multisums on base q^5 for the Rogers-Ramanujan sum function and its partial sum are given. 32 combinatorial interpretations for these identities are given. The classical mod 5 Rogers-Ramanujan identities are recovered as a limiting case. These results are equivalent to a quintic basic hypergeometric identity.
Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices

We prove that every cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose window is a line segment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice: if $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ is a plane which is not spanned by vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, and $σ$ is a segment of any length which is transverse to $V$, then the set of points $v\in V$ with $v+x\inσ+\mathbb{Z}^3$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}^2$. For planes of Diophantine slope this is a theorem of Burago and Kleiner, and the point of the present paper is that no Diophantine condition on the plane is needed. We also show that the same conclusion holds when the window is a finite union of intervals. Together with the author's construction of a cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window of countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to any lattice, this shows that for planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ the answer to the bi-Lipschitz question depends on the shape of the window rather than on the Diophantine properties of the plane.
Large deviations, effective dynamics, and dynamical phase transitions in random maps
Ángela Tajuelo-Valbuena; Jorge Hidalgo; Ricardo Gutiérrez; Carlos Pérez-Espigares

Large deviation theory provides a natural framework to characterize rare fluctuations of time-averaged observables in deterministic and stochastic systems. Building on previous results for deterministic chaotic maps, here we extend the Doob transform to random maps, constructing an effective dynamics in which rare events become typical. This makes it possible to directly reproduce the dynamics of rare trajectories that are exponentially difficult to sample under the original dynamics. We further apply spectral large-deviation methods to characterize dynamical phase transitions in random maps. The spectral structure of the tilted operator provides insight into the mechanisms underlying these transitions and, in particular, allows us to identify the appropriate initial states that select one dynamical phase or another. Our results extend the connection between large deviation theory, spectral methods, and effective dynamics to random chaotic maps, providing a general framework to study rare events and dynamical phase transitions in these systems.

Arinkin's sheaf gives a relative Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence of a general Beauville-Mukai system, extending the usual Poincaré bundle over the smooth locus. We provide an alternative construction of it as a deformation of the Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence on the Hilbert scheme of an elliptic K3 surface obtained by lifting the classical Poincaré kernel for an elliptic surface. As applications, we show that the $P=C$ property for a general Beauville-Mukai system is equivalent to that for the Hilbert scheme fibration, thus providing new proofs for both. We also construct an explicit deformation that connects Markman's construction of a projectively hyperholomorphic bundle on products of hyper-Kähler manifolds of K3${}^{[g]}$-type to that of Hartlieb and Shah. This answers a question of Hartlieb and Shah.
Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
Emiel Claasen; Mehregan Doroudiani; Claude Duhr; Axel Kleinschmidt; Franca Lippert; Oliver Schlotterer; Yoann Sohnle

We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.
A posteriori estimates for inverse evolutionary problems

The paper is focused on a posteriori error analysis of evolutionary problems, which are ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. They may have no solutions and respective approximations may be highly unstable. For these problems, the a posteriori error estimation concept applicable to well-posed problems is not valid and requires a significant reformulation. A posteriori estimates of the functional type provide the basis for addressing this issue. They generate computable quantities that estimate the distance between a function (approximate solution to the inverse problem) and exact solution of a "close" well-posed initial boundary value problem associated with the same differential equation. The solution of this close problem exactly satisfies one part of the imposed conditions and the others are satisfied approximately with the accuracy $\eps$. This idea is elaborated for several evolutionary problems generated by the reaction-convection-diffusion equation: backward parabolic problem, problem with non-local time conditions, Cauchy parabolic problem, and parameter(s) identification problem. The estimates derived not only control the accuracy of approximate solutions, but also suggest a unified approach to calculating them numerically.
Uniformising random greedy maximal independent sets on graphs with at most five vertices

A random greedy algorithm scans the vertices of a finite graph in increasing order of independent exponential arrival times and accepts each vertex unless an accepted neighbour blocks it. We ask an inverse question: can strictly positive finite arrival rates be chosen so that the terminal inclusion-maximal independent sets are all equally likely? We call this exact property exponential greedy uniformisability (EGU). We establish the complete small-order classification: every finite simple graph on at most five vertices is EGU, with the unique exception of the five-vertex path $P_5$ up to graph isomorphism. A strict $2\times2$ probability minor provides an explicit obstruction for the exceptional graph; the positive cases are certified by graph-isomorphism reduction and exact constructive witnesses. We explain the independent-exponential-clock probability law and the formal Lean 4 verification, registered as Palomar PALOMAR-2026-11-19-000021 (version 1). The registration is a formal proof record, not a claim of novelty certification or journal peer review.
Error analysis for the numerical approximation of the quantile hedging problem
Cyril Bénézet; Cyril Nefzaoui-Blanchard; Sergio Pulido

We analyse numerical approximations of quantile hedging in complete linear markets with Markovian diffusion dynamics. The problem is formulated as stochastic control for an augmented state $(X,P)$, where the probability martingale $P$ is constrained to $[0,1]$ and controlled through an unbounded volatility coefficient. We combine control truncation with piecewise-constant policy time-stepping (PCPT), stopping controls continuously upon boundary hitting to preserve the state constraint. Using one-step dynamic programming principles and regularisation, we derive a generator inequality and explicit value-function error bounds. Under standard coefficient regularity and a Lipschitz payoff, optimising the truncation and regularisation parameters yields an error exponent arbitrarily close to $1/8$ from below, uniformly in the probability variable. For controls bounded from the outset, we obtain exponents arbitrarily close to $1/4$ from below, approaching the exponent established by Jakobsen, Picarelli and Reisinger without state constraints. We also implement a fully discrete scheme with neural-network controls. Grid-time projection onto $[0,1]$ introduces a martingale defect and a pricing bias. We quantify this bias in a toy problem and mitigate it using a state-dependent control bound. Experiments in Black--Scholes and Lipschitz local-volatility models illustrate the correction and the decrease in pricing errors under grid refinement.
On the number of edge-disjoint $K_r$ in $K_{r+1}$-free graphs

Gy\H ori and Keszegh [\emph{Combinatorica} \textbf{37} (2017), 1113--1124] proved that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint triangles. We extend this result to cliques of arbitrary fixed order. Specifically, we prove that for every fixed integer $r\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $K_{r+1}$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint copies of $K_r$, where $t_{r-1}(n)$ denotes the number of edges in the Turán graph $T_{r-1}(n)$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $G$ is obtained from $T_{r-1}(n)$ by adding edges within one of its parts, with the added edges forming a triangle-free graph.
Eigenvalues and Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator in the Large-Friction Limit

We study the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator by the methods of analytic dilation and phase-space deformation. We prove that in the large-friction limit $γ\to+\infty$, there are neither eigenvalues nor resonances away from the thresholds $γN$, and that near each threshold $γk$, there exists a bijection between the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and those of the Witten Laplacian at the level $k$, $-Δ_V^{(k)}=-Δ_V\otimes 1_{μ_k}-dΓ_k(\operatorname{Hess}V)$. We also show that each negative eigenvalue of $-Δ_V^{(k)}$, $k\geq 1$, produces a pole of the resolvent at distance of order $γ^{-1}$ below $γk$, whose imaginary part is $O(e^{-cγ})$ for every $c<2δ_V$. Here $δ_V$ is the width of a strip of analyticity of $V$.
Möbius expansion and pointwise energy transfer over arbitrary fields

Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, and let $A\subset F^\times$ have $N$ elements. We prove that, for every $λ\in F^\times$, \[ \card{A+λA^{-1}}\gg\min\{N^{10/9},(pN^2)^{1/3}\}. \] This improves the exponent $31/30$ to $10/9$ in the common small-set range. Over prime fields the bound strengthens to $\min\{N^{10/9},(pN)^{1/2}\}$. Analogous bounds hold for $Af(A)$ when $f$ is a Möbius transformation satisfying the stated nondegeneracy conditions. In characteristic zero, the bound $N^{10/9}$ remains valid. No subfield-avoidance condition is required.

The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners. Kravitz and Leng subsequently showed that $\exp(\exp(\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})))$ rotations suffice. In this paper, we prove an upper bound of \[\exp((\log \varepsilon^{-1})^{50000})\] rotations. We also show that at least $(π/2 + 0.003 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$ rotations are necessary, improving upon the natural lower bound of $(π/2 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$.
Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three

The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence. A divisibility calculation for the mod-$3$ Moore spectrum supplies a lift to a finite spectrum with a degree-$144$ self-map. The resulting iterates have nonzero image in the height-two detector of Carrick and Davies.
Additive Fréchet Regression for Random Objects
Changwon Choi; Wookyeong Song; Hans-Georg Müller; Byeong U. Park

Regression analysis for complex data taking values in a general metric space has gained increasing attention in recent years, particularly in the context of Fréchet regression with Euclidean predictors $\mathbb{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{p}$. However, local Fréchet regression, while more flexible than global Fréchet regression, suffers from the curse of dimensionality for the case of multivariate predictors. To address this issue while maintaining model flexibility, we introduce a framework of additive structured nonparametric regression when responses are situated in a general metric space. Overcoming the challenge of the lack of vector space structure in general metric spaces where the responses reside requires a novel approach that incorporates the additive structure via projection operators. This leads to a unified framework of additive regression for a wide range of response types, including one-dimensional distributions in Wasserstein space, network data represented by graph Laplacians and spherical data equipped with geodesic distances, among others. We establish pointwise and uniform consistency, including convergence rates, for the proposed additive Fréchet regression estimators, using smooth backfitting. The practical utility of this additive model is demonstrated through applications to brain connectivity network analysis using resting-state fMRI data and distributional physical activity data.
A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
Onur Beker; A. René Geist; Michael Posa; Marc Toussaint; Justin Carpentier; Georg Martius

Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact. In particular, we explain how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes. We distinguish equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep. We examine the existence and uniqueness of motion and contact forces, including the solver's role in selecting among multiple solutions. We then compare first-order and Newton-based methods, explain regularization and proximal strategies, and discuss trade-offs between computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity. Connections to widely used simulators, optimal control, and differentiable simulation help readers interpret simulation results, choose suitable formulations and solvers, and develop their own contact dynamics routines.
Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
Emiel Claasen; Mehregan Doroudiani; Claude Duhr; Axel Kleinschmidt; Franca Lippert; Oliver Schlotterer; Yoann Sohnle

The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $Γ(2)$ and $Γ_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $Γ(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.
Relativistic Kinetic Theory of Collisionless Particles with Variable Mass and Frame Transformations
Adrián Casado-Turrión; Paulo B. Ferraz; Mindaugas Karčiauskas; José Jaime Terente Díaz

In this work, we present the relativistic kinetic theory of a gas of collisionless point particles with non-constant mass, which can also be understood as being subject to a scalar force. Our results hold in an arbitrary conformal frame, and we explicitly derive how they transform between frames. The mathematical construction relies on a tilted Sasaki metric, whose associated phase-space geometry is adapted to particles of variable mass, as well as on the one-particle distribution function, from which macroscopic observables are derived. Finally, we show that the one-particle distribution function can always be taken to be gauge- and frame-invariant, and the corresponding generalisation of the Liouville (or collisionless Boltzmann) equation is satisfied in each frame.
Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications

We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.
Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$

In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.
Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift
Rami Atar; Leonid Mytnik; Dominic T. Schickentanz

We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-β.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $β$ as $β_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $β_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure.
