In 1926, Nevanlinna (Acta Math. {\bf 48} (1926), no. 3-4, 367-391) proved that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ CM in the complex plane, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ are four distinct complex values in the extended complex plane, then $f$ is a Möbius transformation of $g$, two of the shared values, say $a_1$ and $a_2$, are Picard exceptional values, and the cross ratio $\left(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4\right)=-1.$ Later on, Gundersen (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. {\bf 277} (1983), no. 2, 545-567. Correction: {\bf 304} (1987), 847-850) proved that if two non-constant meromorphic functions share two values CM and share two other values IM, then the functions share all four values CM. In 1992, Gundersen (Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. {\bf 20} (1992), no. 1-4, 99-106) proposed the following famous question: if two non-constant meromorphic functions share three distinct values IM and share a fourth value CM, then do the functions necessarily share all four values CM? This question is a long-standing question in the studies of the Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions, and has not been completely resolved by now. In this paper, we completely resolve the question, and prove that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ IM and $\infty$ CM, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ are three distinct and finite complex values in the complex plane, then $f$ and $g$ also share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ CM.

We investigate Euclidean self-orthogonality and the generalized Reed--Solomon (GRS) property for coefficient-vector codes generated by a monic polynomial $g$ and its shifts $xg,\ldots,x^{k-1}g$, of length $n=r+k$ and dimension $k$, where $°g=r$ and $3\le k\le r$. We give a complete classification, over any algebraically closed field, of the generators for which these codes are both self-orthogonal and GRS. Such generators have either distinct roots in a geometric progression satisfying explicit order and scalar conditions, or a single repeated root in certain positive characteristics. In particular, only finitely many generators occur for fixed $r$, $k$, and characteristic. We determine their maximal self-orthogonal lengths, show that the corresponding maximal-length codes are cyclic or negacyclic, and obtain exact generator counts over finite fields, together with the least fields of definition. In contrast, when $3\le k<r$, we prove that every algebraically closed field supports infinitely many pairwise monomially inequivalent self-orthogonal non-GRS maximum distance separable (MDS) codes in this family. Consequently, arbitrarily many such codes can be realized over a common finite extension of any prescribed finite field, while remaining inequivalent and non-GRS over its algebraic closure.
Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
Kumpei Tsuji; Ciara Galvin; Hiroyuki Omura; Naoto Mitsume; Mitsuteru Asai

This study assesses partitioned iterative fictitious-domain smoothed particle hydrodynamics (FD-SPH) for free-surface fluid-rigid-body interaction. Extending a strong-coupling framework for deformable structures, it combines volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton-Euler rigid-body updates. Within each time step, the mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious-fluid and rigid-body velocities is fed back iteratively. A fractional-step interpretation identifies conditions under which Passively Moving Solid (PMS) projection and Newton-Euler updates yield identical rigid-body velocities. Single-pass and iterative FD-SPH are compared under matched conditions. A two-dimensional settling-disk benchmark agrees with published results. In three-dimensional buoyancy-driven cube tests, single-pass coupling becomes unstable at specific gravities of 0.1 and 0.2. At 0.1, reducing the time-step size by a factor of 500 does not suppress the instability. Iterative strong coupling remains stable across the tested range of 0.1-1.0. Equilibrium heights and orientations agree with hydrostatic expectations and published stable configurations, respectively. Two- and three-dimensional wet-bed dam-break simulations reproduce experimental trends in wave elevation and floating-body heave and pitch. Two star-shaped rigid bodies demonstrate applicability to complex geometries without explicit interface reconstruction or surface-normal evaluation. All production strong-coupling simulations satisfy the prescribed relative-residual criterion at every time step before reaching the maximum coupling-iteration count. These results support iterative FD-SPH for lightweight and complex floating bodies in transient free-surface flows.
Time-independent equivalent matrix representation for time-domain boundary element analysis of large-scale 3D acoustic problems

This paper proposes a time-independent equivalent matrix representation for large-scale three-dimensional (3D) acoustic analysis with the time-domain boundary element method (TDBEM). In conventional TDBEM, pair-dependent retarded times couple spatial interactions to historical boundary data, causing substantial storage and history-convolution costs. The proposed representation decouples compressible spatial interactions from propagation history, allowing reuse of the same compressed spatial representation across propagation delays and throughout time marching without additional temporal interpolation of the kernel. For conventional space-time discretizations, blockwise low-rank compression yields the compressed equivalent matrix method in the $\mathcal{H}$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}$), with dynamic cluster-pair tracking to skip inactive interactions during wavefront propagation. For low-frequency, long-wavelength problems with a bounded number of nonzero time-lag matrices, the framework is extended to the $\mathcal{H}^2$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$) using delay-consistent partitioning, shared coupling matrices, and nested cluster bases. Under sparsity and bounded-parameter assumptions, storage and per-step cost of CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$ both scale as $O(N_s)$, excluding preprocessing. Numerical results agree well with conventional TDBEM and semi-analytical reference solutions. For CEM-$\mathcal{H}$, the storage requirement for a sphere with $N_s=20,480$ is reduced from approximately 349.0 GB to 1.6 GB, with a speedup of approximately $45.4\times$. For CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$, simulations with up to $N_s=1,310,720$ are performed in the low-frequency, long-wavelength regime. A million-degree-of-freedom underwater-vehicle model is also analyzed. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed framework for large-scale 3D transient acoustic analysis using TDBEM.
Determination of the unbounded potential of the Robin Laplacian from fixed-time boundary measurements of time-fractional diffusion-wave equations

We consider the time-fractional diffusion-wave equation $\partial_t^ρu - Δu + q u = 0$ in a bounded domain $Ω\subset \RR^n$, $n \geq 3$, where $\partial_t^ρ$ is the Caputo derivative of arbitrary order $ρ\in (0,2)$. This framework covers in a unified way the sub-diffusive case $ρ\in (0,1)$, the classical heat equation $ρ= 1$, and the super-diffusive case $ρ\in (1,2)$. The real-valued potential $q$ is only assumed to lie in $L^{n/2}(Ω)$, and the equation is endowed with zero initial conditions and a non-homogeneous Robin boundary condition, whose coefficient is allowed to be unbounded as well. The boundary excitations are supported in an arbitrary open subset $Γ_0$ of the boundary, and the trace of the solution is measured, at one fixed time, on another open subset $Γ_1$. We prove that the corresponding Robin-to-Dirichlet map uniquely determines the boundary spectral data of the underlying Robin Laplacian on $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$, provided that $Γ_0$ and $Γ_1$ overlap. When $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$ is the whole boundary, we deduce that $q$ is uniquely determined by this map in every dimension $n \geq 3$, the critical case $q \in L^{3/2}(Ω)$ in dimension three being included. The proof combines analytic continuation in the time variable, the Laplace transform and an identification of the poles and residues of meromorphic functions. The potential is then recovered from the boundary spectral data through an elliptic Robin-to-Dirichlet map, an integral identity, and complex geometric optics solutions.

Quasi-orthogonality is one of the key ingredients for proofs of optimal convergence rates for adaptive mesh refinement methods (Carstensen, Feischl, Page, and Praetorius, arXiv:1312.1171). The work of Feischl (arXiv:2008.12198) proposed a relaxed quasi-orthogonality that follows directly from the inf-sup stability of the underlying problem discretization. The proof uses an intricate connection to the stability of $LU$-factorization of matrices. Recently, Gantumur (arXiv:2609.16265) presented a vastly simplified argument based solely on Hilbert space arguments. Building on this idea, we show that quasi-orthogonality is a purely geometric property of a set of points. This property is checked for a large class of Petrov-Galerkin methods for monotone, non-linear equations.
Material optimization of optical properties of particulate products by transition matrix method and sequential global programming
Nico Nees; Lukas Pflug; Michael Stingl

Material optimization of nanoparticle assemblies, such as structurally coloured photonic crystals, attracts increasing interest. We combine the transition matrix method (TMM), which avoids spatial discretization of particles and surrounding medium, with sequential global programming (SGP) to optimize optical properties of particulate products by iteratively assigning predefined catalogue materials to individual particles. We derive exact separable models, reproducing the fully coupled objective under single-particle material changes, and computationally accessible first-order correct approximations for general continuously differentiable objectives. These approximations aim to capture the nonlinear, potentially nonconvex dependence on individual material variables beyond their local first-order behaviour. Within SGP, globally minimizing the particle-wise subproblems can yield substantial improvements in few outer iterations, including steps away from unfavourable stationary points, as previously demonstrated for discrete dipole approximation-based SGP. The construction exploits the decomposition of the TMM system matrix into a material-dependent block-diagonal and a material-independent coupling matrix, while the state and adjoint problems remain fully coupled. Applications include extinction, scattering quantities, and colour objectives. In a 35-particle extinction minimization problem, the objective decreases by 31.0% in 13 iterations. A fine-grid evaluation of the fully coupled objective shows that no tested single-particle material change improves the final design. For a 627-particle photonic crystal, chroma increases by 58.4-122.1% for different particle diameters in 17-42 iterations. The optimized designs favour absorbing material in layers away from the incident light, consistent with experimental findings.
The Scott sobriety on countable Frechet-Urysohn dcpos and locally compact meet-continuous dcpos

In this paper, we focus on the Scott Sobriety of countable dcpos and locally compact dcpos. Recently, Chen, Kou and Yang proved that every countable dcpo with its Scott topology first-countable is sober endowed with the Scott topology. A natural question is whether a countable dcpo whose Scott topology is a Frechet-Urysohn sapce must be sober. We show that a countable dcpo with condition FG is Scott sober if its Scott topology is Frechet-Urysohn. Besides, a countable Scott non sober Frechet-Urysohn dcpo is constructed. He and Zhang gave two sufficient conditions for the open problem whether every locally compact dcpo is Scott sober. One of their sufficient conditions is that any locally compact meet-continuous coherent dcpo is Scott sober. We further prove that each locally compact meet-continuous dcpo is always sober with respect to the Scott topology.
Auslander bounds under recollements and arrow removal

Auslander bounds measure uniformity in the eventual vanishing of extension groups and are closely related to homological conjectures, including the Auslander-Reiten conjecture and finitistic dimension conjecture. We study global and finitistic Auslander bounds of finite-dimensional algebras under recollements and arrow removal. For a recollement induced by an idempotent $e$ of an algebra $Λ$, we establish inequalities comparing the bounds of $Λ$ with those of the quotient algebra $Λ/ΛeΛ$ and the corner algebra $eΛe$. We also establish comparison results for cleft extensions and deduce that arrow removal preserves finiteness of both the global and finitistic Auslander bounds. Finally, we construct radical-square-zero algebras with $\findim(Λ_n)=0$ and $\mr{fab}(Λ_n)=\mr{gb}(Λ_n)=n$ for every $n\geq1$, yielding arbitrarily large gaps between finitistic Auslander bounds and finitistic dimensions.
A very robust Ramsey theorem for hypergraph matchings

A fundamental result in Ramsey theory due to Alon, Frankl and Lovász gives an exact formula for the $q$-colour Ramsey numbers of matchings in $r$-uniform hypergraphs: if $n\ge\mathsf{AFL}_r(\mathbf{t})=(r-1)\|\mathbf{t}\|_\infty+1+\sum_{j=1}^q(t_j-1)$ then in any $q$-edge-colouring of $K^r_n$ there is some colour $j$ with a matching of size $t_j$. We show that a very weak quasirandomness assumption suffices for this Ramsey property: we can replace $K^r_n$ by any $r$-graph $H$ on at least $\mathsf{AFL}_r(\mathbf{t})+o(n)$ vertices that is a sublinear connector, meaning that it has no balanced $r$-partite holes of linear size. This generalises the result for $r=2$ (ordinary graphs) that we proved previously using a compression algorithm based on Gallai-Edmonds decompositions. This structure theory is unavailable in the hypergraph setting, so we combine two other proof methods, namely (a) simultaneous optimisation in all colours by clustering vertices using fractional cover weights from LP duality, and (b) local-to-global structure via random sampling and Kahn's matching theorem.
An A $\infty$ -algebra structure for enriched Morse complexes

We construct a homotopy coherent product structure extending the Chas-Sullivan product on chains of the free loop space of a manifold. Our construction uses the framework of Morse homology with DG coefficients and perturbed Morse gradient trees. We define an operad given by moduli spaces of Morse gradient trees with a twisted differential. This Morse tree operad receives a map from a suspended A$\infty$-operad and in turn acts on Morse homology with DG coefficients associated to a fibration over a manifold with a fibrewise monoidal structure.
Finite groups with a fixed-point-free automorphism satisfying an irreducible identity

For any given irreducible polynomial $f(x)=a_0+a_1\cdot x+\cdots+a_d\cdot x^d\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$, we study the structure of finite groups $(G,\cdot)$ that have a fixed-point-free-automorphism $α$ satisfying the condition \[ \{g^{a_0}\cdotα(g)^{a_1}\cdotsα^d(g)^{a_d}\mid g\in G\}=\{1\}. \] We show that such a group $G$ is nilpotent of class at most $d^{2^d}$, provided that $|G|$ is coprime to an explicit, non-zero, integer invariant $ι(f(x))$ of $f(x)$. We do this by extending the solutions of the Frobenius conjecture. We also extend the solution of the restricted Burnside problem in prime exponent and the classification of the $n$-abelian groups.
Scaling limits for products of induced symplectic Ginibre matrices
Can Atacan; Noah Aygün; Yong-Woo Lee

We study the local eigenvalue correlations of products of independent induced symplectic Ginibre matrices in the large-dimensional limit. We establish the scaling limits of the correlation functions in the bulk, at the spectral edges, and outside the limiting spectral support, both near and away from the real axis. At regular spectral points, we show that the limiting correlations coincide with those of a single symplectic Ginibre ensemble, exhibiting Pfaffian structures near the real axis and determinantal structures away from it. At the origin, where the limiting spectral density develops a singularity, we derive an integral representation of the parameter-dependent limiting Pfaffian prekernel. Our proofs are based on a unified approach involving a differential equation for the skew prekernels and their asymptotics.
Higher-order magnetic hopfions in uniaxial chiral magnets
Vladyslav M. Kuchkin; Nikolai S. Kiselev

Chiral magnets host hopfions, but their experimentally observed configurations are largely limited to hopfion rings, heliknotons, and their clusters. Here, we show that uniaxial anisotropy stabilizes a diverse family of knotted and linked hopfions with zero and arbitrary positive Hopf indices. We identify their stability regions in the anisotropy -- field parameter space and introduce a systematic construction based on mapping skyrmion braids into three-dimensional magnetic textures. We find that the minimum energy of stable hopfions increases approximately linearly with the Hopf index.
A proof of the Lyons-Pemantle-Peres monotonicity conjecture for high offspring laws

We prove the Lyons-Pemantle-Peres conjecture for high enough offspring laws, that is we show that the speed satisfies $\ell'(λ) < 0 $ for the entire transient regime of the bias $λ\in (0, m)$ in the special case that the number of children $Z$ in the Galton-Watson tree satisfies $Z \geq 4$ almost surely.
Shrinking Limit for the Stationary Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation on Cross-Shaped Infinite Domains

We study the stationary nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a planar, cross-shaped infinite domain and in the shrinking limit. For any fixed thickness, we establish the existence of solutions through a variational approach. To overcome the loss of compactness inherent to the unbounded geometry and bypass the regularity obstructions caused by the re-entrant corners, we constrain the minimization problem to a cone of symmetric and monotonic functions. We then establish the resolvent-preservation property, ensuring the constrained minimizers are stationary solutions. As the transverse width vanishes, we establish a transverse collapse phenomenon, that is, the two-dimensional solutions flatten across the central junction and become purely one-dimensional along the infinite branches. In this way, we prove that cross solutions converge strongly to a stationary solution on the limiting graph in a suitable sense. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this dimensional reduction recovers both vertex continuity and the Kirchhoff conditions.
On the trajectories of the ID algorithm
Ivano Lodato; Simran Hiranandani; Aditya Varna Iyer

The ID algorithm decides whether an interventional distribution can be computed from observational data and, when it can, returns a formula in which products, ratios and summations of conditional probabilities are nested inside one another. We study these formulas by following the trajectories of the calls of the algorithm, each of which ends with a tail (an alternation of lines 7 and 2) and an exit, and we derive two main results. First, line~4 and the exit lines fix the single outer summation of the output, while the tail forms everything inside it, both the inner summations and the ratios. Second, a ratio keeps a summation in its denominator only when a repetition of the tail is entangled, and a test of ancestry in the original graph decides, before any formula is computed, whether a topological order can be chosen so as to avoid it. We also derive a bound on the nesting depth of the output, and show a simple ``dimensional'' count that every output has to satisfy. Together, these results constrain the form of an ID output and guide its implementation and simplification.
Ordering Is Not Deciding: Towards Preference-Consistent Multi-Objective Design--Decision Optimisation
E. Özer; A. R. M. Wolfert

In integrated design and group decision-making, Pareto filtering identifies non-dominated alternatives but does not determine which design best fits actors' preferences. Applying those preferences after filtering does not guarantee that the best-fit solution will be found: the filter may already have excluded the alternative with the highest aggregated preference, even when all combinations of fixed performance-improvement directions are considered. We compare Pareto--based selection with Integrative Maximisation of Aggregated Preferences (IMAP) on constructed multi-objective design--decision problems, using identical feasible solution spaces and actor preferences for both methods. The problems involve two system performances and up to four preference functions elicited from up to two actors. They cover independent and interdependent relationships between feasible performance values, monotonic and non-monotonic preference functions, and conflicting preferences for the same performance. In some cases, Pareto filtering excludes the best-fit solution, whereas IMAP identifies it. These counterexamples show that Pareto optimality does not guarantee a preference consistent decision, even in problems much simpler than real-world design and group decision-making problems. Pareto analysis can support ordering and exploration in performance space. IMAP instead models and aggregates actor preferences before optimisation and maximises the resulting aggregate preference over the full feasible and acceptable solution space.
X Hedging: towards an eXplainable artificial intelligence option Hedging framework
Bjørn André Aaslund; Johannes Berge; Ayoub Haida; Ying Ni; Rita Pimentel

We propose X Hedging, an alternative to the Deep Hedging framework that addresses computational and explainability limitations of neural-network-based hedging strategies. Deep Hedging leverages neural networks to learn flexible hedging policies but relies on opaque models and typically requires large training datasets, which can complicate interpretation and limit its effectiveness in data-constrained settings. X Hedging takes a step toward addressing these limitations by replacing neural networks with tree ensemble methods, specifically LightGBM, to estimate hedging strategies. This design provides a computationally efficient alternative while preserving strong hedging performance and moving toward more user-centered explainability. To integrate LightGBM into a reinforcement-learning-style hedging framework, we introduce an optimization approach that sequentially trains tree-ensemble models while introducing stochasticity through random training orders. In controlled experiments, X Hedging achieves performance comparable to Deep Hedging while offering greater user-centered explainability, improved computational efficiency, and substantially higher robustness when training data are limited. The numerical results demonstrate that tree-ensemble methods provide an effective computational alternative to neural networks for data-driven dynamic hedging.
Full Rank and Stable Sampling of $\tanh$ Networks

We study the recovery of feedforward $\tanh$ networks of fixed architecture with $P$ parameters from finitely many point evaluations. First, we characterize the set of parameters where the differential of the realization map has full rank and show that it coincides with the regular parameters in the sense of Vla{č}i{ć} and B{ö}lcskei (2021). Second, we make use of this characterization to prove that almost every tuple of $2P+1$ sampling points yields uniform-norm Lipschitz stability on compact subsets of this parameter set. Third, we prove that for exact observations, projected gradient descent and projected Gauss--Newton converge locally from sufficiently close feasible initial guesses. The same evaluations also determine the realized function for arbitrary parameters and identify parameters in the characterized set up to permutations and sign changes of hidden neurons. Finally, we develop a general framework for real-analytic networks that highlights the role of full rank in stability and local reconstruction.
Inference in High-Dimensional Linear Mediation Models
Samriddha Lahiry; Rajarshi Mukherjee; Pragya Sur

Mediation analysis plays an important role in psychology, epidemiology, and genomics. Al- though high-dimensional mediation has been studied extensively, existing inferential methods typically rely on sparsity assumptions that may be difficult to justify when many individually weak mediators collectively produce a substantial effect. We study inference for both the over- all indirect effect and the effect transmitted through an individual mediator in a proportional high-dimensional regime, where the number of mediators and the sample size grow at compa- rable rates, without imposing sparsity on the mediator effects. Standard debiasing procedures for high-dimensional inference commonly rely on design-covariance information or additional structural assumptions on precision-matrix directions. In mediation models, however, the full outcome-design covariance depends on unknown mediator-model coefficients, creating an addi- tional challenge when such information or structure is unavailable. To address this challenge, we introduce an approximate debiasing procedure based on partial ridge regression and show that the resulting estimator is asymptotically bias-corrected and Gaussian. We also develop a cross-fitted estimator with a smaller asymptotic variance than its sample-split counterpart. In addition, we construct consistent estimators of the limiting variances of both the sample-split and cross-fitted estimators. Together, these results provide feasible inferential procedures for global and pathwise mediation effects.
A note on the learning coefficient of exceptional singularities

We compute the learning coefficient of a polynomial neural network at a point of its neurovariety all of whose real parameters are good, and show that it equals $d/2$, with multiplicity one, where $d$ is the difference between the dimension of the parameter space and the dimension of the group of symmetries of the architecture. This is the value attained at a generic point of the neurovariety; consequently, exceptional singularities are invisible to the pair $(λ,θ)$ whenever all real parameters in their fibre are good. By contrast, at a full parameter in the interior of the parameter domain whose differential has non-maximal rank we show that $λ<d/2$. The two statements together give a statistical reading of the geometric distinction between nodes and cusps.
Optimal Impure $(r,δ)$-Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes with Explicit Minimum Localities
Yang Li; Shitao Li; Gaojun Luo; San Ling

Quantum locally recoverable codes with $(r,δ)$-locality ($(r,δ)$-qLRCs) are quantum error-correcting codes in which $δ-1$ erased qudits can be recovered by accessing only $r$ other qudits. The minimum locality of a qLRC is the least $r$ such that it has $(r,δ)$-locality. This paper aims to construct optimal impure $(r,δ)$-qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets and explicit minimum localities, where the optimality is measured by the Singleton-like bound of Guruswami, Kshirsagar, and Trivedi (GKT-optimal). Such qLRCs have particular advantages in recovering as many quantum erasures as possible while operating in parallel and with minimal qudit access overhead. We first characterize the recovering sets and the minimum locality of any CSS code by local relative distances, which are relative minimum distances of punctured codes with respect to shortened codes. We then construct impure qLRCs as CSS codes from nested pairs of generalized monomial-Cartesian codes. Grouping the monomials by their degree in the last variable, we reduce both their minimum distances and their local recovery to nested pairs of codes in the remaining variables, and the coordinates with the same values of these variables form disjoint recovering sets. In this way, we obtain four infinite families of GKT-optimal impure $(r,δ)$-qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets, and determine their minimum localities and the recovering sets attaining them for every admissible $δ$, except for a partial range of $δ$ in one family. These minimum localities need not be monotone in $δ$. In particular, two of the families contain GKT-optimal impure subfamilies of CSS codes CSS$(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})$ with $(r,δ)$-locality for some $r<n-δ+1$ at values of $δ$ for which $\mathcal{C}$ has no classical $(r',δ)$-locality for any $0<r'<n$, where $n$ is the length of $\mathcal{C}$.
Weak Degeneracy with Availability for Planar Graphs

Every planar graph admits exponentially many proper colorings for any assignment of lists of five allowed colors to its vertices. In this paper, we show that very little beyond degeneracy is needed to prove that this statement holds. In particular, given a planar graph G (but not the list assignment), our argument provides an algorithm consisting entirely of instructions of the following form: ``Color the vertex v using any color c from its list, and remove c from the lists of neighbors of v.'' and ``For the edge uv, choose any k colors from the list of u, then color v by any color c from its list that does not appear among these k colors, and remove c from the lists of neighbors of v.'' For every assignment of lists of size five to vertices of G, following this algorithm in all possible ways guarantees that at least $2^{|V(G)|/7}$ different proper colorings of G are produced (and at least one color choice is guaranteed to be available in each step). We also show that this result has the following consequence: for every planar graph G, there exists a set $R\subseteq V(G)$ of size at least 0.06|V(G)| such that G can be properly colored from any assignment of lists of size four to vertices in R and lists of size five to the rest of vertices of G. Moreover, these statements remain true even in stronger settings, such as for correspondence coloring.
Polynomial spaces are locally Paley-Wiener: local spectral geometry, sampling, and interpolation

We identify the local Paley-Wiener structure of multivariate polynomial spaces on centrally symmetric convex bodies and apply it to sampling and interpolation. For a Bernstein-Markov measure with a positive continuous density in the interior, the normalized reproducing kernel at scale $1/n$ converges to the Fourier transform of the uniform probability measure on the dual unit ball of the Baran metric. We call this set the local spectral body. It describes the frequencies available to polynomials near each point. By recovering local bandlimited functions together with their $L^2$ norms, we obtain bulk universality and Christoffel asymptotics uniformly on compact subsets of the interior. This connection allows us to use Fourier methods to study polynomial sampling. If weighted sampling is uniformly stable with asymptotically one node per polynomial coefficient, almost every local spectral body must admit an exponential Riesz basis. Combining this result with Ortega-Cerdà's theorem for smooth spectra, we show that in dimension $d\ge2$, a $C^2$ boundary with everywhere positive curvature forces a positive proportion of extra sampling nodes. This rules out uniformly stable complete interpolation on such bodies. The same lower bound on the number of nodes applies to positive cubature exact through degree $2n$, since such a rule preserves the squared $L^2$ norm of every polynomial of degree at most $n$. The corresponding local-to-global problem remains open. If the local spectral body at every interior point admits an exponential Riesz basis, can one choose exactly as many nodes as polynomial coefficients at each degree so that sampling and interpolation are uniformly stable on the whole body?
Global renormalized finite-energy weak solutions to the three-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system on tori for $γ>4/3$
Guangyi Hong; Hongyun Peng; Changjiang Zhu

Building on the foundational theory of finite-energy weak solutions initiated by P.-L. Lions and further developed by E. Feireisl and collaborators, we establish the global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus, with constant viscosity coefficients and pressure law \(P(ρ)=ρ^γ\), for every \(γ>4/3\) and arbitrary finite-energy initial data. This extends the classical three-dimensional Lions--Feireisl existence theory beyond the threshold \(γ>3/2\), and in particular, covers the important case $ γ=7/5 $ for air (cf. \cite{Anderson}). Compared to the classical theory, we develop a novel approach to establish the improved pressure-integrability estimate compatible with the viscous and inertial terms, via constructing a periodic test field through barycentric optimal transport. This improved pressure-integrability estimate, combined with an effective viscous flux identity and an entropy comparison, provides the compactness needed to identify the nonlinear limits and recover the energy inequality.
Taylor expansions for first-passage time distributions of Brownian motion with moving boundaries

We analyse the distribution of the first-passage time of Brownian motion to a time-dependent boundary as a function of the boundary. We prove that the boundary-to-distribution map is infinitely many times differentiable along the Cameron-Martin space $\mathscr{H},$ and obtain a with a bound on the truncation error Taylor expansion with a bound on the truncation error. We obtain identities connecting (i) the $\mathscr{H}$-derivatives of the first-passage time distribution, (ii) the Wiener-Itô chaos kernels of the indicator that the Brownian motion stays below the boundary, and (iii) Krylov-Veretennikov-Zvonkin-type operators. These identities yield relatively tractable representations for the $\mathscr{H}$-derivatives of the first-passage time distribution when the taboo transition density is available, notably for linear boundaries. As an application of the above results we propose Taylor approximations up to second order of the first-passage time distribution. In the examples considered, the first-order approximation is more accurate than the classical tangent approximation and its hazard-rate variant, while remaining straightforward to implement.
Microscopic Probabilities for U-Statistics and Almost-Balanced Permutations

We estimate the probability that a vector of U-statistics lies within $C/n$ of a target in the range of typical fluctuations. For sufficiently large $C$, we prove a lower bound of the typical Gaussian order under finite variance, and a matching upper bound for bounded kernels. We show that under finite variance alone, stronger concentration may occur, and find the best possible asymptotic upper bound. Our proof is algorithmic, estimating probabilities by counting successful modifications produced by a random algorithm. We apply this result to settle a question of Beniamini, Lavee and Linial (2025), who asked if there exist permutations with $k$-order sub-pattern counts at most $O(n^{k-1})$ away from one another for $k>4$. We prove not only existence, but enumerate these permutations up to a constant factor, showing that there are $Θ(n!n^{-(k-1)^2/2})$ such permutations of size $n$.
Wolff-type ideal theorems for slice regular functions
Zhenghua Xu; Wenwan Yang; Cheng Yuan

We study Wolff-type ideal problems in $H^\infty(\mathbb B)$, the algebra of bounded slice regular functions on the quaternionic unit ball. We construct $f,f_1,f_2\in H^\infty(\mathbb B)$ satisfying $|f|^2\le |f_1|^2+|f_2|^2$ such that $f^{\ast N}\notin\mathcal I(f_1,f_2)$ for every integer $N\ge1$, where $\mathcal I(f_1,f_2)$ denotes the right ideal generated by $f_1$ and $f_2$. We also construct intrinsic functions $a,a_1,a_2\in H^\infty(\mathbb B)$ satisfying $|a|\le |a_1|+|a_2|\le1$ and $a^{\ast2}\notin\mathcal I(a_1,a_2)$. For intrinsic data satisfying $|f|\le\sum_{\ell=1}^n|f_\ell|$, the cube $f^{\ast3}$ has a representation in the generated right ideal with intrinsic coefficients. For general data, we obtain sufficient conditions for ideal membership under a fourth-order pointwise bound with a Dini factor. If the generators preserve a common slice, a quadratic bound with a Dini factor suffices.

In this paper, we will argue that the notion of computational trust can be understood as a form of fallible intuitionistic knowledge grounded in verification. This approach naturally captures a key aspect of trust: it involves vulnerability. Specifically, it validates the principle that verification leads to trust but does not validate the opposite principle that trust leads to verification. Thus, we can trust on good grounds that some program will perform according to its specification but the program might still fail. We present a simple logic for capturing this notion of computational trust based on constructive modal propositional logic extended with a trust modality, which will be specified in an inferential fashion and by utilizing the proofs-as-programs correspondence.
The distribution of greatest common divisors of binomial coefficients and their upper indices

For positive integers $n,d$, let $A_d(n)$ denote the number of integers $0\le k\le n$ such that $\gcd\bigl(n,\binom nk\bigr)=d$, and put $S_d(x)=\sum_{n\le x}A_d(n)$. We prove that, for each fixed integer $d\ge2$, \[ S_d(x)\sim\frac{d-1}{d}\,\mathfrak c\,\frac{x}{\log x}\qquad(x\to\infty),\qquad \mathfrak c=1.526453\ldots \] The key step is to extend the coprimality result of Ford and Konyagin to arbitrary fixed parameters $d\ge2$ and $1\le j<d$, obtaining \[ \#\Bigl\{m\le x:\gcd\Bigl(m,\binom{dm}{jm}\Bigr)=1\Bigr\} \sim\mathfrak c\frac x{\log x}. \] The zero set of the corresponding Kummer carry function is a finite union of intervals of total measure $1/2$. We combine this property with estimates for small prime factors, Selberg trigonometric approximation, and exponential sum estimates over primes to count simultaneous carry conditions. We further prove that, for every fixed integer $e\ge1$, \[ \#\Bigl\{m\le x:\gcd\Bigl(m,\binom{dm}{jm}\Bigr)=e\Bigr\} \sim\frac{\mathfrak c}{e}\frac x{\log x}. \]
Kernel Compensation and Quasi-Newton Iteration for Nonlinear Non-Hermitian Eigenproblems in Photonic Crystals

We extend the kernel-compensated eigensolver developed in our previous work from Hermitian to non-Hermitian nonlinear eigenproblems arising in dispersive photonic crystals. A mimetic finite-difference discretization preserves the discrete curl--divergence complex, and three-dimensional discrete Fourier transforms provide matrix-free realizations of the curl and divergence blocks. The isotropic inverse dielectric coefficient is stored through the material-edge indices, so its value and derivatives can be updated without assembling a Maxwell matrix. Kernel compensation is characterized by a fixed unitary block diagonalization, which remains exact for the nonlinear problem. At each outer step, a right Generalized Davidson iteration solves the non-Hermitian linearized eigenproblem. The exact derivative of a simple eigenvalue branch is expressed through its left and right eigenvectors. To avoid a second eigensolve, we replace the left eigenvector by the available normalized right eigenvector and obtain a right-Rayleigh quasi-Newton update. We prove that the exact left--right Newton iteration is locally quadratically convergent at simple roots, whereas the proposed iteration with exact inner eigenpairs has an explicit linear error factor and is at least quadratic when the derivative defect vanishes. A spectral regularity estimate bounds the gradient appearing in the derivative defect.
Coxeter Group Symmetries of Frieze Patterns

Coxeter group symmetries of frieze patterns are investigated through their relation to $2\times n$ matrices and the associated Plücker coordinates. For odd order $n$, the symmetric group acts on the set of friezes, while for even $n$, the dihedral subgroup acts. We further show that a larger group acts when $n = 6$.
Quantitative approximations for finite-state mean-field configuration models

We establish quantitative approximations for the empirical measures of finite-state mean-field particle systems in a general framework. The scales of the empirical drift and covariance distinguish the ODE and critical diffusion regimes and determine the corresponding time rescaling. In the ODE regime, we obtain quantitative central limit approximations in the $1$-Wasserstein distance and a Bernstein-type concentration inequality. The concentration bound has no dimensional prefactor. Its explicit time dependence also identifies growing intervals on which the ODE approximation remains accurate. In the critical regime, we prove a quantitative nonlinear diffusion approximation in the $1$-Wasserstein distance. We apply our quantitative approximation results to noisy voter systems, Moran models with mutations and selections, heat-bath Glauber dynamics for the $p$-spin Curie--Weiss model, and autocatalytic reactions with mutations.
Symmetry of pole order spectra and freeness of plane curves

Let $C:f=0$ be a reduced plane curve of degree $d$ having only weighted homogeneous singularities, and let $\mathrm{Sp}_P^0(f)$ be the pole order spectrum of the top cohomology of its Milnor fiber. Writing $\mathrm{Sp}^0_P(f)=\sum_q m_q\,t^{q/d}$, we show that $m_q-m_{2d-q}=n(f)_{q-3}-n(f)_{q+d-3}$ for every integer $q$, where $n(f)_k$ is the Hilbert function of the Jacobian module $N(f)$. Consequently, $\mathrm{Sp}^0_P(f)$ is symmetric with respect to $α\mapsto 2-α$ if and only if $C$ is free. For a free curve with exponents $(d_1,d_2)$ we give a closed formula: $\mathrm{Sp}^0_P(f)-t^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}^1_P(f)$ depends only on $(d,d_1)$. This explains the symmetry of pole order spectra of reflection line arrangements, an open problem raised in Dimca's monograph on hyperplane arrangements.
Asymptotic behavior of solutions to the one-dimensional $p$-system with time-dependent non-smooth damping

This paper is concerned with the asymptotic behavior of solutions to the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional $p$-system with time-dependent damping. When the damping coefficient $b(t)$ behaves like $(1+t)^{-λ}$ with $0\leλ<1$, the solutions are expected to converge to a diffusion wave. For $b(t)=(1+t)^{-λ}$, previous studies have established convergence to a diffusion wave together with convergence rates using the energy method, provided that the initial perturbation and the wave strength are sufficiently small. In this paper, we introduce two auxiliary functions and reformulate our problem into two perturbation problems adapted to the structure of the system. This enables us to prove a result analogous to those obtained in previous studies, without assuming the differentiability of $b(t)$. The auxiliary functions are given by the differential equations $1+g'(t)=b(t)g(t)$ and $1-h'(t)=b(t)h(t)$, respectively. Our result shows that it suffices to assume $b\in C([0,\infty))$, $b(t)\asymp(1+t)^{-λ}$, and $|g'(t)|\lesssim(1+t)^{-(1-λ)}$ to obtain convergence to a diffusion wave.
The compressible-incompressible CAO problem introduced by Lions, Temam and Wang

We study the (CAO) system of Lions-Temam-Wang, describing a compressible atmosphere coupled to an incompressible ocean through a fully nonlinear boundary condition representing wind stress at the interface. In their foundational work, the system is reformulated in pressure coordinates under the assumption that the pressure is constant at the interface, leading to a purely incompressible system. In this article, we prove for the first time the strong well-posedness of the coupled compressible-incompressible system both locally and globally for small initial data.
Block decimation and perfect actions for $p$-adic valued path integrals

In earlier work we introduced a finite-partition propagator for $\mathbb{C}_p$-valued wave functions, in which the intermediate positions are integrated against atomic measures. The iterated integral evaluates the action on the equally spaced chain between the endpoints, so each partition level is obtained by iterating an exact, tree-level block decimation of two-point lattice actions, with no integration over fluctuations. This kinematic decimation is the Fréchet derivative, at the free actions, of the variational decimation underlying classical perfect actions. Since the time step $p^n$ is small in the real norm exactly when it is large $p$-adically, refinement and coarsening (the ultraviolet and infrared directions over $\mathbb{R}$) exchange roles, and each yields one limit. Under refinement, potentials supported on $\mathbb{Z}_p$, given there by a convergent power series, and entering the slice action without the time-step weight produce an interaction that stabilizes off the diagonal after finitely many steps and converges uniformly on $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$, with sharp error $p^{-M}$ after $M$ steps, to a scale-covariant (perfect) action, governed near the diagonal by a Volkenborn integral; with the weight no limit exists. For the harmonic oscillator no refinement limit exists at fixed frequency, but under coarsening the variational flow is solved in closed form: the lattice angle is multiplied by $p$ at each step, the coupling obeys a Chebyshev recursion, no caustic occurs, and the rescaled action converges to a free action with renormalized mass $m_0\sin_p(θ_0)/θ_0$. The rescaled linearized map is diagonalizable on polynomial actions with eigenvalues $p^{2-b}$, so directions relevant over $\mathbb{R}$ are irrelevant over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and conversely.
Geodesics for generalised complex Hessian equations
Kartick Ghosh; Ziyue Wang; Yulun Xu

We study geodesics associated with a class of generalized complex Hessian equations on compact Kähler manifolds. The defining polynomial is allowed to have degree \(1\leq d\leq n\) and is assumed to be right-Noetherian. We establish the existence of unique smooth solutions to an elliptic regularization of the geodesic equation and derive uniform a priori estimates, independent of the regularization parameter. A key ingredient is a partial Legendre transform, which reduces the regularized equation to a form that allows us to obtain uniform spatial and mixed Hessian estimates. These estimates yield the existence of unique weak geodesics as limits of the regularized solutions, with convergence in \(C^{1,α}\) for every \(0<α<1\). We further establish convexity properties of associated functionals: the \(I_2\)-functional is affine and the \(J_1\)-functional is convex along weak geodesics. Finally, we study the induced \(\mathcal{E}^{p}\)-Finsler geometry on the space of admissible potentials and prove that the lengths of the regularized geodesics converge to the corresponding path distances, the \(\mathcal{E}^{p}\)-energies of the regularized geodesics converge uniformly in time to the \(p\)-th power of the corresponding path distance, and that the resulting path distance is a genuine metric for every \(1\leq p<\infty\).
Plane curves attaining the Dimca-Sernesi bound and Jacobian syzygies of pencil-type curves

For a reduced plane curve $C:f=0$ of degree $d$ with only weighted homogeneous singularities, Dimca and Sernesi proved that the minimal degree of a Jacobian relation satisfies $\mathrm{mdr}(f)\geq α_C\, d-2$, where $α_C$ is the minimal Arnold exponent of the singularities of $C$. We call $C$ DS-extremal (Dimca-Sernesi extremal) when equality holds. We show that curves of pencil type $f=Φ(g,h)$, in particular curves of $(p,q)$-torus type $g^p+h^q$, are DS-extremal, the minimal syzygy being $
abla g	imes
abla h$. Under a natural transversality assumption we determine the minimal free resolution of the Milnor algebra of such a curve: it depends only on $d$, $\mathrm{deg}\, g$ and $\mathrm{deg}\, h$, and the module of Jacobian syzygies is generated by $
abla g	imes 
abla h$ and the three Koszul syzygies. For irreducible sextics with six cusps we prove that $3\le \mathrm{mdr}(f)\le 4$, that $\mathrm{mdr}(f)=3$ for curves of torus type, and that $\mathrm{mdr}(f)=4$ for the general curve in the component of non-torus sextics containing Oka's curve. Hence Zariski's classical pair is a Ziegler pair detected by $\mathrm{mdr}$, and the reason is the extremality of the torus member. We conjecture that every DS-extremal curve is of pencil type and support this by the nodal case and by computations.
Nonsolvable critical groups with the spectrum of $S_{10}$
D. V. Lytkina; V. D. Mazurov

We classify the nonsolvable finite groups that are critical with respect to the spectrum of the symmetric group $S_{10}$. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: $S_{10}$ and $(A_9\times C_3)\rtimes C_2$, where the involution acts on $A_9$ by conjugation by a transposition and on $C_3$ by inversion. The quotient of any nonsolvable group with this spectrum by its solvable radical is almost simple. All possible simple socles are treated without assuming that the radical is nilpotent. The final cases, $L_3(4)$ and $A_6$, are excluded using the canonical subgroup $K=[R(G)\cap G^\infty,G^\infty]$, actions on chief factors, and the required element orders $9,20,30$. In the $A_6$ case, the final contradiction is the existence of an element of order $16$. Reproducible certificates accompany the character-table and matrix calculations.

An institution must complete a portfolio adjustment, but traders who prepare inventory for it can choose whether to participate. We study how public forecasts affect the institution's cost in a Bayesian execution game with optional activation, transient impact, and uniform-price terminal completion. The curvature of equilibrium cost as a function of the posterior target mean determines the value of information. In the scalar model, information benefits every fixed participation roster. Optional supply can reverse this ranking at entry, at full participation, and in a smooth interior with lognormal activation costs. For centered scalar targets, information weakly lowers cost relative to no information, strictly when the posterior mean is nonzero with positive probability. Centered Gaussian precision gains are always beneficial. An exact symmetric finite-population equilibrium identifies how information resolution and individual strategic size interact near entry. A portfolio extension gives a matrix criterion for the fixed-roster ranking, which can fail under general cross-impact. Even with isotropic execution, shared activation allows equally accurate signals about target magnitude and composition to have opposite execution values under one unchanged prior. Intraday ETF price data is used to characterize target uncertainty and trading conditions without identifying activation or institutional costs.
A note on a recent result by Lorist, Meyries, and Veraar, or the counterexample which I missed

Recently Lorist, Meyries, and Veraar showed, among others, that the inverse of an infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup on a Hilbert space need not to be an infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup. In this note we show that with the ingredients of that paper, the example can be constructed more directly. Furthermore, the author reflects on the reason why he did not construct this a decade ago.
Global-in-Time Nonrelativistic Limit and KAM Tori for the Complex Klein-Gordon Equation on the Circle

This paper establishes a global-in-time nonrelativistic limit for families of small-amplitude quasi-periodic solutions of the cubic complex Klein-Gordon equation on the circle. Firstly, we construct by a KAM block scheme, small-amplitude two-frequency invariant tori and show that their linear stability depends on whether the two excited Fourier indices coincide or are distinct: coincident indices yield linearly stable tori, whereas distinct indices yield partially hyperbolic tori. Moreover, controlling the dependence of the KAM scheme on the speed of light, we construct quasi-periodic solutions whose frequencies, after a gauge transformation, coincide exactly with those of quasi-periodic solutions of the limiting coupled NLS system, obtaining an approximation uniform for all times in the nonrelativistic regime. By this result, we further show that there exists a positive-measure set of frequencies such that, for each frequency, we can fix a quasi-periodic solution of the coupled NLS system and a suitable subsequence of Klein-Gordon solutions converging globally in time to the fixed NLS solution.
Self-Supervised Operator Learning for Channel Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems
Erqiang Tang; Zixin Wang; Wei Guo; Shenghui Song; Jun Zhang; Khaled B. Letaief

Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communications through adaptive antenna repositioning. Recently, Fourier neural operators (FNOs) have shown strong potential for FAS channel estimation owing to their ability to learn resolution-invariant mappings and generalize across different port densities. However, existing operator learning approaches require densely sampled channel realizations as training labels, whereas a practical receiver only collects noisy pilot observations from a small subset of ports. This mismatch between training requirements and practical channel acquisition poses a major obstacle to deployment. To address this challenge, we develop a self-supervised framework that trains the FNO-based estimator directly from noisy sub-sampled pilots without any labeled channel fields. The proposed objective combines a pilot splitting strategy, which creates supervision at ports hidden from the model input, with a correction based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE) that eliminates the measurement noise bias. We prove that this objective admits the same minimum mean square error (MMSE) solution as the ideal supervised criterion. Since the loss relies solely on received pilots, the estimator can be continually adapted online on the live pilot stream. Simulation results show that the self-supervised FNO achieves accuracy comparable to supervised training, generalizes zero-shot to unseen port resolutions, and rapidly recovers from distribution shift via online adaptation.
The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers -- A simple Introduction

The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here. We give an elementary introduction to the subject.
Global well-posedness for the 2D full compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system
Liening Qiao; Juntao Sun; Jiahong Wu; Fuyi Xu

This paper establishes the global well-posedness and nonlinear stability of the 2D full compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system $\mathbb T^2$, for smooth initial data close to the equilibrium with constant density and temperature, zero velocity and background magnetic field $\mathbf e_2=(0,1)$. Neither the density nor the magnetic field is damped or diffused in this system. Here, we impose no Diophantine condition on the background magnetic field, no symmetry on the data and no special geometry on the domain. Our proof rests on two intrinsic stabilizing mechanisms hidden in the structure of the system. First, the background magnetic field generates damped wave structures which provide dissipation for the $x_2$-derivatives of the density and of the magnetic field. Second, we introduce a new good unknown $Φ$, an effective total pressure gradient that combines the density, the temperature with the magnetic pressure. Although none of its constituents is dissipative by itself, we show that the coupling of $Φ$ with the divergence of the velocity and with the temperature produces dissipation for $Φ$ in all directions, together with an extra regularization of the divergence of the velocity. Combining these two mechanisms with new anisotropic commutator estimates and a hierarchy of time-weighted energy estimates, we prove that the system admits a unique global solution in $H^N(\mathbb T^2)$ for every $N\geq5$, and obtain a uniform-in-time bound on the highest-order energy as well as explicit algebraic decay rates. Even in comparison with the known result for the simpler isentropic counterpart, where the highest-order energy was only shown to grow at most algebraically in time for data in $H^{N}$ with $N\geq10$, our result removes the possible growth and lowers the regularity requirement to $N\geq5$.
Beyond geometric lattices: pseudo-atoms and redundant join representations in the face lattice of the permutohedron

We study the lattice obtained from the poset of ordered set partitions (the Fubini poset), ordered by merging adjacent blocks, by adjoining a bottom element of rank -1. It is the face lattice of the permutohedron. We look at it from the point of view of geometric lattices: it is graded, atomic and coatomic in the strong sense that every element is a meet of coatoms, but it is not semimodular. Its atoms are the $n!$ permutations, and its elements of rank one, which we call pseudo-atoms, are the edges of the permutohedron. Describing ordered set partitions by chains of subsets, the cuts, we show that the rank is modular whenever the meet is above $\bot$, while the join of two distant atoms can have large rank, so that the rank of the join is a metric on permutations. An element has a unique representation as a join of atoms only up to rank one; above it, irredundant representations have sizes ranging from two to the rank, and the redundancy of an element is its number of atoms minus two. The Möbius function is that of an Eulerian lattice, the Whitney numbers are the face numbers of the permutohedron, and the characteristic polynomial has the alternating coefficients of the geometric case, but only $\bot$ and $\top$ are left-modular, so the lattice is not supersolvable. We show that it is CL-shellable, we exhibit EL-labelings for $n\le5$, and we compare the independent sets of Raz arXiv:2307.05005 (v3, Jan. 2026) with irredundant families and with the matroid of the vertices of the permutohedron. Replacing ordered set partitions by partial flags of subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^n$ gives a $q$-analogue, whose Möbius function is $(-1)^{\mathrm{rk}+1}q^κ$, with $κ$ the number of pairs of elements in a common block at $q=1$, and whose characteristic polynomial and Betti numbers are polynomials in $q$.
Supersymmetric Hilbert complexes and Witten deformation on stratified pseudomanifolds

We present a framework to study topics related to index theory and Dirac operators with N=1,2 supersymmetry (SUSY), extending it to stratified pseudomanifolds with wedge metrics (iterated conic metrics). Taylor, we give a broad overview of the relevance of SUSY to index theory on manifolds with boundaries and singularities, mainly focusing on the new insights and results related to N=2 SUSY that the authors have uncovered recently.
A generic construction of complex codebooks from functions over Abelian groups

Codebooks with small inner-product correlation play a central role in direct spread code division multiple access communications, space-time coding, compressed sensing, and related areas because they improve system performance. This paper presents a generic construction and a modified construction of complex codebooks from functions on finite Abelian groups. By choosing perfect nonlinear functions, we systematically obtain several families of optimal or asymptotically optimal codebooks with respect to the Welch or Levenshtein bounds. These constructions recover a number of known optimal codebooks and also yield new codebooks with previously unreported parameters.

A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Compactness of branched conformal immersions with free boundary

We prove bubble tree compactness for branched conformal immersions with free boundary under uniform Dirichlet and Willmore energy bounds, with images in a fixed compact subset of \R^K and possibly degenerating conformal structures. In particular, we prove that the convergence satisfies the Dirichlet energy identity and the no-neck property. Finally, as applications of the bubble tree convergence results, we obtain Willmore energy minimizers for short free boundary annuli under a Steklov constraint and concentration of free boundary disk minimizers near maxima of the support mean curvature under a small area constraint. We construct a complete Kähler threefold $(M,ω)$ with positive Ricci curvature and infinite-dimensional third rational homology. It admits no analytic compactification, answering Yau's compactification question negatively (see \cite{Yau1992}, Problem~71, p.~304). The metric is obtained by solving a complex Monge--Ampère equation on an affine threefold and lifting the solution to an infinite cyclic cover. Neural predictions are accepted only when they satisfy deterministic numerical safeguards, including descent, scale, and out-of-distribution requirements; otherwise, the corresponding deterministic recovery or fallback mechanism is retained. A Hausdorff space $Y$ is called rigid if, for every positive integer $k$, every continuous open $k$-to-one map $p:X\to Y$ from a Hausdorff space $X$ admits a partition of $X$ into $k$ open sets, each mapped homeomorphically onto $Y$. In $\mathsf{ZFC}$, we obtain a characterization for arbitrary limit ordinals: a limit ordinal $α$ is rigid if and only if every coherent family $\langle f_ξ:ξ<α\rangle$, where $f_ξ:ξ\to\{0,1\}$, admits a uniformization. We study the weakly singular Volterra integral equation V(t) = A - (1/Gamma(alpha)) int_0^t (t-s)^{alpha-1} h(|V(s)|) ds, t >= 0, where alpha in (0,1), A > 0 and h is a class-K function. We prove that, given a projective minimal model and a projective family of good minimal models, the subset of the base parametrizing fibers isomorphic (or birationally equivalent) to the given minimal model is constructible in the Zariski topology. Together with recent boundedness results for polarized log Calabi--Yau fibrations, this constructibility theorem provides new finiteness results predicted by the relative Kawamata--Morrison--Totaro cone conjecture.
Oisín Flynn-Connolly; José M. Moreno-Fernández; Fernando Muro

We introduce the determinant Massey product, a secondary operation on the cohomology of commutative dg algebras which is reminiscent of the classical Massey product. We prove some of the elementary properties of this product, compute several examples, and relate them to classical and matric Massey products. When 2 is invertible, a determinant Massey product is a matric Massey product, but over $\mathbb F_2$, it is not. In this case, we produce a finite-dimensional cdga whose Harrison cohomology does not inject into its Hochschild cohomology, and a divided powers algebra which is formal as an associative dg algebra, but not as a commutative one, with an explicit determinant Massey product witnessing the failure. Propagation of chaos with singular potentials: A weighted duality approach

We establish the propagation of chaos and derive the Vlasov equation from a many-body $N$-particle system in the mean-field regime with singular interaction forces bounded by $|x|^{-α-1}$ for $0\le α<(d-1)/2$ in dimensions $d\ge 2$, which in particular include the full range of sub-Coulomb interactions in three dimensions as well as the Coulomb interaction in two dimensions. Our proof is based on an energy-based framework for deriving weighted uniform bounds on cumulants that builds upon the recent duality method developed by Bresch--Duerinckx--Jabin in combination with a new Morawetz-type estimate, allowing us to remove the restriction to locally square-integrable interaction force kernels and handle more singular regimes.
Extremal spectral results of outerplanar graphs without starlike trees

A graph $G$ is $F$-free if it does not contain $F$ as a subgraph. Let $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ denote the set of $n$-vertex $F$-free outerplanar graphs with maximum spectral radius. Define $S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t)$ as the starlike tree obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint paths of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one endpoint of each path, and $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$ as the graph obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one vertex from each cycle. Fix a cyclic profile of coprime rank $r$ and level $\ell$, both at least three, and an entry bound $n\ge1$. Let $d$ be the deficit from the maximum volume of a tight cylindric partition. For $d\le n\min(r,\ell)$, the one-row combinatorial $R$ matches the tight cylinders whose last slice lies inside the maximizer's last slice with the partitions of $d$ in which each part occurs fewer than $r$ times. Let $H$ be a quasi-triangular Hopf algebra of sqaure-free dimension over $\mathbb{C}$. In this note, we show that $H$ is semisimple and cocommutative. Equivalently, a braided finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ of square-free Frobenius--Perron dimension with a fiber functor is tensor equivalent to the representation category of a finite group.

Given a symmetric matrix $A \in [-1,1]^{n \times n}$, we estimate the probability that a random principal submatrix, obtained by taking each index independently with probability $p$, is positive semidefinite. As a corollary, we show that $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ indices chosen uniformly at random suffice for testing positive semidefiniteness with squared Frobenius distance threshold $\varepsilon n^2$, thus nearly matching the lower bound of Bakshi, Chepurko, and Jayaram (``Testing Positive Semi-Definiteness via Random Submatrices'', FOCS 2020). Large-scale regularity theory for optimal $p-$transport maps and application to concentration in the matching problem

We consider the random bipartite matching problem between two independent families of uniformly distributed points in dimension three and higher, for the cost given by the $p$-th power of the distance. We show that, up to logarithmic factors, every moment of the displacement of the optimal matching is of the order of the typical interparticle distance. Wireless systems are becoming harder to operate because service goals are increasingly expressed in outcome-oriented terms, while radio platforms still expose mainly low-level configurations and protocol-specific controls. This mismatch makes it difficult to translate latency, reliability, throughput, and continuity requirements into coherent radio behavior. This article argues for Intent-Defined Radio (IDR) as a new system abstraction for next-generation wireless networks. Rather than treating the radio stack as a fixed mechanism set to be manually engineered and then tuned, IDR connects explicit service goals to executable radio behavior within a constrained design space by leveraging the capacity of large language models (LLMs). We position IDR relative to programmable radio, intent-based networking, and learning-based protocol design. We also present two simulation studies using Intent2MAC to illustrate the design loop, demonstrating executable MAC synthesis and offline refinement guided by evaluation feedback. Nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with singular viscosity

We study the nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional isentropic Navier--Stokes system with fast diffusion and singular viscosity. The waves connect a positive left state to zero specific volume at the right far field, where the density becomes unbounded and the viscous coefficient is singular. We then prove global existence and convergence to the profile for sufficiently small perturbations in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main difficulties stem from the singular nonlinear viscous term. We provide a characterization of these spaces via the $φ$-transform in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth, and establish the corresponding Sobolev embeddings. Furthermore, we obtain smooth atomic and molecular decompositions for these spaces. Our approach relies on several new maximal inequalities.

It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that every smooth ALG or ALG$^*$ gravitational instanton of type $A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3$ is, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, isometric to a rank-two wild Hitchin moduli space on $\PP^1$ with its $L^2$ metric. We compute the compact hyperkähler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems.
Collineations of the diamond lattice in a Hilbert space

Let $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ be non-trivial closed subspaces of a separable Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}$ such that $\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}=\{0\}$ and $\mathscr{M}+\mathscr{N}$ is dense in $\mathscr{H}$. We characterize when there exists an invertible operator on $\mathscr{H}$ which maps $\mathscr{M}$ onto $\mathscr{N}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ onto $\mathscr{M}$. We prove that such an operator exists if and only if $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ have a common algebraic complement. This happens if and only if either neither of the operators $(I-P)Q$ and $(I-Q)P$ is compact, or $P-Q$ is compact and $\dim(\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}^\perp)=\dim(\mathscr{M}^\perp\cap\mathscr{N})$, where $P$ and $Q$ are the orthogonal projections onto $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$. Moreover, the operator can be chosen to be an involution. Consequently, the group of collineations of the diamond lattice $\{\{0\},\mathscr{M},\mathscr{N},\mathscr{H}\}$ which fix $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ is always complemented in the group of all its collineations.
Subfactor symmetries of real Hadamard matrices

Every Hadamard matrix gives rise to a {\it spin model commuting square} and a hyperfinite subfactor with finite Jones index. The standard invariant of this subfactor is comprised of quantum symmetries of the subfactor which can be viewed as ``non-invertible'' symmetries of the Hadamard matrix. We show that if the Hadamard matrix is real and has order greater than four and congruent to four modulo eight, the standard invariant is minimal, i.e. it consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Consequently, both principal graphs of the subfactor are $A_\infty$. In particular, this holds for every Paley type II Hadamard matrix. The proof uses a congruence for products of four rows and Jones's annular decomposition. More generally, we show that if an irreducible subfactor of finite index greater than four has bounded annular multiplicities along an infinite subsequence of degrees, then its principal graph is $A_\infty$.
Finitely supported mapping classes on infinite-type surfaces

We study the topological closure of the group of mapping classes group with finite-type support on an infinite-type surface. Since every such mapping class fixes each end which is not a puncture, we have that the closure is contained in the pointwise stabilizer of infinite-type ends. A natural question is therefore when this inclusion is an equality, and if it is not, what must be added to obtain the full stabilizer. We prove that finitely supported mapping classes are dense in the stabilizer precisely when there is at most one end accumulated by genus and at most one end accumulated by punctures. We show that if we remove either of these conditions, we need to add puncture and/or handle shifts to topologically generate the stabilizer.
Uniqueness and non-uniqueness of smooth solutions to the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}$
Zipeng Chen; Song Liu; Zhaoyang Yin

We study the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb T^d$ with $d\ge2$. For every $2<q\le\infty$ and every smooth mean-zero background solution $U$, we construct two distinct mild solutions with the same initial datum arbitrarily close to $U(0)$ in $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)$, both belonging to $C([0,T];\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)) \cap C^\infty((0,T]\times\mathbb T^d)$. The time $T>0$ depends on the background solution but is independent of the prescribed tolerance for the initial data. This gives non-uniqueness for arbitrarily small initial data and density of non-unique initial data in the mean-zero divergence-free subspace of $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)$ for $2<q<\infty$. We also prove uniqueness in the same solution class for $1\le q\le2$, establishing the sharp threshold $q=2$ in this Besov scale. The uniqueness result extends to $\dot B^{-1+d/p}_{p,q}(\mathbb T^d)$ for $1\le p<\infty$ and $1\le q\le\infty$, under the same continuity and smoothness assumptions.
Operator generated topologies and the Krein property

Let $X$ be a Banach space and $Z\subseteq X^*$ a subspace separating the points of $X$. We say that $Z$ has the Krein property if the $σ(X,Z)$-closed convex hull of every norm-bounded $σ(X,Z)$-compact set is $σ(X,Z)$-compact. We show that this property passes from $Z$ to every subspace between $Z$ and its sequential weak$^*$ closure in $X^*$, and that the closed convex hulls do not change. In particular, it passes to the smallest $V^*$-invariant space $Z[V]\supseteq Z$ whenever the operator $V$ is a pointwise $σ(X,Z)$-limit of a sequence of $σ(X,Z)$-continuous operators; for nets this fails in general and holds under a double limit condition. As a source of spaces with the Krein property we show that the Mackey topologies $μ(X,Z)$ and $μ(Z,X)$ are complete if the identity of $X$ is suitably approximated by a sequence of operators whose adjoints map $X^*$ into $Z$; in particular, $μ(E^\odot,E)$ and $μ(E,E^\odot)$ are complete for every $C_0$-semigroup on a Banach space $E$ with sun dual $E^\odot$. The results are applied to the history space $\mathrm{BUC}(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ of delay equations with infinite delay, where every space of bounded measures containing $L^1(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ has the Krein property.
Criteria for memory-induced blow-up in distributed delay differential equations

This paper investigates the conditions under which solutions to distributed delay differential equations describing memory accumulation and forgetting blow up in finite time. It provides criteria for memory-induced blow-up, which means finite-time blow-up of the delayed equation while the corresponding non-delayed equation, obtained in a certain limit, has global solutions. In the author's previous work, memory-induced blow-up was shown for specific nonlinearities by means of Poincaré-type compactification, but a general theory was not established. Here, the two-dimensional ODE system derived by the linear chain trick is rewritten as an orbit equation, and a comparison theorem and an Osgood-type integral condition are applied to obtain a blow-up criterion based on the existence of a subsolution. This characterizes the nonlinearities for which memory-induced blow-up occurs. This paper also gives a necessary condition in a special case, a global existence condition based on a supersolution, and a systematic method for constructing subsolutions for separable nonlinearities. These results recover the author's previous results and are illustrated through several examples.
Unbounded Gaps Between Matrix Monotonicity and Frobenius Radial Convexity

We show that the gap between matrix monotonicity and Frobenius radial convexity can be arbitrarily large. For every integer $m\ge 2$, we construct rational functions that are matrix monotone of order $m$ but not of order $m+1$, and Frobenius radially convex of order $2m-1$ but not of order $2m$. Thus, the difference between their exact matrix-monotonicity and radial-convexity orders is $m-1$, which can be arbitrarily large. As a consequence, for every $n\ge 3$, Frobenius radial convexity of order $n$ does not imply matrix monotonicity of the same order, either increasing or decreasing.
Markov processes with jump kernels blowing up at the boundary of $C^{1, η}$ open sets
Soobin Cho; Panki Kim; Renming Song; Zoran Vondraček

We study the boundary behavior of nonnegative harmonic functions for a class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes in $C^{1,η}$ open sets $D\subset\mathbb R^d$. The jump kernels are allowed to blow up at the boundary of $D$ and the processes may have a critical killing potential. We identify the exact boundary decay exponent $p$, characterized by the coefficient of the critical killing potential. We establish a boundary Harnack principle which yields the comparability of $f(x)/δ_D(x)^p$ for nonnegative harmonic functions that vanish continuously on a portion of the boundary. The key ingredient of the proof combines estimates of the exact decay rate for the survival probability of the killed process with a modified box method and uses a regularized distance function to handle the limited boundary regularity.
k-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most one
Zihao Geng; Ji-Ming Guo; Jongyook Park

The problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most $1$ was posed by Hoffman and first studied by Cvetković in 1982. In this paper, all $k$-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most $1$ are characterized. We determine all equality cases and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $1$. For each fixed $k\geq2$, we also determine the $k$-trees attaining the largest second largest eigenvalue below $1$ and the smallest above $1$. Finally, we determine all minimal forbidden induced subgraphs among $k$-trees with $k\geq 1$, each of which has second largest eigenvalue greater than $1$, but deleting any vertex gives a graph whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $1$.
Depth of Powers of Cover Ideals of Path Ideals
Nguyen Thu Hang; Truong Thi Hien; Thanh Vu

Let $ J_t(P_n) = (x_1, \ldots, x_t) \cap \cdots \cap (x_{n-t+1}, \ldots, x_n) $ be the cover ideal of the $t$-path ideal of a path graph inside the polynomial ring $ S = K[x_1, \ldots, x_n] $ over a field $K$. For every $ n \ge t \ge 2 $ and $s \ge 2$, we prove that \[ \operatorname{depth} \left ( S/J_t(P_n)^s \right ) = q(s+1) + \left\lfloor \frac{r-1}{t} \right\rfloor, \] where $ n = q(ts + 1) + r $ with $ 1 \le r \le ts + 1 $. Our proof shows that all powers of $J_t(P_n)$ have linear quotients in increasing lexicographic order and explicitly describes the corresponding colon ideals.
Adaptive Tests of Pricing Restrictions with Observed and Latent Factors
Anlin Liu; Guowei Yan; Zhaojun Wang

This paper develops a high-dimensional test for asset pricing models with observed and latent factors. The null hypothesis allows the intercepts from an observed-factor regression to be nonzero, provided that they lie in the latent factor loading space.
