Specifically, variables and constraints are identified as complicating based on their structural role and/or their functionality (contribution to nonlinearity) in the mathematical program. The framework allows us to assess the viability of different decomposition types (variable, constraint, cross) and identify multiple potential decomposition formulations of the same type (e.g. different combinations of complicating variables for Benders decomposition). The systematic nature of our framework facilitates broader studies into the efficacy of different decompositions across a range of problems including energy markets, process design, and machine learning.
On counting integer symmetric matrices of fixed determinant in families of slant boxes

In this article, we develop an upper bound for the number of integral symmetric matrices of fixed determinant in a slant box with coefficients bounded by some given power of the volume of the slant box. We develop a counting method that expands on Shankar-Siad-Swaminathan's work on rank-3 integer symmetric matrices of fixed determinant to higher-rank matrices using geometry-of-numbers methods and invariant theory on the splitting of quadratic forms associated with the determinant formula into corresponding linear forms. We expect this generalization will allow us to apply the counting results to arithmetic statistics frameworks. In forthcoming work, we will apply the counting results to study the distribution of 2-torsion subgroups of class groups of unit-monogenised number fields.
Minimal super dominating sets of maximum cardinality
Diana Avella-Alaminos; Magdalena Lemańska; Rita Zuazua

Let $G = (V,E)$ be a graph. A subset $S \subseteq V$ of vertices is a super dominating set if every vertex $v \in V - S$ has a neighbour $u \in S$, whose only neighbour in $V - S$ is $v$. A set $S \subseteq V$ is called open irredundant if every vertex $u \in S$ has at least one neighbour $v \in V - S$ whose only neighbour in $S$ is $u$. In this paper we establish connections between super dominating sets and open irredundant sets, similar to the connections that exist between dominating sets and irredundant sets. In particular, we define the new parameter $Γ_{sp}(G)$ as the maximum cardinality of a minimal super dominating set of $G$ and calculate $Γ_{sp}(G)$ for some families of graphs $G$. Finally we present some properties of open irredundant sets and we will develop Gallai theorems involving domination, super domination and open irredundance parameters of graphs.
Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states

Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state. We show that the two formalisms are equivalent and related via spatiotemporal operator frames. In the Kirkwood-Dirac phase-space formalism, the spatiotemporal distribution and the cost function are complex-valued, and the spatiotemporal couplings are Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distributions that yield the correct marginals for the local states. In the spatiotemporal state formalism, the cost operators are generally non-Hermitian, and the spatiotemporal couplings are generally non-Hermitian and yield the correct reduced local states. The Margenau-Hill phase-space distribution gives rise to a real-valued optimal transport in spatiotemporal phase space; in the spatiotemporal state formalism, this corresponds to a Hermitian spatiotemporal coupling state. We give a rigorous definitions and a careful discussion of its duality. We also introduce a spatiotemporal quantum Wasserstein metric based on a metric in spatiotemporal phase spaces and show that it satisfies the metric axioms.
Beyond Area: Perimeter Optimization in the Planar Skorokhod Embedding Problem

The planar Skorokhod embedding problem asks for a simply connected planar domain whose Brownian exit distribution has a prescribed real marginal $μ$. We investigate the minimization of conformal perimeter over the class of all such embeddings. We first establish the main existence theorem showing that whenever a finite-perimeter embedding exists, the infimum is attained (and vice versa). We derive necessary conditions for finiteness and sufficient conditions based on logarithmic integrability of the density. In particular, we demonstrate that finite area does not guarantee the existence of an embedding with finite perimeter. Although Gross's canonical embedding minimizes area, we construct an explicit family of domains for which Brownian symmetrization strictly increases perimeter, disproving its universal perimeter minimality. On the positive side, using Pruss's containment theorem and inequalities from convex geometry, we establish a general lower bound in terms of the convex hull of the Gross domain. Consequently, whenever the Gross embedding is bounded and convex, it is the unique perimeter minimizer. Finally, we formulate an open problem concerning the relationship between the existence of finite-perimeter embeddings and the regularity of Gross's canonical embedding.
Antidirected paths on five vertices in 5-chromatic digraphs

We prove that every 5-chromatic digraph containing no copy of the regular tournament on five vertices contains both antidirected paths on five vertices. This answers a question posed by El Sahili in 2004. The proof uses an edge bound for 5-critical graphs to constrain the out-degrees in a counterexample and obtain a contradiction by constructing a proper 4-colouring.
Wasserstein Target Diagram for Model Evaluation

The target diagram is often used in geosciences, which provides a visualization tool for model evaluation and shows the temporal or spatial matching of data. However, its construction requires paired data of equal sample sizes, limiting its application to model comparisons involving unpaired samples or probability distributions. In this study, we propose the Wasserstein target diagram based on the 2-Wasserstein distance from optimal transport. Unlike the original target diagram, the Wasserstein target diagram does not require paired data of equal sizes and evaluates models from the probability distribution perspective. We further establish that the two target diagrams coincide when the given paired data are comonotone, which is common in climate science, such as cumulative precipitation and solar radiation. Through two simulation studies and an application to wind speed distribution fitting, we demonstrate that the proposed diagram can detect the probability distribution discrepancies that the original target diagram may not distinguish. The Wasserstein target diagram therefore lifts the model evaluation to the probability level and provides a complementary approach to estimating the agreement in probability distributions.
On the local boundedness of weak solutions to doubly nonlinear equations with variable exponents
Simone Ciani; Mariia O. Savchenko; Igor I. Skrypnik; Yevhen S. Zozulia

We establish local boundedness, together with quantitative estimates, for non-negative weak sub-solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear parabolic equations whose prototype is \[ (u^q)_t-\operatorname{div} \Big(|Du|^{p(x,t)-2}Du\Big)=0, \qquad p(x,t)>1,\quad q>0. \] The results are obtained under a logarithmic continuity condition on the variable exponent $p(x,t)$ and suitable relations between $q$ and the local bounds of $p(x,t)$. In certain ranges of the exponents, an additional local integrability assumption is required.
Finite regularity moduli stacks through diffeology

Diffeological non-Abelian Hodge theory motivates the study of $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and flat bundles for finite $r$. In this article, we provide a uniform language for treating moduli stacks parametrizing such objects in terms of diffeology. More specifically, we develop a theory of stacks presentable by diffeological groupoids over the site of $C^r$ manifolds for arbitrary $r$. As an application, we construct moduli stacks over the sites of $C^r$ manifolds parametrizing $C^r$ vector bundles over a smooth manifold, and $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and of flat bundles over a complex manifold. We also construct $C^r$ versions of the non-Abelian Hodge filtration stack, interpolating between Higgs bundles and flat bundles through $λ$--connections. We show that all these stacks are presentable by diffeological groupoids. Finally, we construct moduli stacks parametrizing $C^r$ families of $Δ^n$--shaped diagrams of these objects, and show that they assemble into simplicial stacks whose levels are all presentable by diffeological groupoids.
Minimax estimation for simultaneous deconvolution model in random design using wavelets

Simultaneous deconvolution model is investigated when the design points are random and follow bounded densities and errors are either $i.i.d.$ or long-memory dependent. We propose wavelet hard-thresholding estimators, and show that they achieve asymptotically near-optimal convergence rates for the $L^2$-risk when the response function belongs to Besov space under both $i.i.d.$ errors and homoskedastic, long-memory errors. However, under heteroskedastic, long-memory errors the estimator is not optimal. For the $i.i.d.$ errors, the convergence rates are {identical} to those found in simultaneous deconvolution under regular design {and $i.i.d.$ errors}. However, for long-memory dependent errors, the convergence rates are new {and completely different from those in simultaneous deconvolution under regular design and long-memory errors}.
Akram Alishahi; Kristen Hendricks; Cheuk Yu Mak

We study the behavior of Manolescu's construction of symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology under symmetries. Specifically, for k<n we construct a localization spectral sequence from the symplectic sl(n) homology of a knot to the direct sum of the symplectic sl(k) and sl(n-k) homologies of the same knot, giving a geometric analog of rank-reducing spectral sequences arising from deformations on the non-symplectic theory. We also prove the existence of a localization spectral sequence relating the symplectic Khovanov--Rozansky homology of a two-periodic link to the symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology of the quotient link, in analogy to a theorem of Seidel and Smith for symplectic Khovanov homology. The proofs rely on a generalization of the localization theorem of Seidel-Smith and Large for equivariant Lagrangian Floer cohomology with respect to order two actions; in particular, we extend the theory to the case that the fixed set of the action carries a stable normal real polarization.
Replicating chaotic dynamics from sparse sensors with recurrent latent states
Jan P. Williams; J. Nathan Kutz; Krithika Manohar

Forecasting a high-dimensional nonlinear system from a few point sensors requires an estimate of the current state and a model of its evolution. Reduced-order models usually take the full state as input, so with only sparse sensors they require an auxiliary full-state estimate whose error is inherited by the latent representation. We instead build the latent state from sensor measurements alone, using a shallow recurrent decoder (SHRED) network that encodes a history of point measurements, and train an echo state network to advance that latent state autonomously. We show that the resulting latent dynamics replicate the long-term dynamical invariants of the underlying system rather than merely tracking its short-term trajectory. For the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation, the autonomous latent model reproduces the leading Lyapunov exponents of the full system from 25 of 128 state components, using a latent state with 6-14% as many components as the full state. Because Lyapunov exponents are invariant under smooth coordinate changes, this is consistent with the recurrent encoder recovering an embedding of the attractor, in the spirit of Takens' delay embedding theorem. The recurrent encoding also decouples forecast skill from reconstruction accuracy. SHRED reconstructs less accurately than a convolutional autoencoder given the full state, yet it forecasts comparably on the simpler chaotic case and better on the more complex one. For Kolmogorov flow, with sensors at 6% of grid points and a latent state 0.3% the size of the vorticity field, the autonomous model remains on the learned latent manifold over long horizons.
The Spectral Distribution of Matrix Least Squares Solutions, and the Ellipsoid Fitting Problem
Afonso S. Bandeira; Yue M. Lu; Petar Nizić-Nikolac

We study the spectral distribution of the least squares solution to a random linear system whose unknown is a symmetric matrix. In the normalized and isotropic setting, we derive a closed-form description of the support of the spectral distribution. As an application, we consider the ellipsoid fitting problem: given $n$ standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$, does there exist a centered ellipsoid passing through all of them? It was recently shown that this problem has a sharp phase transition at $n \approx d^2/4$. On the satisfiability side, unlike earlier results, these sharp results do not rely on least squares candidates. We show that the least squares candidates considered in earlier works have a threshold of positive semi-definiteness at $n \approx d^2/10$, which was previously observed numerically and predicted non-rigorously using statistical physics methods. Moreover, we show that the corresponding least squares dual certificates have a threshold of positive definiteness at $n \approx 2d^2/5$. Our approach combines several matrix concentration tools. A key technical ingredient, which may be of independent interest, is showing that a certain kernel matrix is well-conditioned with high probability until $n \approx d^2/2$.
Evergreen leaves and universal lifetime laws in preferential-attachment trees

We study leaf lifetimes in general preferential-attachment trees. First we characterize the existence of evergreen leaves, that is, vertices that remain leaves forever. When no evergreen leaves exist, we establish, for a broad class of attachment functions, a remarkable one-parameter universality: the normalizations and limiting laws for various characteristics of leaf lifetimes depend on the attachment function only through a single numerical parameter. In particular, we obtain a shifted Pareto limit law for individual lifetimes and a joint functional limit theorem for the lifetime and label of the longest-lasting leaf. The limiting two-dimensional process, which we call the beta-decorated Fréchet extremal process, admits an elegant representation in terms of the Stoev--Taqqu extremal integral and the sets of optimal choices considered by Molchanov and Strokorb. We also establish a Poisson point-process limit for rescaled leaf lifetimes and corresponding labels, a finiteness criterion for long-lasting leaves, and a functional central limit theorem for their number at the critical threshold.
A Study of Fixed versus Adaptive Step Sizes for Phasor Dynamics Simulations
Steven B. Roberts; Luke Lowery; Slaven Peles; Adam Birchfield; Carol S. Woodward

Transient phasor dynamics simulations model the response of power systems to disturbances using differential-algebraic equations (DAEs). Fixed-step integration is widely used to solve these DAEs numerically, but a step size suitable for resolving a fault transient may be unnecessarily small during the rest of a simulation. In this work, we provide a quantitative comparison of fixed and adaptive backward differentiation formulas on a suite of seven grid test cases ranging from 200 to 70,000 buses. Adaptive step sizes automatically shrink near faults, perturbations, and controller limits, and grow during less active portions of the simulation. At the global error achieved by a fixed quarter-cycle step size, adaptive results give 1.8 to 2.6 times speedups. Local error distributions, step size profiles, and work-precision plots show how accuracy, nonlinear solver, and step selection contribute to these differences. The results establish adaptive integration as the preferred approach for these simulations.
We show pairs of posets such that the largest families not containing any of them is substantially smaller than the largest families avoiding only one of them.
Incremental Roseland: Batch-wise Landmark Diffusion via Kernelized Sequential Karhunen--Loève Update

Landmark diffusion (Roseland) computes a diffusion-map-style spectral embedding from the singular value decomposition of a degree-normalized data-to-landmark kernel matrix, at a cost far below that of full diffusion maps. It assumes, however, that all data are available at once. We introduce incremental Roseland (iRoseland), which casts the landmark affinity as a row-growing matrix whose SVD can be updated with a kernelized Sequential Karhunen--Loève (SKL) scheme. Degre correction is handled by a first order expansion about a reference mean kernel row and so that the landmark-side eigenbasis may be recovered from a single landmark-by-landmark eigendecomposition at each step. The presented method requires only a single pass over the data and runs in bounded-memory with state independent of the number of points processed. A forgetting factor lets the method track drifting distributions, and a sample-size-invariant embedding keeps outputs comparable across time. Experiments show agreement with Roseland to round-off on stationary data, and accuracy that exceeds equal-memory Roseland by an order of magnitude on long streams. On drifting data, we observe large gains from forgetting with a window matched to the drift.
On the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic

This paper gives a new path to determine all $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic, which had been done by Huang, Lai, Li and the author. The path used in this paper is based on the idea of operator generation, which originated from the work of Todd, developed by the author, and independently by Im-Kim-Ngo Dac.
Symmetry classification of hyperfine rovibrational molecular phase space
Elin Ranjan Das; Jing-Chen Zhang; Victor V. Albert; Yuan Liu

Symmetry-based structures have advanced molecular spectroscopy and quantum information science, yet connections between these fields remain largely unexplored. We construct a phase space theory of a molecule by jointly treating rotational, vibrational, and nuclear-spin degrees of freedom as the quotient of orientations and normal coordinates by the molecule's point group. The various combinations of how these three degrees of freedom transform under symmetries organize a molecule's states into molecular species, and we show that each species is defined by a particular absolutely maximally entangled (AME) carrier state, or, for 45 species, by a two-dimensional space of them. Up to local unitaries and the order of the sectors, molecular species realize 21 AME states across 75 point groups: a product state, four maximally entangled pairs, and 16 genuinely tripartite states. A Fourier transform on the quotient relates orientation and angular-momentum descriptions while preserving these carrier states. We propose an example experimental protocol for preparing and driving symmetry-adapted bend states of $\mathrm{CaOCH_3}$.
Joint extreme-value asymptotics for the radius and centre of smallest enclosing balls

We study the joint extreme-value behaviour of the radius and centre of the smallest ball containing an i.i.d.\ spherically symmetric sample. In the Gumbel and Weibull regimes, we obtain joint limit theorems and show that the enclosing ball is asymptotically supported by exactly $d+1$ sample points, thereby resolving an open support problem in the Gumbel case. In the Fréchet regime, the limit is given by the smallest enclosing ball of an extremal Poisson cloud. For planar Gaussian samples, we derive an explicit joint limit law from Daniels' finite-sample formula and show that this law is universal throughout the planar Gumbel domain. In the bounded-support Weibull regime, we additionally obtain uniform tail bounds, moment convergence and an explicit limiting density, while the uniform-ball case admits an interpretation in terms of a Poisson zero cell.
The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
Niklas Garner; Brian R. Williams; Paul-Hermann Balduf

We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng. A linear differential-graded presentation identifies the universal bulk with Chern--Simons theory near a principal nilpotent background, where holomorphic gauge gives a finite, 1-loop exact quantization. The quantum oper boundary observables form the principal affine $W$-algebra at level $k-h^\vee\hbar$; we also obtain this level shift directly for affine current algebras. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.
Exact Solutions to Matrix Models and String Theories: The Global Construction
Jasper Kager; João Rodrigues; Ricardo Schiappa; Maximilian Schwick; Noam Tamarin

Exact nonperturbative solutions to matrix models and string theories are obtained in closed-form via a discrete-Fourier/Zak-transform representation of their partition-function resurgent-transseries. Examples include all hermitian one-matrix models (paired with their topological string duals) alongside all their multicritical and minimal-string double-scaling limits. The resulting structure is resonant, necessarily including both eigenvalues (D-branes) and anti-eigenvalues (negative-tension-branes). In a complementary preceding paper these solutions were extensively verified at the local level. In order to study them globally across their phase diagrams, complete non-linear Stokes data (and corresponding connection formulae) are still needed -- all of which are obtained herein. This involves a careful study of (anti-) eigenvalue tunneling across the complete multi-sheeted structure of their associated spectral-curves, and how the result descends from multi-cut smooth-curves to single-cut singular-curves -- all of which are extensively checked via large-order analysis and matrix-integral computations. Making use of the resulting exact Stokes automorphisms, nonperturbative solutions can be fully tested, from weak-to-strong 't Hooft coupling, as well as from large-to-small N, and for any complex-values of all parameters, by correctly implementing Stokes-transitions at the crossing of all possible Stokes-lines. Several analytical and numerical tests are carried through in diverse examples covering from matrix models through non-critical strings, which produce very sharp numerical matches fully validating our exact analytical expressions. Anti-eigenvalues or negative-tension D-branes are an absolutely essential part of the story in order to find such precise agreements.
Theta-Eta Mellin Transforms, Shifted Reflections, and Rigorous Approximation Theory for a Variant Theta Construction

We develop a rigorous analytic framework for investigating a proposed functional equation associated with a variant theta construction. We prove the classical Mellin identity connecting the Jacobi kernel $1-θ_4(0\mid ix^2)$ to the completed Dirichlet eta function, and extend its Mellin transform meromorphically to the whole plane with a single simple pole at the origin. Mellin uniqueness identifies $x^{3/8}(1-θ_4(0\mid ix^2))$ as the unique kernel in a natural weighted $L^1$ class whose Mellin transform is the shifted completed eta function. We distinguish this Gaussian kernel from the weighted exponential series $Θ^B(s)=\sum_{n\geq1}ne^{-ns}$, whose Mellin transform is $Γ(s)ζ(s-1)$ and obeys a different, explicitly derived reflection relation. We show that every affine reflection $s\mapsto c-s$ can be generated for a shifted completed eta or zeta function by choosing the shift appropriately; consequently, the occurrence of $\tfrac14-s$ alone cannot identify the original variant with a shifted eta function. The corrected analytic product defined here is an elementary meromorphic multiplier of the completed zeta function and therefore has a precise $1-s$ functional equation. We prove an explicit eta-tail bound, a sharper alternating-tail asymptotic, a uniformly convergent Euler-transformed eta series with a geometric error bound, a uniform zeta-approximation bound away from the line $\Re s=1$, and a combined truncation estimate when both the zeta and weighted-exponential factors are truncated. We also determine the principal Laurent data and the cancellation of the gamma poles at the trivial zeta zeros for the corrected product. Reproducible high-precision experiments verify the stated error scales. The exact identification of the original variant with a shifted completed eta function remains open.
An Explicit Construction of Large Families of MSTD Sets

A finite set $S\subset\mathbb Z$ is more sums than differences (MSTD) if $|S+S|>|S-S|$. Yufei Zhao's bidirectional-ballot construction gives $Θ(2^N/N)$ MSTD subsets of $[0,N-1]$, the best previously known size bound for an explicit family, to the author's knowledge. We improve this bound: for every fixed integer $T\geq1$, we construct a family of $Θ_T(2^N/(\log_2^{\circ T} N)^{2^T})$ MSTD subsets, where $\log_2^{\circ T}$ denotes the $T$-fold iterated logarithm. This family is asymptotically larger than Zhao's for every fixed $T\geq1$. A subfamily of the same order of magnitude can be numbered so that any chosen member can be generated deterministically in time polynomial in $N$, without listing preceding members. As a supplementary comparison, replacing the terminal ballot rule by exhaustive fringe search gives a positive-proportion family with the same polynomial-time generation property.
CFTs with Large Virasoro Primary Gaps

We construct the first explicit examples of compact unitary bosonic full conformal field theories (CFTs) in two dimensions with a unique vacuum and an all-spin Virasoro-primary gap greater than two. Our constructions use asymmetric orbifolds of lattice CFTs built from even unimodular lattices of sufficiently large minimum norm, ensuring that no charged state lies below the desired gap. The gauged symmetries combine a common orthogonal action on the left- and right-moving currents with independent sign reversals; the latter project out the dimension-two scalar primary $\sum_i J_L^iJ_R^i$ that survives when the symmetry acts identically on both chiral halves. We prove that the gauging is anomaly-free and determine the exact gaps by analyzing the invariant untwisted spectrum and all twisted sectors. From lattices constructed using ternary quadratic-residue codes, we obtain an infinite family with gap three at $(c_L,c_R)=(p+1,p+1)$ for primes $p\ge71$ with $p\equiv23\pmod{24}$. From Barnes-Wall lattices, we obtain an infinite family with gap four at $(c_L,c_R)=(2^m,2^m)$ for odd $m\ge7$. We also obtain two additional examples, with gap three at $(c_L,c_R)=(48,48)$ and gap four at $(c_L,c_R)=(512,512)$.
On the multiplicity of crossing limit cycles of double diagonalizable piecewise linear vector fields

We consider planar piecewise linear vector fields with two zones separated by a straight line and having two diagonalizable components, which we call the \emph{double diagonalizable configuration}. In this configuration, the Poincaré half-maps correspond to separatrices of saddle points in the foliations of symmetric differential forms $ω_r(x)-ω_r(y)$, where $ω_r$ is a rational $1$-form with exactly three simple poles. Limit cycles correspond to non-diagonal intersections of two such separatrices, and the multiplicity of a limit cycle is precisely the order of contact at the intersection point. We prove that two distinct separatrices which are not nested segments of the same straight line have a contact of order at most $4$ at a diagonal point and at most $2$ at a non-diagonal point. As a consequence, we obtain that the multiplicity of limit cycles in the double diagonalizable configuration is at most two, this bound being sharp.
Veronica Bitonti; Emma Hogan; Jonathan A. Noel; Dmitry Tsarev

We introduce relative Sidorenko and relative anti-Sidorenko inequalities for oriented graphs, strengthening the corresponding well-studied notions for tournaments by allowing arbitrary host graphs. An orientation $\vec H$ of a graph $H$ is relatively Sidorenko if $\hom(\vec H,\vec G) \ge 2^{-e(H)}\hom(H,G)$ for every oriented graph $\vec G$ with underlying graph $G$, and relatively anti-Sidorenko if the reverse inequality holds. We provide a complete characterisation of the class of connected relatively Sidorenko graphs in terms of weakly norming graphs, and exhibit several families of relatively Sidorenko and relatively anti-Sidorenko oriented graphs. Despite the substantially stronger definitions, many known tournament Sidorenko and anti-Sidorenko examples satisfy the relative inequalities, suggesting a broader theory of these phenomena in arbitrary host graphs and motivating several new structural and classification problems.
An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization

In this paper, we study a class of constrained convex finite-sum optimization problems. In many practical applications, all or some of the constraints are hard constraints that represent imperative requirements. Consequently, any desirable approximate solution must (nearly) satisfy these constraints. Motivated by this, we focus on computing an $ε$-$surely\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ ($ε$-SFSO) solution, in which the constraint violation is deterministically bounded by $ε$, and the expected optimality gap is at most $ε$. While a recently proposed stochastic variance-reduced first-order penalty method can compute an $ε$-SFSO solution, there remains a significant gap between its first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution and that for computing an $ε$-$expected\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ solution, where both the expected constraint violation and the expected optimality gap are bounded by $ε$. To narrow this gap, we propose an inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient (SVRG) method that significantly improves the previously best-known first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution. Furthermore, when the objective consists of a single function, the proposed method reduces to a novel deterministic first-order method for solving standard convex conic optimization. It achieves a significantly lower gradient evaluation complexity with respect to the objective function compared to existing methods, and can outperform them when computing constraint gradients and projections onto the associated cone is cheaper than evaluating the objective gradient. Preliminary numerical results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.
Asymptotics of Gibbs Posterior Measures on Infinite-Dimensional Hypothesis Spaces

We prove almost sure contraction rates and consistency for Gibbs posterior measures on arbitrary hypothesis spaces, in general infinite dimensional, under dependent data, nonadditive and time-dependent losses and learning rates, misspecified models, and unattainable minimisers of the limiting objective. In particular, we develop a novel proof approach in contraction rate theory by studying the asymptotics of Gibbs measures through Lorentz spaces, real interpolation theory, and Laplace transforms dispensing with testing or variational formulations which are unavailable in the considered generality. As a consequence we obtain almost sure contraction rates for dominated Bayes and fractional Bayes posterior measures in the same generality, extending existing theory on misspecified Bayesian inference. Furthermore, we demonstrate our theoretical results on novel applications to Gibbs posteriors for Dirichlet process priors with a nonadditive Wasserstein metric loss function under ergodic, non-Markovian observables.
Non-homogeneous parabolic conormal boundary problem with singular-degenerate coefficients

We study non-homogeneous conormal boundary value problems for a class of divergence-form parabolic equations whose volumetric heat-capacity coefficients belong to a Muckenhoupt class of weights. Consequently, the equations exhibit singular, degenerate, or simultaneously singular-degenerate behavior. Under smallness conditions on the partial mean oscillation of the diffusion coefficients and the weighted mean oscillation of the volumetric heat-capacity coefficient, we establish regularity estimates, existence, and uniqueness results in appropriate weighted Sobolev spaces. To obtain these results, we employ the level-set argument introduced by Caffarelli and Peral. We also establish weighted parabolic cylinders, weighted inequalities, and a weighted Aubin-Lions compactness theorem, which are essential tools in our analysis.
Circular Vector Tomography with Partial Radial Data

In this article, we introduce and study several generalized circular Radon transforms acting on smooth vector fields compactly supported in a planar annulus, with centers restricted to the outer acquisition circle and truncated measurement radii. The operators of interest are the longitudinal and transverse circular Radon transforms and their weighted analogues. We characterize the kernels of the individual unweighted transforms. Then we establish the reconstruction of a vector field from the combined longitudinal and transverse circular Radon transform data. We further show that the pairs formed by each transform and its weighted analogue is not sufficient for the complete recovery of a vector field. However, we demonstrate that full reconstruction is possible with suitable additional data. Finally, we numerically implement and validate the derived inversion formulas.
Multifractal analysis of Takagi-type functions built from beta-expansion cylinders

We study a family of Takagi functions obtained by placing a normalized tent on each beta-expansion cylinder, with amplitude $β^{-αn}$ at order $n$, where $β>1$ and $0<α\le1$. We characterize their pointwise Hölder regularity in terms of cylinder lengths and distances from the point under consideration. The characterization holds more generally for nested interval partitions with exponentially decreasing mesh, without requiring interval lengths at a given order to be comparable. For beta-expansion cylinders, we compute the full multifractal spectrum whenever the remainders of the expansion of $1$ have a finite upper exponential decay rate. The functions are monofractal when this rate vanishes, as it does for Parry, Pisot and Salem bases. When it is positive, the spectrum is affine on a nondegenerate interval. The bases defined by $\sum_{k\ge0}β_\ell^{-\ell^k}=1$, for integers $\ell\ge2$, give explicit non-monofractal examples. We also prove that every function in the family is nowhere differentiable.
Global genetic inference at the scale of mass disasters
Youri Weesie; Ritsaart Bergsma; Aafko Boonstra

DNA-based disaster victim identification is commonly performed sequentially, with matches accepted before all genetic evidence is considered jointly. However, early matches may be incorrect or inconsistent with the globally most likely assignment, and treating them as final can affect subsequent identifications. Joint analysis avoids this dependence on decision order, but combinatorial growth has historically made it prohibitive in large cases. In this paper, we show that the general joint identification problem is NP-hard and develop a local-to-global framework for joint genetic inference at scale. We reduce the search using genetic compatibility tests, likelihood-based pruning of unlikely assignments, and symmetry reductions. We represent pedigree likelihoods as polynomials and reformulate the Elston-Stewart algorithm for efficient parallel likelihood evaluation on GPUs. Together, these advances yield a manageable set of candidate assignments and their likelihoods, from which we construct an integer linear program that resolves competing identifications and determines the global maximum-likelihood assignment. In small benchmarks, the method recovers the exhaustive-search optimum with up to 99.96% fewer likelihood evaluations. We also apply it to simulated disasters involving up to 10 thousand victims and missing persons. The framework is not limited to a single global optimum but yields a list of probable alternative assignments, thus providing a flexible tool to be used alongside other forensic evidence.
Second-class particle in ASEP. Rarefaction fan

We study the asymptotic behavior of a second class particle in ASEP on the integer lattice. We prove a general formula for the distribution of its position at any fixed time for arbitrary initial conditions. As a first application, we obtain its limiting distribution for arbitrary initial conditions in the rarefaction fan case, generalizing the result of Cator--Pimentel from TASEP to ASEP.
Guy Blachar; Jonathan Hermon; Justin Salez

We prove the long-predicted equivalence between the cutoff phenomenon and the product condition along any sequence of abelian random walks whose inverse transition probabilities grow at most logarithmically with the size of the group. Our result does not require reversibility, and comes with a sharp quantitative estimate on the mixing window. Moreover, we show that our sparsity restriction is optimal by constructing abelian Cayley graphs which satisfy the product condition but fail to exhibit cutoff, and whose degrees are arbitrarily close to being logarithmic in the volume.
Emmie Fitz-Gibbon; Maximilian Jerdee; Yuanzhao Zhang; Rosemary Braun; Cristopher Moore

Many dynamical systems unfold on networks of nodes coupled by edge interactions. This work is motivated by the following question: can we remove most edges from a networked dynamical system without significantly altering its behavior? For a given network, our goal is to find a sparser network that approximately preserves the dynamics on the nodes. We first study linear diffusion, where node values evolve according to the graph Laplacian. The dominant network sparsification method, effective resistance sampling, preserves all Laplacian eigenvalues within a uniform multiplicative bound. We show that with a limited edge budget, this is dynamically inefficient: diffusion is dominated by the slowest-decaying modes, so enforcing a uniform guarantee spends edges on fast modes that barely affect long-term dynamics. Based on this observation, we derive Diffusion Spectral Error (DSE), which evaluates in closed form the typical error in trajectories between the original and sparsified graphs over random initial conditions. Minimizing this error, which naturally prioritizes slow modes, yields sparse networks explicitly designed to preserve dynamics. At the same sparsification levels, DSE sparsification often preserves diffusion dynamics with several-fold lower error than effective resistance sampling, and up to two orders of magnitude lower on strongly modular networks. Although derived in a linear context, we empirically find that DSE sparsification gives similar improvements in the Kuramoto model (a nonlinear system of coupled oscillators), where DSE sparsification approximately preserves the synchronization threshold and, at strong coupling, order-parameter trajectories.

We give a generating function for the V-toothpick sequence and an algorithm that computes any term in time polynomial in the number of binary digits of its index. We determine its quadratic growth and periodic fluctuations, and give convergent series for the constants in its asymptotic bounds.
Congruence Patterns in Spectral Gaps of mod $p$ Markoff Graphs

We establish lower bounds on the second-largest eigenvalue of mod $p$ Markoff graphs for three infinite, positive-density families of primes $p$, each defined by congruence conditions. These lower bounds arise from the structure of integral orbits on Markoff-type surfaces over certain number fields, and are strong enough to establish that $$\liminf_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv1\pmod{4}}}λ_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.875> 2\sqrt{2},$$ partially proving a conjecture of de Courcy-Ireland and Lee, and that $$\limsup_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv 3\pmod{4}}}(λ_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.835 > 2\sqrt{2},$$ disproving another conjecture of the same.
A bordism perspective on ends of manifolds

We refine the classical pro-homotopy type of the end of a manifold by recording the boundaries of a compact exhaustion together with the bordisms between them. We show that this assignment, the bordism-end, is functorial in embeddings, and independent of the choice of exhaustion. Its target is the free sequential colimit completion of the bordism $\infty$-category. Along the way of defining the bordism-end, we show that the category of all smooth $d$-dimensional manifolds and embeddings is formally obtained from the analogous category of compact manifolds. Through the formalism of the bordism-end, it follows that a manifold is diffeomorphic to the interior of a compact manifold if and only if its bordism-end is representable. Moreover, this formalism yields a fibre sequence relating the classifying spaces of the compactly supported diffeomorphism group of a manifold and its full diffeomorphism group, and a space of bordism-ends. Finally, we set up the pro-end functorially in embeddings, with target the cospan $\infty$-category of pro-spaces, and show that it factors through the bordism-end.

Let $G$ be a plane graph with vertex, edge, and region sets $V(G),$ $E(G),$ and $F(G)$ respectively, and let $Γ$ be a nontrivial abelian group with identity element $0$. A $Γ$-zonal labeling of a plane graph $G$ is a labeling $\ell: V(G)\rightarrow Γ\setminus\{0\}$ such that for every region $f\in F(G)$, the sum of labels on the boundary of $f$ is $0$ in $Γ$. We say a $Γ$-zonal labeling is generative if the labels used generate $Γ$, and strong if the additive order of each label matches the degree of the corresponding vertex. Given a graph $G$ or a family of graphs $\mathcal{G}$, we explore restrictions on the groups $Γ$ for which there can exist a $Γ$-zonal labeling. Here we specifically determine restrictions on compatible groups when $\mathcal{G}$ is the family of $2$-connected multigraphs or $2$-connected simple graphs. We also demonstrate how the Smith normal form decomposition of the face incidence matrix of a plane graph $G$ can help characterize the groups $Γ$ for which there exists a generative $Γ$-zonal labeling.
Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from infinitesimal gradings

We develop a theory of infinitesimal gradings for $\mathbb{Z}/2$-graded $A_\infty$-categories and use it to detect Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from quantum cohomology. The dimensions we find agree with predictions from Serre functors of Kuznetsov components, such as $2$ for Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds and the fractional value $\frac{n-2}{n}$ for the symplectic Grassmannian $\operatorname{IG}(2,2n)$. An infinitesimal grading induces endomorphisms on cohomological morphism spaces, and we prove a straightening theorem that realizes its weights as an actual grading compatible with the $A_\infty$-structure. We use this grading to show that Dehn twists give faithful braid group representations in the symplectic mapping class groups of Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds.
A Normal Form for Invertible Semilinear Maps and the Category of Isocrystals Over a Finite Field

For a field $L$, and a finite order automorphism $σ$, we classify invertible $σ$-semilinear endomorphisms on finite-dimensional $L$-vector spaces up to equivalence. This is deduced as a consequence of a description, in terms of certain norm equations in finite extensions of $L$, of the semilinear Schur indices for the group $\mathbb{Z}$ acting on $L$ via $σ$. As an application, we give an explicit description of the category of isocrystals over a finite field.
Global strong solutions and large-time behavior for the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson system with general bulk viscosity and Navier slip boundary conditions

The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system with Navier slip boundary conditions is established in a smooth bounded domain that may be multiply connected. Arbitrarily large initial data and vacuum are allowed, and the positive doping profile may have large spatial variations. The bulk viscosity satisfies a logarithmic derivative bound and a growth condition on its primitive, including every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with a logarithmic gain larger than one half. Time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponential convergence to the nonconstant hydrostatic state are obtained. For strictly positive initial density, uniform positivity and exponential convergence to the hydrostatic state in higher Sobolev norms are proved. An initial vacuum point persists and causes exponential growth of density gradients.
General curves on smooth quadric hypersurfaces

We prove a sharp existence theorem for non-degenerate maps from a general curve to a smooth quadric hypersurface, deforming in a smooth family of expected dimension. Along the way, we prove that if a general curve in projective space lies on a quadric (as dictated by the Maximal Rank Conjecture, now a theorem of E. Larson), then a general such quadric is smooth.
$\ell^p$-Improving for Discrete Fractional Integrals and Averages on the Moment Curve

We prove the $\ell^p$-improving estimates in the full range for discrete fractional integral operators on the moment curve (except at the endpoint) and discrete averages on the moment curve (with $N^ε$-losses). This follows via essentially sharp Diophantine solution counting estimates for inhomogeneous Vinogradov systems with an odd number of variables.

We prove that every real polynomial $p$-harmonic function on $\Rn$ is affine when $n\ge3$ and $p\ge n-1/13$. The proof uses the Bernstein--Szegő inequality on great circles and a deficit estimate at the first Chebyshev node.
Inverse Boundary Value Problems for a Coupled Semilinear Klein-Gordon System
Parveen Kumar; Soumen Senapati; Manmohan Vashisth

This article addresses the coefficient identification inverse problem for a coupled nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation with cubic nonlinearity. More precisely, we consider a coupled nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation in a bounded cylinder contained in $\mathbb{R}^{1+\ell}$, where $ \ell\geq 2$, and establish the unique recovery of the time-independent coefficients appearing in both the zeroth-order perturbation and nonlinearity term from both full and partial boundary measurements of the solution. The unique recovery of zeroth-order coefficients is obtained via first-order linearization; however, the nonlinearity coefficients are recovered using the higher-order linearization. Finally using the unique continuation principle, we establish the unique identification of the coefficients from the partial boundary measurements of the solution.
The Bessis Moussa Villani conjecture in finite von Neumann algebras
Liviu Paunescu; Florin Radulescu; Andreas Thom

We prove the Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture, which is known for matrix algebras, for bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state. Following the approach of Heinavaara, for a pair of positive operators, we construct a tracial joint spectral measure on the punctured plane whose moments are the traces of symmetrized words. We construct a scalar measure by holomorphic spectral selection and a Lyapunov identity. An integral identity for its moments then gives positivity of two coordinate-weighted distributions. From these we obtain the planar measure and the Laplace representation of the trace exponential.
Tropicalization and slow manifolds: A case study of the Michaelis--Menten reaction

We present a case study of a recently developed approach to multiple-scale systems based on exponential scaling and tropicalization (Kristiansen and Sarantaris, \emph{On a tropicalization of planar polynomial ODEs}). Parameters and variables are scaled exponentially with respect to a small parameter $ε$, so that orders of magnitude become a genuine non-smooth singular limit $ε\to 0$. Tropical geometry, via subdivisions of the Newton polygon, classifies the asymptotic regimes and locates the candidates for slow manifolds on all scales of the variables simultaneously. Here we combine this framework with blow-up and geometric singular perturbation theory. {In particular,} the non-smooth singular limit is resolved by spherical and cylindrical blow-ups, and degeneracies caused by exponentially small terms with flat contact are treated by adding the exponential quantities as new variables {(following Kristiansen, \emph{Blowup for flat slow manifolds})}. As the case study, we take the Michaelis--Menten reaction. The tropical classification yields three asymptotic regimes of parameters. In two of these, we find a sequence of blowups and desingularizations where the system has a {global} normally hyperbolic critical manifold on the blown up space. In the remaining case, we obtain a similar result, but only for a subcase. In particular, there is an asymptotic regime of parameters where there is no global slow manifold of the Michaelis--Menten reaction.
Optimal Min-Entropy Estimation with High Probability

Min-entropy plays a fundamental role in assessing the unpredictability of randomness sources. In particular, NIST SP 800-90B specifies min-entropy estimation as a key procedure for entropy sources used in cryptographic random bit generators, illustrating the practical importance of reliable min-entropy estimation. In this paper, we settle the sample complexity of min-entropy estimation with high probability in both the classical and quantum cases. Specifically, for min-entropy estimation with additive error $\varepsilon$ and probability at least $1-δ$, the sample complexity is $Θ(d\log(d/δ)/\varepsilon^2)$ for classical distributions on $d$ symbols and $Θ((d^2+d\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon^2)$ for quantum states on a $d$-dimensional Hilbert space. Our results admit short and simple proofs.
Derandomized Sunflowers and Radical Lower Bounds
Bruno Cavalar; Théo Borém Fabris; Partha Mukhopadhyay; Srikanth Srinivasan; Amir Yehudayoff

Robust Sunflower lemmas imply that any large enough monotone DNF of width $w$ contains a sunflower, i.e., a DNF equivalent to the conjunction of a common core with a DNF that is heavily biased towards $1$. While these lemmas are typically proved in the context of the uniform distribution or i.i.d. distributions, they also hold for $O(w^2)$-wise independent distributions by Bazzi's theorem (Bazzi (SICOMP 2009); Tal (CCC 2017)), which states that width-$w$ DNFs cannot distinguish between such distributions and the uniform distribution. We prove a derandomization of robust sunflower lemmas for $O(w)$-wise independent distributions, which recovers the derandomization above with slightly weaker parameters. Notably, our result also holds for distributions whose marginals are "locally independent" and "approximately identically" distributed. It is not known whether such distributions fool general DNFs, which makes the derandomization via DNF-fooling techniques unavailable. Our proof of this derandomization is via the method of moments, which might be of independent interest. We apply this result to obtain improved separations between non-monotone arithmetic circuits and the radical of monotone circuits. Specifically, we construct an explicit family of multilinear polynomials $P_n$ that have small non-monotone arithmetic circuits such that any power of $P_n$ cannot be computed by monotone arithmetic circuits of sub-exponential size. This improves on a recent result of Cavalar, Fabris, Mukhopadhyay, Srinivasan and Yehudayoff (STOC 2026), who proved a non-explicit separation that was quasipolynomial. Our construction uses Nisan-Wigderson designs with an additional linear-algebraic expansion property.
Holomorphic Vector Bundles on the Quantum Projective Line
Paolo Aschieri; Masoud Khalkhali; Giovanni Landi

We study Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting for holomorphic vector bundles on the quantum projective line in the Dolbeault-module framework. We prove that every polynomial holomorphic bundle admitting a finite filtration by standard line objects is a direct sum of standard lines, with uniquely determined splitting integers. The proof uses a Dolbeault differential graded category and the two-arrow Kronecker quiver. For a three-parameter rank-two extension family, we determine the splitting types and distinguish the nonzero splitting strata by the determinant of a quantum connecting map. For general non-diagonal rank-two connections, we derive noncommutative Riccati equations for invariant graph submodules and formulate the global splitting problem in terms of holomorphic projectors. We also discuss twisted positive Hochschild cocycles and formulate a variational principle and a conformal-stability conjecture. On the algebraic side, we explain why both the bare sheaf category of the quantum projective line and the Artin--Zhang category of the quantum plane inherit classical Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting. We distinguish these results from unrestricted standard-line splitting, which fails for polynomial gauges, and outline a differential quantum GAGA programme with explicit attention to regularity and equivariance.
Riemannian geometry and quantum gravity on trees

We show that the tree graphs that admit a quantum Riemannian geometry (QRG) with a positive ratio metric are exactly the Dynkin graphs of finite type $A,D,E$ and affine type $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$. A metric in this context is an assignment of a nonzero real value to each arrow and positive ratio requires that the two directions on any edge have the same sign. It turns out that the metric value in one direction can be chosen freely and the other is then determined. For finite $A, D, E$ type, the construction involves $q$-integers where $q=e^{\imathπ/h}$ with $h$ the Coxeter number and there is a conjugate pair of $*$-preserving quantum Levi-Civita connections (QLCs). In the case of type $A$, these are necessarily contained in a previously known 1-parameter space of connections. For affine $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$ type, there is only one QLC, with real coefficients. Using the quantum Riemannian geometry, we construct a natural Einstein--Hilbert action and hence new quantum gravity models on $A_3,D_4,\widetilde D_4,\widetilde D_5,\widetilde D_6,\widetilde E_6$ in a functional integral approach, other than the 4-star $\widetilde D_4$ which we revisit.
An algorithm for solving structured problems involving $L$-infimal convolutions
Cong Bang Vu; Xuan Nham Vu

We develop an operator-splitting framework for solving structured minimization problems involving linear compositions of $L$-infimal convolutions. We introduce a primal-dual shadow Douglas-Rachford splitting method and establish its convergence. As a result, we derive a fully primal-dual splitting algorithm for the class of the aforementioned minimization problems.
Sparse optimal control for a class of infinite-dimensional bilinear systems: optimality conditions and uniqueness

We study optimal control of an evolution equation in which a scalar control multiplies a bounded operator acting on the state, with free dynamics given by a $C_0$-semigroup. The cost combines tracking terms, a quadratic control cost and an $L^1$ term promoting sparsity in time. We prove existence, derive optimality conditions, and show that optimal controls are thresholded functions of a switching function whose derivative is governed by the commutator of the drift and control operators. Consequently, commuting problems with a terminal cost admit no temporally sparse controls. The $L^1$ term also matters for uniqueness: two distinct controls satisfying the optimality conditions differ on a set of measure bounded from below, contained in the union of their supports, which yields, for the first time, uniqueness for every horizon in stable problems steered to zero. Second-order sufficient conditions and experiments on a bilinear heat equation complete the study.
New bounds on simplex-avoiding sets in two dimensions
Domonkos Czifra; Ákos Dúcz; Péter Madarasi; Dániel Varga; Pál Zsámboki

We study extremal densities of measurable subsets of metric spaces avoiding prescribed finite geometric configurations. We prove two new upper bounds for three-point avoidance problems: a measurable subset of $S^2$ containing no orthonormal basis has normalized spherical measure at most $7/11$, and a measurable subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ containing no unit equilateral triangle has upper Banach density at most $9/16$. The first bound appears to be the first improvement over the trivial averaging bound for this problem, while the second improves the previously best known upper bound. The proofs are applications of the geometric fractional chromatic number method introduced by Ambrus et al. For this purpose, we formulate the method in a framework that applies both to compact homogeneous spaces and to Euclidean spaces with upper Banach density.
A Two-Spectrum Deterministic Equivalent for Random Skew-Kernel Matrices

Rank-one perturbations of the mean characteristic polynomial of a random skew-kernel matrix assign a positive spatial weight to each root. For independent centered isotropic rows, the resulting response tracks the sample almost surely against each deterministic spatial test, uniformly over positive scales and arbitrary inputs, exactly when row energies concentrate on common projections of proportional rank. Directional absolute first moments determine this condition. The determinant Jensen gap controls the spatial response in every real orthonormal basis. For identity spatial covariance, logarithmic derivatives of the mean determinant give the temporal weights of the row energies it detects. Flat kernels of one prescribed rank suffice to test the row condition. A scalar equation in the two input spectra approximates the matrix response of the roots within $4/d$ in normalized trace norm. A varying ordinary response and the same-scale overlap of independent samples recover both input laws up to reciprocal rescaling, with Lipschitz stability of the relative spatial parameter and an optimal logarithmic modulus for the compactified laws on intervals of positive variation. Brownian area gives explicit spatial half-Cauchy mixtures.
Regularity of solutions to complex Monge-Ampère equations in big classes

We study the non-pluripolar complex Monge-Ampère equation in an arbitrary big class on a compact Kähler manifold. Under a weighted Laplacian lower bound on the log density, we obtain local $C^{2,α}$ regularity on the part of the ample locus where the data satisfy the stated hypotheses. A second criterion based on a quasi-plurisubharmonic decomposition gives similar regularity. In particular, a smooth positive density gives a smooth solution on the ample locus. None of these regularity results require nefness of the background class, resolving positively a question of Dinew, Guedj, and Zeriahi.
Zero mode surface of Hermitian two-by-two matrices

We classify the zero mode surfaces, also called Clifford spectra, of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices. Using the covariance of the Dirac operator under the Euclidean group and its invariance under unitary conjugation, together with a singular value decomposition, every $m$-tuple of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices, after adjoining zero matrices if $m<3$, is reduced to the normal form $(b_1σ_1,b_2σ_2,b_3σ_3,0,\dots,0)$ with $b_1\geq b_2\geq b_3\geq 0$. Since adding a vanishing matrix only embeds the Clifford spectrum into a higher-dimensional space, it suffices to consider three matrices. In this normal form the determinant of the Dirac operator is given in closed form and its critical points are determined explicitly. The zero mode surface consists of one or two points if $b_3=0$. Otherwise it consists of two disjoint topological spheres if $b_1>b_2+b_3$, of two topological spheres touching at one point if $b_1=b_2+b_3$, and of a single topological sphere if $b_1<b_2+b_3$. The topology is thus governed by the triangle inequality for $(b_1,b_2,b_3)$, which can be interpreted with Heron's formula. In particular, the Clifford spectrum of any tuple of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices is never empty.
The Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem

In a previous paper, the authors established the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem, which generalizes the Stone-von Neumann Theorem in quantum mechanics and yields a classification of all unitary Heisenberg representations of an abelian elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system up to unitary equivalence. In this sequel to that paper, we establish an infinitesimal version of the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem in the setting of real elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical systems. Firstly, we generalize Stone's Theorem to secure a one-to-one correspondence between the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups and the regular self-adjoint densely defined operators on a Hilbert $ C^{\ast} $-module. Secondly, we define the infinitesimal Heisenberg representations and the infinitesimal Schrödinger representation of a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system. Thirdly, we construct a one-to-one correspondence between the unitary Heisenberg representation and the infinitesimal Heisenberg representations of a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system, providing a rigorous two-way passage--which we call ``Heisenberg differentiability-integrability''--between the global unitary formulation of Heisenberg covariance and its infinitesimal formulation in terms of regular self-adjoint densely defined operators. This allows us to prove the Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem: For a real elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system, every infinitesimal Heisenberg representation is a direct sum of copies of the infinitesimal Schrödinger representation. Lastly, we obtain explicit descriptions of the position and momentum operators for a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system and construct a natural common invariant core of analytic vectors for them. All requisite technical domain and integrability issues are fully accounted for.
Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
Haihan Zhang; Wendao Wu; Chenheng Zhang; Chunyuan Zheng; Yanyi Li; Cong Fang; Haoxuan Li; Zhouchen Lin

Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization. Here, the central question is how efficiently a problem class can be solved through a prescribed information interface and what costs no admissible algorithm can avoid. The gap between achievable guarantees and unavoidable limits defines the frontier recorded in its Complexity Atlas, a living map of frontier settings and the current state of knowledge. Self-Organization turns unresolved gaps into adaptive research programmes, coordinating conjecture formation, mathematical investigation, and replanning as evidence accumulates. Adversarial Co-Ascent develops algorithms and hard families through reciprocal challenge, exposing mechanisms of information use and concealment that guide stronger methods and proofs of unavoidable costs. Independent review and Lean-based formal certification check mathematical claims, while the Long-Term Memory carries supported findings and research experience across settings. To date, Colombo has established optimal or near-optimal rates for more than fifty settings in the Atlas. Colombo thus takes a concrete step toward Autopoietic Science: a scientific process whose validated advances regenerate the conditions of its own progress, continually reshaping how inquiry is organized and what it can discover.
Divisible design graphs from a construction of antipodal distance-regular graphs based on Ree groups and Suzuki groups
Bart De Bruyn; Sergey Goryainov; Yilin Xie

In this paper, we present a new construction of divisible design graphs with new parameters, obtained by plugging a difference set into a known construction of antipodal distance-regular graphs of diameter 3 that is based on Ree groups and Suzuki groups.
Well-posedness of compressible $2D$ nonlinear transport equations and quasiconformal maps
Juan Carlos Cantero; Albert Clop; Daniel Faraco; David Horas; Joan Mateu; Joan Orobitg; Banhirup Sengupta

We prove uniqueness of solutions to a class of nonlinear transport equations in the plane, for which the velocity field is obtained as the convolution of the classical Cauchy kernel with the unknown. Even though the initial datum is bounded and compactly supported, the velocity field may have unbounded divergence. The proof relies on the theory of quasiconformal mappings.
First Order Geometry of Equilateral Small Polygons
José Ayala Hoffmann; Tomás Ayala Coppola

We develop a first order calculus based on the geometry of realised diameter graphs for perimeter maximisation among convex equilateral small polygons. Polygon side equalities and active diameter constraints define a linearised feasible cone and an associated equality space. We prove that an equilateral small polygon is a strict local maximiser of perimeter modulo Euclidean motions if a multiplier balance holds with strictly positive active diameter multipliers and the active equality space consists only of infinitesimal Euclidean motions. The proof uses a local Euclidean slice and a geometric limiting argument and requires neither independence of the active constraint gradients nor second order information. As an application, we combine our criterion with validated interval arithmetic to establish strict local maximality for Bingane and Audet's polygons $A_{16}$, $A_{32}$, $A_{64}$ and for reconstructions of their polygons $Z_{32}$ and $Z_{64}$. For each $n\in\{32,64\}$, the perimeter of $Z_n$ is strictly larger than that of $A_n$. Thus, strict local maximisers with different perimeters coexist in the space of convex equilateral small polygons with the same number of sides.
Associative Log Rings and their Bimodules
Deik van der Horst; Tommy Lundemo

We propose a definition of associative log rings. The role of the commutative monoid is replaced by a variant of a crossed module whose source is a monoid, and we use the resulting group action to control the failure of commutativity. This extends the classical notion of a log ring, even in the commutative case. Natural examples include algebras of logarithmic differential operators. The definition lends itself to a canonical construction of a log enveloping algebra and hence of log bimodules, and we prove that the resulting second log Hochschild cohomology group classifies log square-zero extensions. Along the way, we complete the logarithmic analog of Quillen's classification of abelian group objects in augmented algebras: In exact augmented associative log rings, abelian group objects recover log bimodules. Our constructions enjoy animated analogs, and we develop the basic theory of associative animated log rings \emph{en route} to our classification of exact log square-zero extensions.
Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian

We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$. As an application, we prove a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant.

We show that, for every $\infty$-topos $\mathcal{X}$, the profinite shape induces a canonical equivalence between the $\infty$-category of pro-objects in locally constant constructible sheaves of anima in $\mathcal{X}$ and the slice $\infty$-category of profinite anima over the profinite shape $\widehatΠ_{\infty}(\mathcal{X})$. We deduce this profinite shape equivalence from the monodromy classification theorem by establishing a continuous version of the straightening-unstraightening equivalence for profinite anima. In addition, we explain how the monodromy classification theorem recovers its classical counterparts concerning locally constant sheaves of finite sets and of (abelian) groups.
Large diameter growth for vortex patches
Junhong Fan; Dengjun Guo; Xiaoyutao Luo

For every $N>0$, the 2D incompressible Euler equation admits a smooth, simply connected vortex patch initially contained in the unit disk whose diameter exceeds $N$ at some finite time. We discover a point-vortex mechanism in which a bounded motion of three equal positive vortices drives a passive particle outward through successive transitions. A finite-time point-vortex approximation transfers the resulting separation to a single simply connected patch.
Identifiability of latent variable models with flexible latent distributions

Latent variable models are popularly used to characterize dependence among many observed variables through underlying latent variables. Recent advances in statistics and machine learning methods have encouraged growing interest in studying latent variable models with flexible latent distributions that capture complex latent structures. This flexibility, however, raises a fundamental question of whether model parameters can be identified when the latent distribution is unknown and must itself be learned. In this paper, we show that exact identifiability fails almost everywhere, in the sense that distinct but arbitrarily close pairs of model parameters and latent distributions can yield exactly the same distribution for the observed variables. Nonetheless, the resulting identification ambiguity is small. In particular, we prove that the identification ambiguity, measured by the diameter of the set of parameters inducing the same marginal distribution, vanishes at a superpolynomial rate of $\exp\{-c(\log p)^2\}$ as the number of observed variables $p$ grows. Building on this result, we show that the failure of exact identifiability need not preclude consistent estimation or valid inference of the model parameters and latent distribution. These results suggest that, when many variables are observed, the identifiability issue is far less of an obstacle to estimation and inference in latent variable models than is commonly expected.
Compensation Formulas for Branching Lévy Processes

This paper aims to establish two compensation formulas for branching Lévy processes. The first expresses expected sums over spatial jumps as integrals against the Lévy measure, with the future family of the jumping particle started from its position immediately after the jump. The second expresses expected sums over reproduction events as time integrals weighted by the branching rate and the offspring distribution, with each event marked by the ordered tuple of branching processes initiated by its offspring. Combined with the fixed-time many-to-one formula, it recovers the whole-tree many-to-one identity for functionals of ancestral spatial paths.
Mukhiddin Ismoilov; Zhiqiang Li; Karim Rakhimov; Chengliang Tan

We prove Conjectures~3 and~8 of Sendov's 2002 survey and deduce Conjecture~9. More precisely, let $p$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. For every integer $s$ with $1\le s<n$, we prove that each zero of $p$ lies within distance $2s/(s+1)$ of a zero of $p^{(s)}$. For quartics, we obtain the sharp bound $2/\sqrt3$ for the second derivative and determine all polynomials attaining it.
Finite element nonlinear nudging for the Navier-Stokes equations
Elizabeth Carlson; Rui Fang; Ali Pakzad

Nonlinear nudging augments the classical linear nudging (continuous data as- similation) term with a nonlinear feedback that strengthens as the observed error decreases, and yields super-exponential convergence to the true state. In this paper, we study nonlinear nudging for the 3-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with the finite element method, which allows complex geometries and physical boundary conditions. We propose an implicit-explicit (IMEX) finite element scheme with inf-sup stable elements, prove its unconditional long-time stability, and show for the spatially semi-discrete scheme that the error reaches a prescribed tolerance in finite time. Our analysis also suggests that the non- linear nudging term requires the mesh resolution to be fine enough (${χ= O(H^{-1})}$, where $χ$ is the nonlinear nudging intensity and ${H}$ is the observation mesh size). Further, our error estimates suggest that a larger nonlinear exponent $γ$ requires finer observational resolution, which is confirmed by numerical tests. Numerical experiments, including two-dimensional forced viscous flow in a periodic box, flow past a cylinder, and flow over a flat plate, show that nonlinear nudging synchronizes with the true solution considerably faster than linear nudging. We also show that observations in a subregion suffice to synchronize the whole flow
The orbital architecture of 14 Herculis system as a KAM-stable three-body configuration
Francisco Crespo; Jesús F. Palacián; Edward A. Turner; Patricia Yanguas

The 14 Herculis system hosts two massive giant planets on eccentric and mutually inclined orbits, making it a compelling test case for long-term stability in the spatial planetary three-body problem. We develop an analytical description of its dynamics using averaging, symplectic reduction of symmetries and KAM theory. For parameters compatible with the observed architecture, the secular quadrupole Hamiltonian possesses two elliptic relative equilibria that organise the nearby dynamics. The octupole contribution introduces a second slow angle and yields a properly-degenerate multiscale Hamiltonian. Under the corresponding smallness, non-resonance, and non-degeneracy conditions, families of quasi-periodic orbits coming from the relative equilibria of the quadrupolar approximation fill invariant 2-tori. Restoring the two fast mean anomalies and the cyclic angle conjugate to the angular-momentum, and considering the full system, produce two Cantor families of five-dimensional quasi-periodic tori in the reconstructed planetary problem. These invariant structures provide a Hamiltonian mechanism for the long-term confinement of eccentric and mutually inclined configurations compatible with 14 Her.
On the $ϕ^4_2$ theory on $\mathbb R\times S$

We present a construction of the Euclidean two-dimensional $ϕ^4$ quantum field theory model on $\mathbb R\times S$ using parabolic stochastic quantization and discuss the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, we first construct finite-volume measures on a family of tori with varying geometry. To construct an infinite-volume measure on the cylinder, we establish uniform renormalization and stochastic estimates as the complex structure varies, including the degenerating regime in which the torus approaches an infinite cylinder.
Invariant flags and integral matrices with prescribed characteristic polynomial
Caihua Luo; Xu Song; Yilin Zeng

We give an asymptotic formula for integral matrices with a prescribed characteristic polynomial in an expanding entry box over a number field. For cyclic matrices, normalized logarithmic covolumes of a primary invariant flag become uniform on a permutohedral chamber. Their joint distribution with the rescaled matrix factors for tests invariant under reflections at the real places. Separating irreducible factors of multiplicities \(e_i\) into distinct translates multiplies the leading coefficient by \(\prod_i e_i!\). We also bound every noncyclic rational type.
Right shape, wrong time: phase errors of ODE solvers in the flame problem

The flame model $y'=y^2-y^3$, $y(0)=δ$, is a standard illustration of stiffness: for $δ=10^{-4}$ the stiff MATLAB solvers ode23s and ode15s need only 99 and 140 steps, against 3040 for ode45. We show that these cheap solutions have the right shape at the wrong time: they place the front 29 and 329 time units early, with maximal errors 0.95 and 1.00. Because all solutions are time translates of one master profile, the global error of every numerical solution with values in $[δ,1)$ is exactly a phase error, $y_k=y_δ(t_k-D_k)$. For fixed-step one-step methods of order $p$ we prove $D=h^p\int_δ^{y}g+O(h^{p+1})$ with a remainder bounded uniformly in $δ$, so that the delay grows at most like $h\ln(1/δ)$ for $p=1$ and stays bounded for $p\geq2$. For any computed solution the delay is exactly the sum of its defects with respect to the exact flow, converted into time; a heuristic model, confirmed by MATLAB runs, explains why it is created in the first few steps and why tightening the tolerances is an expensive cure. Integrating for $1/y$, which runs like a clock in the slow phase, with an absolute tolerance reduces the error by several orders of magnitude, at a median cost close to that of the standard formulation. The mechanism needs only that the equation is autonomous; its general form is the subject of a companion paper.
A singularity detecting uniformly convergent quantum wavelet framework for weakly singular nonlocal Emden--Fowler systems with quantum Mittag--Leffler sources
Arushi; Pranay Goswami; Pratibhamoy Das; Sudarshan Santra

We develop a quantum wavelet-based computational framework for coupled systems of Caputo-type quantum ($q$-) fractional Emden--Fowler problems with $q$-Mittag--Leffler source terms, where the solutions exhibit singular behavior in time. Here $q\in(0,1)$ denotes the parameter of $q$-calculus. The highest-order Caputo $q$-fractional derivatives are expanded through the Haar wavelet basis, and the lower-order fractional derivatives are approximated through Jackson $q$-fractional integrals of Haar wavelets. The continuous problem reduces to a nonlinear algebraic system on the midpoint collocation points. Under suitable structural assumptions, the Banach fixed-point theorem yields the existence and uniqueness of the continuous solutions and wellposedness of the discrete solutions on collocation points.
